ChIJkVrN-lUodTERUK5DwRPI4bQ.author: max e-ng (Rú)
ChIJkVrN-lUodTERUK5DwRPI4bQ.text:
this is the first time i’ve come back after 7 years, and i can see that the food quality is slowly degrading as time goes by. here are some things to take note before you make a comeback to Popeyes:

1/their fish burger is best in all chicken joints, no doubts.
2/all-you-can-drink softdrink is also great.
3/ their herb dries are still the best fries i can eat amongst other brands.
3/the staff team here is funny, relaxed. they also take their jobs very seriously.
4/they stopped selling their spicy mayo/tartar sauce. i thought they stopped producing it but it turned out that they just don’t sell them separately from the meals anymore, as my fish burger still has the spicy cajun sauce in it. how disappointing. they still sell white mayo sauce for 5k, but you can’t compare them to the superior Lousiana sauces, the highlights of Popeyes.
5/their fish sauce chicken is horrible. i said what i said, maybe they were dipped in sauce for way too long, because the meat taste like rubber. i spent a tremendously long time trying to tear the chicken apart with the utensils.

after nearly 10 years, I’m confident to say that Popeyes has lowered their standards and is now serving days-old chicken dipped in fishsauce.

this is really sad because this brand was part of my childhood. i will not be coming back.

ChIJx_bh79UrdTERcLV9NLXmIsU.text:
I recently visited Popeyes Trung Chánh - Hóc Môn and had an absolutely fantastic experience. From the moment I walked in, I was greeted with warm smiles and excellent customer service. The ambiance of the restaurant was inviting and clean, making it a comfortable place to enjoy a meal.

Now, let's talk about the food! The chicken here is out of this world - crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside, with just the right amount of seasoning to tantalize your taste buds. The sides were also delicious, especially the Cajun fries. Everything was served fresh and piping hot, adding to the overall satisfaction of the meal.

What truly stood out to me was the speed of service. Despite the restaurant being busy, my order was prepared and served promptly, showcasing their efficiency and dedication to customer satisfaction.

Overall, I highly recommend Popeyes Trung Chánh - Hóc Môn to anyone looking for mouthwatering chicken and exceptional service. It's a five-star dining experience that I can't wait to repeat!

ChIJTwjjX6IpdTER3l70-ntiHL0.text: I just had the opportunity to visit Lotteria Van Phuc and was really satisfied with the experience here. In particular, the chicken sauce dishes here are really delicious and diverse. HS chicken sauce is my favorite dish, the mild spicy taste combined with a little sweetness is very tasty, the chicken skin is crispy but the inside is still soft and soaked in sauce. Bean sauce has a completely different flavor, light and not too strong, suitable for those who do not like strong flavors. Finally, the chicken sauce with cheese is rich, the cheese melts just right, not too greasy, making the chicken dish more attractive than ever. The space at Lotteria Van Phuc is quite spacious, clean, suitable for dining with friends or family. The staff is enthusiastic, attentive, always ready to support. The waiting time for food is also very fast, not too long. With the quality of food and service like this, I will definitely come back many times

ChIJJ4DiiUgvdTERnw0LDbg6b-I.author: Jennifer N
ChIJJ4DiiUgvdTERnw0LDbg6b-I.text:
Dirty cramped alley and no free seating available.

There are multiple vendors there selling everything from bot chien (fried dough with scrambled eggs), sup cua (crab soup), spring rolls, banh canh cua (crab noodles), banh khot (think bite sized banh xeo), snails, and corn.

I got banh khot, spring rolls and banh canh cua. The first two dishes were below average. The banh canh (30k vnd) was good though.

There is no seating available other than some stools at the back of the alley near the motorbike parking and near the snail vendor. It looked like communal seating, but the snail vendor has employees that will force you to buy beverages from them in order to sit down. It seems a bit ridiculous to monopolize the seating like that and to charge as much as other  vendors do for food.

Traffic in the alley is cramped between food traffic from customers, motorbike drivers, and garbagemen dragging rubbish dumpsters dripping with filthy water inches away from your  table and stool. If you're not a cat person I'd stay away as well because stray kittens will go underneath all the tables looking for scraps.

ChIJg1Jo_NspdTER2s4BCjM52vQ.text:
Fish balls are varied, with clear origins and reasonable prices. They are served with only cucumber and shredded mango.

The homemade dipping sauce is delicious, but I did think the portion was a bit small. It would be great if there were sauce bottles on the tables so we could help ourselves.

Crispy fried chicken skin is definitely a must-try here, it is (probably) their signature dish for a reason! As the name suggests, the skin is perfectly coated and fried until it is wonderfully crispy.

The drinks are also fantastic. I particularly enjoyed the peach milk tea.

However, when the place is busy, things can get a bit chaotic. Some of my fish balls were overcooked. The fried wontons had very little filling, almost none at all.

ChIJP_Wan7gpdTER9bO5ARNnD1Y.author: Genevieve Vox
ChIJP_Wan7gpdTER9bO5ARNnD1Y.text:
It appears that Son Ca is a rather popular snack shop among young people. The primary dish served here is phá lấu, but there are numerous other options, making it a hit with students.

However, the phá lấu itself is somewhat underwhelming. The broth is thin and contains excessive food colouring, the dipping sauce is overly sour, and the accompanying bread is cold.

Other dishes, such as fried chicken wings with fish sauce, Son Ca dumplings, or fish balls are of average quality. The drinks on offer are quite disappointing; the lemon tea seems to be simply a Lipton tea bag with a slice of lime, and the coconut and kumquat drinks lack any discernible coconut flavour and taste more like sugary water.

Moreover, the service at Son Ca is rather chaotic. Despite customers placing their orders by ticking items on a paper, the servers frequently deliver incorrect dishes or to the wrong tables. The premises are also not kept in a pristine condition, with evidence of baby cockroaches.

ChIJ-8YYdqAndTERAGWQ6oAZF2c.author: Dương Đăng Phúc
ChIJ-8YYdqAndTERAGWQ6oAZF2c.text:
* The parking space on the sidewalk is a bit small, 2-3 cars are full, there is no parking attendant so everyone lock their cars and keep their belongings safe!

* The shop space is bright, the shelves are easy to see, there are chairs to wait.

* There are quite a lot of snacks such as ice cream, milk tea, rice paper, dried foods, etc. to choose from. The packaging and labels are clean and look very good.

* I bought about 4-5 dishes and found them quite ok, actually the taste is not much different from the ones I bought outside but it is beautiful and clean.

* The staff are friendly, polite and quick.

* At the entrance there are some sample dishes, you can try them before buying! In addition, there are free chopsticks, spoons and paper there.

* This place has points when buying, 5% discount for orders of 1.5 million, there are some dishes I saw also buy 5 get 1 free, I think it was ice cream. There is also a return policy!

* Payment by bank transfer, momo, cash are all accepted. The payment screen is displayed at the counter for customers to see
———
Enjoy your meal!

You choose what you want/as much as you want, and then they cook/fry/stir-fry it for you. For the kind of food it is, it's good. It doesn't taste like dinner or lunch food, rather snack food. That being said, it's quite popular.

The tables and chairs are small, so it feels a little tight. Seems like a comfortable place for Vietnamese.

I ate two trays of food, but each one was much smaller than any other tray of food I saw from other people/tables. Few tables were had single customers, mostly 2+ per table.

ChIJWyEXVgEndTERvxZFb0W6VpY.text:
This is a skewer buffet restaurant located in the alley of Thu Duc High School. I recently had an experience here and have the following review:
- About the restaurant space: the restaurant is a bit small but quite airy, clean, and has air conditioning. Inside the restaurant, there are tables, chairs, and skewers for customers to choose from. After choosing, take the plate of food you just picked out for the staff to fry. Outside the restaurant is a fryer, so the space inside the restaurant does not smell of grease.
- About service attitude: the staff is enthusiastic, has a good attitude, and keeps and drives vehicles for customers.
- About food quality: the food is delicious and clean. When it is time to open the restaurant, the skewers are just taken out of the freezer, so if you come early, the food is still frozen, and some types are difficult to put on the plate because they stick together. The restaurant serves fried food on request, including regular fried food, fried fish sauce and garlic fried food, and cheese shaken food. Fried garlic fish sauce is the hottest dish here because it has a strong flavor, is not boring and comes with stir-fried vegetables. I was eating halfway through and just remembered to take a photo so the buffet in the picture is not very nice :v
- Regarding the variety of dishes: In my opinion, the variety of skewers is just enough because I don't see fried okra and some other types.
- Regarding the price: 1 buffet ticket here is 69k, teas like peach tea... are about 20k so it is considered cheap and suitable for students.
In conclusion, I rate 5 stars ^^ and in my opinion, when experiencing eating at this restaurant, each person needs to spend about less than 100k. The review is here :3

ChIJlZlykK4vdTEROVqMqsKOLHw.text:
As a big fan of live fire grilling, I can confidently say this place is all about the fire. You can tell the place is a hit instantly just base on the smell, we just couldn't resist. I am confident to say the place is on par with some Michelin's recommended list in Saigon. The price is affordable, friendly and the owner is the head chef + server + line cook there too 😂. Love to support local business with the owner who cares about the customers.

**Cons** There are a couple of drawbacks. The restaurant is tucked away in a small alley, so the best way to get there is by motorcycle. Additionally, since each dish is handmade to order, be prepared for a bit of a wait. Despite these minor inconveniences, we would definitely recommend to check this place out.

ChIJlZlykK4vdTEROVqMqsKOLHw.text: The other day, my friend introduced me to this restaurant. One of us came from Phu Nhuan and the other from Thu Duc to try it out. The result was very good. In the picture I took, there were grilled chao intestines, grilled skewers, and tofu, and it didn't stop. The tofu here was soft and melt-in-your-mouth. My friend also said that the tofu was fragrant and fragrant, and then it was called the real Lang Mo tofu. My table drank beer. Later, we ordered duck tongue and grilled chives. Before we could take a picture, they were all gone because they were both delicious and interesting. This duck tongue is marinated with various spices, and finished with Chinese cooking wine, so it has a light, refreshing aroma of cinnamon and anise, and it's not as spicy as the shops on the street. The grilled chives are marinated with salt and spices, which is also very unique and easy to eat. You should try the above dishes. Tomorrow I will probably go back down to "scrape" other dishes on the menu 😋

About 18 years ago, a friend took me to a very delicious grilled offal restaurant on this street, but I don't know if it's this restaurant or not...
The restaurant is located in a fairly clean alley, on the sidewalk but the seats are also clean, quite chill.
The offal is soft, not smelly, marinated a bit sweet, grilled wet, not very dry. It feels a bit like watery offal then brought to the stove to grill, like that, served with pickled cabbage, Price 100k/plate. I only eat offal, haven't eaten other types of grilled skewers so I can't rate the others. Overall the offal is ok
The only downside is probably the seller's facial expression. The older lady is quite friendly but the older brother's face is a bit grumpy, when I ate another dish on the second day, I asked to grill it a bit more because I like it drier but he didn't seem happy, kkk
Overall the offal is ok so I still recommend everyone to try it.

ChIJ46YpEAAvdTERCN2tb73oDLU.author: Pinkamew
ChIJ46YpEAAvdTERCN2tb73oDLU.text:
Can’t stop eating!!!!

This is a true hidden gem that only locals know — serving insanely delicious Northern-style grilled pork skewers.

Authentic Hanoi flavors, grilled right in front of you. You’ll sit on those tiny, cute street chairs, soaking in the real local vibe.

They only sell one thing: Northern-style grilled pork skewers —SUPER tasty! The pork is served hot and juicy, perfect on its own or dipped in their Northern-style chili sauce. Don’t miss the free pickled papaya and carrot — highly recommended because it pairs so well with the pork.

The perfect rhythm goes like this:
👉 dip the pork in chili sauce → take a bite → eat one pickle → repeat (pure happiness).

One tip: estimate how many skewers you can eat and order them all at once. If you order just 1–2 more later, you’ll have to wait a bit — and waiting makes it slightly less yum 😅

I can easily eat 5 skewers in one go, while my male friends can finish 10 skewers lol.

Worth to spend sometime to find this place and enjoy it!

I’m not 100% sure about their hours, but I usually eat here in the afternoon, around 2–5 PM.
Price : 12,000 VND per skewer only!

ChIJFcK4z4IpdTERyQHZZ_Chz94.text:
I like this ice cream place. They are known for this dessert: avocado smoothies with coconut ice cream.  I don't think they have the best quality ice cream. But I like their combination of Vietnamese traditional Vietnamese avocado smoothies with coconut ice cream which is an excellent choice since our country has a lot of coconut. I especially love their Vietnamese traditional ice cream topping - ground roasted peanut and shredded coconut - that brings me right back to my childhood. I also like that their avocado coconut ice cream is not too sweet.
Other things I have tried was fresh durian on my ice cream. I would not recommended, their durian was not quality, hard and not soft. I ended up threw it out of my ice cream. I also tried their fried combo snack. It was ok, but not that good, especially the fish balls, wasn't that quality.  I think their customers are mainly young kids. So their price needs to be reasonable for that group.
Their location is chill at night. You get to experience a nice street food culture. Recommend.

ChIJ9Wtu0iwvdTERIoCwOF9TxvY.author: Duc Bui
ChIJ9Wtu0iwvdTERIoCwOF9TxvY.text:
The second floor, in particular, caught my attention. Adorned with vintage decorations, it exudes a warm and nostalgic charm. The unique furniture, especially the cozy couches, encapsulates the essence of home, making one feel instantly at ease.
When it comes to their ice cream offerings, simplicity is the key. While they have a range of flavors, my personal recommendation would be to stick to their original coconut. For the more adventurous, the "Bo Gia" signature flavor is an absolute must-try. Taste-wise, it's on par with the renowned "Kem Bach Dang", but what makes it stand out is the slightly more affordable price tag.
For those who prefer a hearty meal, the restaurant offers both Western and Vietnamese dishes. While their Western plates, especially the beef, are commendable, it's their authentic Vietnamese dishes that steal the show. The "Bo Kho", a traditional Vietnamese beef stew, is particularly noteworthy.

ChIJ9Wtu0iwvdTERIoCwOF9TxvY.text: The presentation of the food was quite nice, but the taste was average and not memorable. ChIJ9Wtu0iwvdTERIoCwOF9TxvY.text: Favorable price , about 75k per big glass. There has many type of ice cream. The taste in my opinion there has no special but I like it.

ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU.text: This spot has some of the best gelatos that I’ve ever tested! Unlike a lot of other places, all of the gelatos are made with real ingredients and, you can tell! ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU.name: places/ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VKV1Mwc09QaE5iNmZ3EAE
ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU.author: Charles Barnes
ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU.text:
Best gelato in HCMC, for sure. Nowhere else is even close.
Super creamy, delicious, premium ingredients, affordable and a really nice spot off an alley. Run by a couple of Canadians who've moved back to VN- they really know what they're doing. Can't recommend highly enough!

ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU.name: places/ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNfc2FfR3FRRRAB
ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU.author: Just Me
ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU.text: Very impressive. About as good a gelato I've had outside of Italy which is high praise. We tried strawberry, pistachio, Oreo and salted caramel flavours and every single one was rich and tasty, smooth, and with a strong taste of the flavour it represented. The pistachio and strawberry in particular were excellent. Flavour and texture wise this place does an excellent job, I was actually shocked at how good it was but less so when I watched the videos on their TV of how they prepare the ice cream, they clearly know what they are doing. It's quiet and in an area you may not normally go, but it's worth the detour. Nice venue too with seating inside and outside and well decorated. Just to reiterate, all flavours were great but don't miss the strawberry and pistachio ones.

ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU.name: places/ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNUX042Vmh3RRAB
ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU.author: Chau Nguyen
ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU.text: This is a lovely spot for enjoying some delicious gelato and sorbet in a peaceful and cozy setting. The staff here are incredibly kind and welcoming. They take the time to introduce you to their products and make sure you feel right at home. The sorbet and gelato here are incredibly smooth and silky with a wide variety of flavors to choose from. The tropical fruit flavors, in particular, are especially fresh and never icy or milky. It's no wonder why this place is considered one of the best in town.

ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU.name: places/ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURWbDd1Tjd3RRAB
ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU.author: K Tran
ChIJmd8m88gvdTERZkQ0R7SRGEU.text:
I am a German tourist and this was my first time eating authentic Italian cream in Vietnam could taste sooo good, even better than Italian ice cream in Germany!
The ice cream was so rich and so creamy
And the flavours we're exceptionally amazing.
Compared to the ice cream I've tried in Germany the flavour was so intensive and you could taste that the ice cream from Amore was made from fresh ingredients. I tried Oreo, durian and my all time favorite pistachio. All three were on Point, not to sweet, pistachio tastes actually like real pistachio and durian was a new experience for me.
I will definitely come to visit again to try the other  tropical fruit ice cream like soursop or Passion fruit, flavour I haven't seen at any other ice cream stores before.

Besides that, the people who work there were very nice, the inferior was nice and cozy and free WiFi was available.
Was worth my time coming to this place👍

ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.name: places/ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT201bU5GY3hlRVZMUW1kRlFWVm1hVTUyY1dSUmFtYxAB
ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.author: LP Pua
ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.text: While walking back to our hotel, we stumbled upon a very busy dessert shop at the corner of an even busier traffic junction on a Sunday night. Seeing many people enjoying ice cream served in coconuts, we decided to take a break and ordered coconut ice cream along with a lychee drink. The ice cream itself was fairly standard, but the novelty of serving it in a coconut—and being able to scrape out the fresh coconut flesh—added to the experience. Prices were on the steeper side, though.

ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.name: places/ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2s5M05reGZlVUZVZUhaU1RsTnVVelpYVGpoaGRtYxAB
ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.author: LPQ
ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.text: A nice ice cream bistro with a long history. The service is excellent, and the ice cream is extremely delicious, made with a mix of coconut cream, milk cream, and fresh fruits. The taste of these ice creams is unique and cannot be found anywhere else. Definitely worth trying at least once when visiting to Ho Chi Minh City.

ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.name: places/ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2pKQ2VtOUNiblF4TkhCTWFIQnhhM0l5VFZjelRWRRAB
ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.author: Abutalal Kitchen
ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.text: I visited Kem Bach Dang Ice Ceam in Ho Chi Minh - Vietnam on July 14, 2025 they are Very welcoming and accommodating staff ordered Coconut Ice Ceam 2 scoops one coconut flavor the other durian flavor, and Bach Dang Ice Cream  2 scoops one coconut flavor the other durian flavor. The Ice Cream are delicious and tasty and fresh and portion sizes also great. The service is wonderful. I thank all the Ice Cream store workers for good treatment and service and their interest in providing the best they have. I recommend trying and visiting.

ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.name: places/ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VMeW1vYzZMbFB2OU9BEAE
ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.author: Jennifer teh
ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.text: Bach Dang Ice Cream is a treat for both nostalgic and adventurous palates! They offer a delightful mix of old and new ice cream flavors, catering to a wide range of tastes. The classic flavors bring back fond memories, while the new and innovative ones are a thrilling discovery. Whether you're in the mood for something familiar or want to try something new, Bach Dang Ice Cream has got you covered. Their commitment to quality and variety is evident in every scoop, making it a must-visit destination for ice cream lovers of all ages.👍👍👍🥰

ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.name: places/ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT205S1VFZEZRMGwxWm5aMVRqQmFVR3RYVUVKS2FXYxAB
ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.author: yumz
ChIJ9y8U5yQvdTERYsbV4KIk-s0.text:
bach dang ice cream is a classic spot with complicated vibes

THE LEGENDARY STATUS
this place is a true saigon landmark that's been serving up scoops for generations. it's one of those iconic spots that everyone knows, with a history that's basically woven into the city's story.

THE REALITY CHECK
keeping it 100, the ice cream itself is mid at best - especially after all the hype. the flavors are basic and the texture doesn't quite hit right.

THE PRICE SITUATION
this is way too expensive for what you get. the price-to-joy ratio is seriously off when you can find better quality for less at other spots around town.

THE PEOPLE WATCHING PERKS
where this place actually shines is the prime people-watching situation. grabbing a seat here lets you take in the full saigon street theater. it's better entertainment than the dessert.

THE FINAL VERDICT
come for the history and the vibes, but maybe don't get your hopes up about the ice cream being life-changing. it's more about the experience than the actual scoop.

don't forget to ❤️.

ChIJtTUX_DovdTERhcCrBI9uIIk.name: places/ChIJtTUX_DovdTERhcCrBI9uIIk/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25OT1dFRjBaMlF6VkRJeFpIcFdhalJ4VG1GTFpGRRAB
ChIJtTUX_DovdTERhcCrBI9uIIk.author: John Winter
ChIJtTUX_DovdTERhcCrBI9uIIk.text:
Afrocado - Premium Handcrafted Gelato & Dessert in Ho Chi Minh City is a vibrant little pit stop that’s all about fun, flavor, and flair. From the moment you step inside, the quirky interior design, playful wall art, and even a giant plush bear on the couch make the place feel inviting and a little whimsical.

We came during their generous happy hour (10:30am – 3:30pm), where each scoop is 50% off. The gelato was impressively smooth, creamy, and packed with flavor. We tried a few combinations, dark chocolate, mango, and strawberry and every scoop was beautifully presented with details like marshmallow, chocolate curls, strawberry slices, and delicate crisp wafers.

The atmosphere was relaxed, and the staff were friendly and upbeat, offering great suggestions and quick service. It’s clearly a popular spot, with a steady flow of locals and visitors enjoying their treats or lounging with headphones and a coffee.

They also offer unique items like mochi waffles, lavender milk tea, and avocado-themed desserts, in keeping with their quirky “Afrocado” branding. The whole experience felt cheerful and creative, definitely worth a visit if you’re looking for a cool, tasty break in the middle of District 1.

ChIJtTUX_DovdTERhcCrBI9uIIk.name: places/ChIJtTUX_DovdTERhcCrBI9uIIk/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2taa1ZscFdlSHBHY1VGa1ZteDZjRFJZZUU0eGJtYxAB

ChIJtTUX_DovdTERhcCrBI9uIIk.text: Afrocado is a must-visit for ice cream lovers! I tried the salted caramel and tiramisu flavors — both were rich, creamy, and absolutely delicious. The real highlight was pairing them with their freshly made waffles, which were warm, soft inside, and slightly crispy on the outside. The combo was perfect! Highly recommend for a sweet treat that hits the spot.

Definitely worth a visit if you’re looking for a quiet midday break!

ChIJ8_v9mRUvdTERXMWx0qsbLX8.text: If you’re an ice cream lover like me, Swensen's in Saigon is a total gem. The second you walk in, you’re hit with a rainbow of flavors that all look amazing. The ice cream is super smooth and creamy, with all the classic favorites like chocolate and vanilla, plus some more unique options if you’re feeling adventurous. The portions are seriously generous, and the prices are totally worth it. It’s got a cozy, chill vibe that makes it the perfect spot to kick back, whether you’re wandering around the city or just craving something sweet on a hot day. If you love ice cream, this place is a must!

ChIJ8_v9mRUvdTERXMWx0qsbLX8.text:
Thought this would be a nice spot to get some nice dessert a few times but will only be having it once due to the abysmal customer service. It looks like they’re a bunch of students but still, that’s not an excuse for the poor service. Only reason why I’m giving this a 1 star is because the customer service is that bad.

They sat me down as I was going to eat there and there were no other customers here other than a table that had already ordered. Not once did anyone come to take my order after they sat me down. I waited 20 minutes to see if they would ever come but they did not ask me at all.

Had to ask them to take my order. Looks like they are quite over staffed for such a small location yet none of them thought to ask the only waiting customer if they are ready to order. Lots of staff standing and staring at each other making the dessert. I could walk out without paying my bill and they probably wouldn’t bat an eye, that’s how invisible I feel here.

The ice cream is fine I have no issues with it and it also did not take long for them to make it. I’d recommend it here as a decent place with nice air conditioning inside if it weren’t for the customer service.

ChIJ_0c3tD8vdTERV7qbhNMrwBU.author: SuSu Babe
ChIJ_0c3tD8vdTERV7qbhNMrwBU.text:
The shop is tiny, fitting only about six people comfortably. We weren’t satisfied with the staff’s attitude during our visit, which affected the overall experience. When we asked what was included in the spaghetti ice (which listed “fresh strawberries”), she didn’t answer our question and instead told us to go to the shop across the street if we wanted “fresh fruit”. This response felt very rude and unprofessional, especially for a place that markets itself as offering handcrafted, high quality gelato.
The gelato itself was generally fine, but the caramel flavor was a letdown, it had a strong powdered milk taste, and I ended up throwing away the whole cup.
Overall, cramped space, inconsistent flavors, and poor service made the visit far below expectations.

ChIJ_0c3tD8vdTERV7qbhNMrwBU.name: places/ChIJ_0c3tD8vdTERV7qbhNMrwBU/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNQOHJQTG93RRAB
ChIJ_0c3tD8vdTERV7qbhNMrwBU.author: Genevieve Vox
ChIJ_0c3tD8vdTERV7qbhNMrwBU.text:
Ralf's new spot at Eco Wellness is a bit cosy, but it got a lovely balcony overlooking the street. There is seating for about six people out there, with four spots right by the railing. Inside, you will find two more seats with a pool view and another two in the courtyard downstairs.

The menu changes monthly, so there is always something new to try. In addition to traditional flavours, there will be about 2-3 creative gelato flavours with special ingredients, such as fish sauce gelato or beef pho sorbet – the kind of quirky treats that made Ralf's Gelato stand out among Saigon's gelaterias a few years ago.

The price of VND 70.000 may sound expensive at first, but if you consider the weight and quality you get, Ralf's is definitely the place that sells the best and cheapest gelato in the area! For VND 70.000, you can get 2 scoops of 2 different gelato flavours, 1 large scoop and 1 (not at all) small scoop.

I reckon the best combos are ones with similar base notes (strawberry and lime / chocolate and coffee / smurf and coconut). Those who prefer a bold flavour combo can try the combination of raspberry sorbet and Belgian chocolate like me. But to be honest, I am not a huge fan of that pairing myself.

ChIJ6aWmjrwudTER5BnT9kZJWIg.text:

Going so far away just to buy ice cream is so sad.

Ice cream is also ok, lots of it, cheap. But probably mainly use colors and flavorings. Eating quickly gets boring. Eating occasionally is ok

ChIJ6aWmjrwudTER5BnT9kZJWIg.text: The ice cream shop is super cheap but very delicious (especially for those who like ice cream with moderate sweetness). The owner is very cheerful and enthusiastic. ChIJV1Jy-e8udTERVE8MdSAd858.name: places/ChIJV1Jy-e8udTERVE8MdSAd858/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNydVltamx3RRAB
ChIJV1Jy-e8udTERVE8MdSAd858.author: Genevieve Vox
ChIJV1Jy-e8udTERVE8MdSAd858.text:
This place is known for its unique dessert: three ice cream flavours nestled inside a coconut flesh carved into a lemon wedge shape.

Unfortunately, the ice cream itself was a disappointment. Instead of the smooth, creamy texture you would expect, it was icy and more akin to flavoured snow than decadent ice cream. The saving grace was the chocolate ice cream, not bad at all.

The mixed deep-fried fish balls, on the other hand, were a satisfying savoury option. They come with two dipping sauces: a delicious hoisin sauce and a "meh" chilli sauce with a strange sour flavour.

However, a major concern was the hygiene. The food prep area appeared quite messy, and disturbingly, my coconut ice cream had inexplicably had a faint cockroach smell.

ChIJ23rD_hkmdTERC74wRz6yMK0.text: This ice cream shop in Thao Dien offers a truly unique experience with its one-of-a-kind flavors. Overall, it’s a must-visit for anyone looking for a fresh and flavorful ice cream experience in District 2!

ChIJf-01KSUvdTER0q9mh5Lynzk.text:
One day, I had a sudden craving for ice cream, so I searched on Google Maps and luckily found Kem To Mi, an ice cream store conveniently located near the main road of Cach Mang Tháng in Ho Chi Minh City.

Kem To Mi specializes in ice cream and also offers some desserts. The taste of their ice cream is exceptional. I tried three flavors: cookie, Snickers, and caramel. Each one was perfect, boasting rich and delightful flavors.
The quality of the ice cream was impressive, and I am definitely looking forward to trying more flavors on my next visit.

Although the prices are a bit on the higher side, ranging from VND 60,000 to 80,000 per scoop, the quality of the ice cream justifies the cost. The premium taste and creamy texture make it well worth the price.

I would even say that the ice cream at Kem To Mi can be compared to that of Häagen-Dazs. For anyone in Ho Chi Minh City looking to satisfy their ice cream cravings, Kem To Mi is a must-visit.

ChIJaUNbkggpdTERIDHnVC5YJyY.text: I found this sweet dessert shop on TikTok and was pleasantly surprised — the chè here is delicious, easy to enjoy, and not overly sweet like many other places. They have a nice variety of toppings such as jelly, jackfruit, and grass jelly, all fresh and nicely presented. I tried two types: Dừa Dầm and Thái Lọt, both served with ice on the side so you can adjust the chill to your liking. The syrup is light and refreshing, and the toppings have a pleasant crunch. The shop is casual and outdoors, breezy and comfortable — perfect for a relaxed evening with friends. Service is quick and friendly, and the prices are very reasonable for the quality. I’d definitely come back if I’m in the area again!

ChIJAe_q8CovdTER4Uet9JgueOQ.text: 1 star because the phone staff ordering the cake had extremely poor EQ. You should know that people order cakes on special occasions, the wishes on the cake are extremely important. Whether the baker makes a mistake or the delivery staff distorts the wishes, it's your staff. Customers who complain should apologize first! No one wants to receive a birthday cake where 'Forever beautiful' becomes 'Forever black', do you understand what it means when the word 'black' appears on a birthday cake? I ordered a cake to give to my aunt, my aunt took a picture of the cake and asked me to read the wishes for her. I was really embarrassed. I work in the service industry so I should be more tactful in those situations!

ChIJzYKptIIvdTERjX_loSl579U.author: Ngoc Tran
ChIJzYKptIIvdTERjX_loSl579U.text:
Before placing your order, I recommend checking with the staff to confirm whether the bingsoo you want is available. My friend and I each ordered a bingsoo separately, and while both orders were accepted without any mention of an issue, I was only informed that mine was unavailable after my friend’s was already served. I specifically came here for the Thai tea bingsoo, so had I known it wasn’t available, I would’ve gone elsewhere. It’s disappointing to just sit here watching my friend eat.

I understand the staff member who took my order might not have known right away and only found out after the kitchen informed them. But this kind of communication should happen immediately after the order is placed—not after everyone else’s food has already been brought out. It would be much more considerate if the staff could actively check item availability and inform customers upfront to avoid situations like this.

ChIJ5RrTfrAndTERDjn5cVqAmBU.text:
Let me ask you a question, Mixue can't buy ice cream for 10k in a cup?

I want to buy ice cream cone in a cup, not 25k in a cup. The staff member had a bad attitude and told me "don't sell that way". Okay, I understand, it's okay.

But later, a guy came to buy ice cream to take home. He wanted to buy ice cream cone in a cup. Same as above, not selling. The problem is that guy bought a 25k ice cream cup, and held a 10k ice cream cone to take home :) Saigon weather at 2pm is so hot :)

First time eating at this Mixue establishment. I asked to buy ice cream cone in a cup because at the establishments I've eaten at, they serve like that. Note, I asked, I didn't talk like I was ordering you.

I spoke very gently and respectfully, why did you order and talk with an attitude like I'm asking - you give me?

ChIJJSnLzvspdTERMCT3M_QBVVE.text:
I had the opportunity to visit this bakery and was really impressed with the quality of the cakes and service here. Each type of cake has a unique flavor, is carefully prepared and takes care of every detail.

**About the quality of the cakes**:
The cakes here are very diverse, from sweet cakes, savory cakes, to cream cakes. Each cake is soft, delicious and has a moderate sweetness

**Shop space**:
The bakery is decorated cozy and clean, bringing a comfortable and pleasant feeling

**Service**:
The staff is very enthusiastic and friendly, always ready to advise customers about the types of cakes and help choose the right product. Moreover, the service time is very fast, no need to wait long.

**Price**:
The price is reasonable compared to the quality of the cake. You can completely feel satisfied with the money you spend when enjoying the delicious cakes here.

All in all, this is a bakery I will definitely be returning to. Well worth a stop and a taste!

ChIJaftTLwApdTER_qo-jn9PDfI.text:
cơm thố giòn is bringing the clay pot rice realness

THE CLAY POT SITUATION
cơm niêu is vietnam's iconic clay pot rice that absolutely serves. we're talking crispy bottom rice with that perfect texture that hits different from regular rice.

THE FLAVOR FLEX
everything here is straight fire and lowkey delicious. each dish is an absolute serve with flavors that are good for the soul. don’t forget to add the chilis and ask for them chopped to get the seeds.

THE SERVICE VIBES
the customer service stays on point and the whole spot is lowkey impressively clean. the team's energy and tidy setup make the experience even better.

THE RELIABLE MOVE
when you are craving that perfect clay pot rice situation, this place is a total yes. the quality and care in each bowl is next level.

THE FINAL VERDICT
if you want proper cơm niêu that actually delivers on flavor and cleanliness, this spot is a must. your taste buds will thank you later

don't forget to ❤️.

ChIJc4e_IUEvdTERfdMLD248bSc.author: Sajid Sadikeen
ChIJc4e_IUEvdTERfdMLD248bSc.text: Tucked away in a narrow alley of District 1, Tiệm Cơm Thố Chuyên Ký is a true Saigon institution that’s earned its Michelin Bib Gourmand status with timeless Cantonese claypot comfort food. The setting is no frills, with scooters parked out front and stainless steel tables inside but that’s exactly the charm. We tried a delicious spread of sizzling shrimp with onions, fluffy egg with daikon and tender braised chicken, each paired with fragrant rice served in traditional claypots. The flavors were bold, homey and deeply satisfying. It’s the kind of place where tradition is the main ingredient and for the price, the quality is unbeatable. A must visit for anyone chasing real local flavor.

ChIJc4e_IUEvdTERfdMLD248bSc.name: places/ChIJc4e_IUEvdTERfdMLD248bSc/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTURvalpDcmFREAE
ChIJc4e_IUEvdTERfdMLD248bSc.author: The MY World
ChIJc4e_IUEvdTERfdMLD248bSc.text: It's very old Chinese restaurant. After I visited, I found that this shop was selected as michelin bib gourmand. Nh...I had chicken soup, because some people were saying it's their signature one. The chicken inside was very tender and soup was not bad. Also had clay pot rice with chicken and also beef and Chinese sausage. Those were very small, but tastes good. Then I got one vegetable plate, and also kinda small. Nh... the value for the price was not good for me. It was good but I didn't get the point why this shop was selected by Michelin. Anyway I thought it was expensive as local food, but if it was selected by Michelin, then may be OK to visit. Of course, as food, it's not expensive, but as local restaurant in Vietnam, it is a bit. Probably good to try here if you have the same tang with the one from Michelin Lol.

ChIJc4e_IUEvdTERfdMLD248bSc.text:
[Review of a Chinese Restaurant]

I visited this restaurant about four years ago and was quite impressed with the delicious and authentic food. However, my recent visit was disappointing. The quality of the dishes has noticeably declined, and the flavors are no longer as rich as they used to be. The prices remain quite high compared to similar places, but the current quality doesn’t justify the cost. Additionally, the restaurant charges a parking fee of 10,000 VND per vehicle, so be aware of that before you visit. If you’re looking for a quality Chinese dining experience, you might want to consider other options.

ChIJc4e_IUEvdTERfdMLD248bSc.text:
We had a great experience here! The service was absolutely incredible! The owners and staff brought our daughter as much fruit as she could eat, plus some to take home! We ordered the Cantanese chicken which had a mushroom sauce that was excellent! Chicken and broccoli, which had more cauliflower than broccoli but the flavor was so good! The chicken in this dish did have more bones, but some Vietnamese do like bones and do not waste any parts of yhe chicken! It's just not our preference. The fried rice was excellent 😋 The price for it all cost us about $10 USD
We review michelin recommended resturaunts as well as others with our honest opinions on pur youtube channel "The Trippin' Family" as well as get into more depth on the cost, flavors and what go order!

ChIJxb33aPsvdTERyNOElsAOINI.author: Mark Chan
ChIJxb33aPsvdTERyNOElsAOINI.text:
Cantonese soup lover location in the heart of the city. Serve a variety of soup like chicken feet, pig brain, pork rip etc. Doesn't have a lot of fancy other option for other side dish. I have ordered a triple type stream egg and also steam ginger chicken. Food taste is reasonably nice without MSG. The rice bowl is very cute and it is in 2 "small" bowl. I would say have a healthy meal instead of those oily friend of BBQ food.

Price wise is below 100k Dong per pax... It is inside a small street along Ton That Dam road where it is a old traditional market. Once you see the Mi Guang sign, walk into the small alley till the end turn right and you will find it at the end of a residential house. Do make booking early as it open at 11am and usually sold out before 10:30am. It is correct, they should out before they are open. They can speak Cantonese so it is easier for me as a non local natives.

Really don't sell much stuff so it is more like a home meal restaurant. Doesn't serve other drinks except for standard ice tea "Tra Da" that all.

I tried this place for the first time with fellow teachers. It's an alright local hot bowl place. The rice comes cooked in a clay pot/bowl, I tried the xá xíu (char siu - pork), 45K/$1.85. There wasn't a ton of meat, but it tasted alright. The rice was a little plain, so everyone seemed to add soy sauce and/or hot sauce.

[Update 28/1] We went back, I tried the beef bowl (cơm thó bò). The same price, but added a chicken leg on the side for 25K ($1.00). I probably liked the beef more than the pork, but the rice was still on the drier side. The chicken was a bit overcooked or had been cooked earlier and then reheated - it was ok.

[Update 3/2] Tried the plain fried rice with an egg for 25K ($1.00), it was standard.. a little dry and plain. The other folks had pork, beef, chicken bowls, and the meat looked better. I had a chicken leg on the side (again, 25K). Compared to the previous time, this piece was much better - better meat, less dry, and more meat.

ChIJM6Z2fzAvdTERTTyJk3v3TMI.author: Ryan Adams
ChIJM6Z2fzAvdTERTTyJk3v3TMI.text:
Great little local place with several locations serving a wide variety of Vietnamese dishes, including many not commonly spotted. Everything we tried was solid.

The fried flying fish was pretty interesting - like a large, mild sardine - and it was seasoned with some quite unique spices that we couldn’t quite identify. Very good. The purple yam soup is mild in flavor, but brightens up with a bit of fish sauce and chili. The squid was super tender. The two styles of char siu were tender and balanced in flavor - not overly sweet like some places.

Service was friendly and quick throughout even though it was pretty busy. The a/c room could be a bit cooler - was still quite warm.

ChIJM6Z2fzAvdTERTTyJk3v3TMI.name: places/ChIJM6Z2fzAvdTERTTyJk3v3TMI/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xkRmJqQnVVVEJLWWxsSVREaHdVVzlpZUZZMFdYYxAB
ChIJM6Z2fzAvdTERTTyJk3v3TMI.author: Kenny Nguyen
ChIJM6Z2fzAvdTERTTyJk3v3TMI.text: Really delicious and homely meal! The soup was nicely sour but not sweet — just the way it’s typically cooked  mien trung. The stir fried veggie was flavorful, and the fried egg was great too. The braised pork belly had a lovely taste, though the portion could use a bit less fat. Overall, a sweet and cozy place with fair prices and tasty food. Definitely worth a visit!

The menu is diverse, both vegetarian and non-vegetarian. 
The most impressive thing for me is lotus leaf rice and mussel rice here. In addition, the pot rice dishes are also quite delicious, with unique and reasonable food combinations. 
Besides, there are many other delicious dishes. 
Previously, it was Mon Hue - Com Tho Chay combined together. Now I heard that MH is closed, it is quite a pity because the food is delicious :(

ChIJdadbKS4vdTER8s5ebJKIOZU.text:
We made a reservation for a family dinner event with a large group, and Cơm Niêu Sài Gòn went above and beyond to accommodate us. They kindly reserved an indoor room to keep things quiet since they had live music performing outside that evening.

We were very impressed by their extensive menu — I remember seeing over 300 dishes listed! The staff was incredibly patient and helpful, guiding us through the options and making recommendations that worked perfectly for our group.

My family and friends thoroughly enjoyed all the dishes we ordered, and the highlight of the evening was definitely watching the signature clay pot rice presentation — the way they broke the pot and tossed the rice across the room was so impressive!

Overall, a wonderful dining experience with delicious food, attentive service, and a fun cultural performance. Highly recommend for gatherings or anyone looking to experience authentic Vietnamese cuisine with a show!

Vietnamese Clay Pot Rice Restaurant – 234 Cong Hoa Street

If you are looking for an authentic taste of traditional Vietnamese cuisine, Vietnamese Clay Pot Rice Restaurant at 234 Cong Hoa Street is a destination you should not miss. Known locally as Cơm Niêu Việt Nam, this restaurant brings back the nostalgic flavors of family meals while offering a warm and welcoming atmosphere for both locals and visitors.

The highlight of the restaurant is its signature clay pot rice, a dish deeply rooted in Vietnamese culinary heritage. The rice is cooked in small clay pots over a slow fire, creating a unique texture—soft, fluffy grains with a deliciously crispy golden crust at the bottom. This simple yet delightful dish pairs perfectly with a variety of side dishes such as caramelized fish, braised pork, stir-fried vegetables, and fragrant soups. Every meal here feels like a journey back to the countryside kitchens of Vietnam.

Beyond the food, Vietnamese Clay Pot Rice Restaurant is also known for its cozy and inviting atmosphere. Wooden furniture, rustic décor, and the aroma of freshly cooked rice create a sense of comfort that makes guests feel right at home. Whether you are dining with family, friends, or colleagues, the restaurant offers a relaxing space where good food and good conversations naturally come together.

Located on Cong Hoa Street, just minutes away from the bustling center of Ho Chi Minh City, the restaurant is easily accessible for both city dwellers and travelers. It has become a favorite stop for those who want to experience authentic Vietnamese home-style cooking in the heart of the city.

At Vietnamese Clay Pot Rice Restaurant – 234 Cong Hoa Street, every clay pot of rice is more than just a meal—it is a celebration of tradition, culture, and the timeless flavors of Vietnam.

BUT when we (2 people) were about to leave, many of them laughed and talked behind our backs because we didn't tip them. TIPING is when customers find the service excellent, so they give more, but why laugh at customers like that? Besides, you guys who serve others haven't given them a WOW feeling! You have to serve them in a way that when they leave, they will always remember you in a good way, then you can call it excellent! We didn't just come here once, if it was delicious, we would come back many times, and the way many of the service staff laughed behind our backs like that is VERY BAD!  That is UNPROFESSIONAL and VERY UNPOLITE, UNCULTURED. I was going to say a few words to those staff but my friend and I were having a good time so I didn't want drama. In short, I will NEVER visit such a restaurant a second time! I hope the restaurant will take your comments into account and the staff will serve other customers better!

ChIJeykSyjovdTERq8-UCmLeijA.text: Wow.    I am dizzy with all the 5-star reviews and I wish my experience was a 5- star too but it was not.   The food was so so and certainly below expectation.  The clay pot rice is just that: plain steam rice in a clay pot!    No burned rice at the bottom.    The clay pot fish was good with good chunk of fish fat and I haven’t had that for years and the fish was fresh.   The green banana with snail was not well cooked.   Maybe it was because we four were there toward the end of the day.   However there was no excuse for the workers to start packing the clay pot shards in the middle of the dining room while there were two tables of guests still dining.   And on top of that, the dining room was big and yet the two tables were next to each other!  At least should spread out to the opposite ends of the room so we can all have privacy.   It was the little things that separated a so-so restaurant from a higher class one.

ChIJI1U-Lu4udTER0hW-6M67SDA.author: Jennifer
ChIJI1U-Lu4udTER0hW-6M67SDA.text:
Hakka restaurant in District 11 of HCM City found in a narrow alley with a clear signage. The ground floor is the kitchen, and they bring the food upstairs. It’s definitely an interesting place, despite being a bit dingy, cramped and chaotic.

It’s my first time eating Hakka food, so I have nothing to compare to, however, I would say the taste was pretty good! The price was 1M something VND, and we were a crowd of around 10 people, so it was quite cheap!

We tried all the speciality dishes here:
• Khoai Môn Khâu Dục (Taro Pork)
• Tàu Hủ Đông Giang (Tofu Stuffed Three Treasures)
• Gà Hấp Muối (Steamed Salty Chicken)
• Thú Linh Chiên Giòn (Deep Fried Pork Intestines)
• Phá Lấu Giò Heo Thập Cẩm (Pork and Internal Delicacies)
• Lotus Soup
• Nước Sâm (Herbal Drinks)

I’d say I like the taro pork, steamed salty chicken and deep-fried pork intestines the most. Taro pork is an interesting taste – it tastes a bit like fermented bean curd, and the taro had a nice texture. Deep-fried pork intestines is also a must-try, it’s sweet and crunchy, and I never had intestines prepared this way before.

ChIJI1U-Lu4udTER0hW-6M67SDA.name: places/ChIJI1U-Lu4udTER0hW-6M67SDA/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNMaF9lUjNRRRAB
ChIJI1U-Lu4udTER0hW-6M67SDA.author: C
ChIJI1U-Lu4udTER0hW-6M67SDA.text: Tucked away in a small alley in District 11, Tiệm Cơm Truyền Ký is an old style restaurant that has been around since the 50s. Located on the upper floor of a shophouse, the restaurant is not very big and the environment won’t wow anyone with next to no decor besides a few Chinese style paintings. Note that the menu does not show prices. Expect to pay around VND200,000 per person for three dishes that is still within reason. The restaurant serves good tasting authentic Hakka dishes, including the signature steamed chicken with salt, which is a must-try. Popular among locals and certain tourists familiar with the cuisine, the staff are efficient but don’t expect warm Western-style service. If you are looking for a genuine Hakka dining experience, this is a great place to visit.

🌟 Review of Com Tho Truong An Restaurant - Di An 🌟

Having the opportunity to have lunch at Com Tho Truong An, I was quite satisfied with the experience here. The restaurant is located right on the main road, very easy to find, the space is clean and tidy. Although the area inside is not too large, it is quite cool inside, sitting and eating feels comfortable.

🌾 About the food:

The rice pot here is delicious, the rice is sticky, the side dishes are seasoned to taste.

I ordered the special portion and found it quite good in both quality and price.

I recommend everyone to try the special rice dish or char siu rice, the meat is soft, flavorful, eaten with vegetables and eggs, very delicious.

The accompanying soup is also a big plus - moderate flavor, not too sweet, refreshing, easy to eat.

💰 Price: Reasonable, compared to the quality, it is worth the money.

🚗 Small note:

There is limited parking space, especially during rush hour.

The service staff is okay, but if possible, they should proactively guide customers to choose dishes - especially for first-time customers, they should suggest the restaurant's signature dishes.

👉 In short: If you are looking for a delicious, reasonably priced rice pot restaurant in Di An, then Com Tho Truong An is a choice worth trying. I will definitely come back again to try other dishes!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️☆

Here’s a warm and enthusiastic review based on your visit to Cơm Niêu Thiên Lý:

A Taste of Home at Cơm Niêu Thiên Lý

If you’re looking for authentic Vietnamese comfort food, Cơm Niêu Thiên Lý is a must-visit. The flavors are incredibly rich and well-balanced—just like a proper home-cooked meal. Every dish we tried was full of soul and tradition, from the crispy golden cơm niêu (clay pot rice) to the tender, flavorful braised pork and fresh local vegetables.

The portion sizes are perfect—not too heavy, but definitely satisfying. It’s the kind of meal that leaves you full and happy without feeling overstuffed.

The service is consistently excellent. The staff are always friendly, attentive, and welcoming, making the whole experience feel even more like dining in someone’s home.

If you’re craving authentic Vietnamese food that’s prepared with care and served with heart, Cơm Niêu Thiên Lý delivers every time. Highly recommend!

ChIJQa8iZwApdTERoAfHTxtHJh4.name: places/ChIJQa8iZwApdTERoAfHTxtHJh4/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTUNnOW9TUkt3EAE

ChIJQa8iZwApdTERoAfHTxtHJh4.text:
This is a fantastic restaurant that offers authentic Vietnamese cuisine from all three regions—North, Central, and South. The flavors are rich and true to traditional cooking styles, making it a great place to experience the diverse culinary heritage of Vietnam.

I had the chance to try a variety of dishes, and overall, I was extremely satisfied. The food was well-seasoned, perfectly cooked, and presented beautifully. The highlight of the meal was the signature “cơm niêu” (clay pot rice), which had a crispy outer layer and a fragrant, fluffy texture inside. It paired wonderfully with other dishes, especially the braised meat and seafood options.

The menu featured many traditional Vietnamese favorites. The stir-fried vegetables were fresh and cooked just right, retaining their natural sweetness and crunch. The braised pork and fish in clay pots were flavorful, rich, and tender, absorbing the seasonings well. One of the most unique dishes was the purple yam soup, which had a striking color and a naturally sweet, earthy taste. The hot and sour soup with fish was another standout, balancing tanginess, spice, and umami flavors in a way that made it incredibly comforting.

Despite ordering a lot of food, my group of three managed to finish everything, which speaks to how delicious each dish was. The portions were generous yet not overwhelming, allowing us to try a variety of flavors without feeling too heavy.

The atmosphere of Cơm Niêu Đầu is warm and welcoming, with a rustic yet clean and comfortable setting. It feels like a home-style Vietnamese dining experience, which adds to the charm. The service was attentive and efficient, with staff making sure we had everything we needed throughout the meal.

This restaurant is definitely a place I will revisit every time I return to Vietnam. The authentic flavors, quality ingredients, and skillful cooking make it a must-try for anyone who appreciates Vietnamese cuisine. Whether you're looking for a nostalgic taste of home or an introduction to traditional Vietnamese food, Cơm Niêu Đẩu is a top choice in Ho Chi Minh City.

I immediately fell in love with the concept of “Cơm niêu”, and I’m heartbroken I won’t be getting a taste of it anytime soon. Offering claypot comforts intermixed with seafood and veggie stir fries, the braised cobia fish feigned innocence, initially concealed within a crowd. Like an assassin, it took my breath away after one taste, the flaky and tender flesh releasing an explosion of deeply sweet-savoury caramelized flavour. Along with the fish was a subtle brininess that complemented the sweetness to elevate this dish above the rest. Since there’s plenty to go around, you don’t have to fight your siblings over the best part of the rice: the crispy edges. The golden, crispy crust is contrasted with a soft, fluffy under-layer and accompanied with decadent crab fat sauce topped with fried pork bits to pack an extra dimension of texture. Another crowd-pleaser were the fried fish paste cake, with a flaky, golden-brown exterior and delightfully bouncy interior that’s packed with flavour. The veggies are stir-fried in garlic, and you’ll definitely know – garlic lovers rejoice – and serve as an extra component to the carousel of dishes to eat from.

Cha Gio Tom Thit : Spring Roll
Very crispy, very nice with the chilli sauce provided

Dau Hu Sot Ca: Fried Beancurd
Loved this beancurd in the chilli dipping sauce with the fish sauce

Kho Qua Xao Trung: Bittergourd with egg
not bad !

Bo Xao Thien Ly: Beef slices and Tonkin flower creepers
Was the best dish in my opinion so far, went so well with the grilled rice! I loved the taste of flower creepers and it was my first time eating it, it coated the creepers in sauce very well!

Canh Chua Ca Hu: Sour soup with Hu fish
Loved the citrusy taste in this soup due to the pineapples in it, the fish was very lovely with the vietnamese soy sauce

Nah Dam Hat Chia: Aloe Vera Chia Seed Drink
Very refreshing after a hot day of shopping!

Ca Thu Kho Thom: Braised Mackerel with Pineapple
Very savoury sweet, the sauce coats the thick meat of the mackerel well and when eaten with rice its a great meal.

ChIJXc4f_0gvdTERbE_ZFaJHuf8.author: Dominic Nguyen-Kessell
ChIJXc4f_0gvdTERbE_ZFaJHuf8.text:
I recently brought a few friends to Cơm Niêu Thiên Lý - Hàm Nghi for their last dinner in Saigon, hoping to treat them to some authentic Vietnamese flavors in a cozy setting. Having dined at Cơm Niêu Thiên Lý - Phu Nhuan many times before, I was confident in the food and as expected, it didn’t disappoint. The dishes were delicious, rich in flavor, and beautifully presented. It’s this consistency in taste that keeps me coming back and was the very reason I recommended it to my friends.

That said, this visit was unfortunately marked by a series of service missteps that made the overall experience less enjoyable.

From the moment I stepped inside, I felt slightly uncomfortable. There was a noticeable shift in attention, whispers, giggles, and the sense of being watched. While I tried to brush it off, my friends noticed it too. We were seated near the entrance and quickly realized the restaurant only had three English menus, a surprise, considering its location in District 1 and the size of the establishment. We had to share and supplement with Vietnamese menus, relying on Google Translate to navigate the rest.

The ordering process was more frustrating than it should have been. We clearly stated the dishes, reconfirmed everything twice and pointing to the pictures in the menu to ensure we got it right, especially more important since one of my friends doesn’t eat pork. He ordered two dishes, including a grilled mackerel, which never came until we followed up halfway through the meal. Even then, we received mixed messages: first, we were told it was sold out, then suddenly it was “on the way.” When it finally arrived, the fish was overcooked and dry, clearly rushed. Sadly, it was barely touched.

There were also other minor issues like an orange juice that was ordered but never served, only to be informed later (after following up) that it was out of stock. Ironically, the staff had no issue using Google Translate to inform us earlier that the tofu wasn’t available, so the inconsistency in communication felt frustrating.

Toward closing time, the atmosphere became increasingly uncomfortable. Several staff members lingered downstairs, watching us eat. It didn’t feel like casual observation, it felt more like we were being monitored, and a few of my friends found it hard to relax. I kept encouraging them to focus on the food, but I can understand how unsettling it can be when your every move feels scrutinized.

When the manager came to take payment, I did bring up the fish issue, but nothing came of it beyond a quick check and no follow-up. It felt like a missed opportunity to address a genuine concern.

In summary:
✅ The food was wonderful, especially for anyone wanting a true taste of Vietnam.
❌ The service and communication were lacking, especially in handling out-of-stock items and guest comfort.
❌ The atmosphere, especially near closing, felt tense and awkward.

I still appreciate the culinary experience this restaurant offers, but for it to truly shine, more attention needs to be paid to guest communication and ensuring a welcoming, respectful environment for all diners, locals and foreigners alike.

ChIJSzcDPAAvdTERE4cn7tPsWvg.text:
Follow @bredgyeats for more food posts!

Business strategy alert: Put "Com Nieu" in your restaurant name and you'll see me there. Expect a wide variety of braised fish and pork, slowly bubbling in a sticky and savory caramelized sauce that'll even make celery taste good. The cobia steak was a no-brainer, a delicately moist, tender and flaky flesh that has fully assimilated with the salivating sauce, which includes deep-fried pork fat and pork belly inside for a richer depth of flavour. The perfect pairing doesn't exis- oh wait, the golden crispy rice is the one you're looking for, adding a satisfying crunchy texture while toning down the saltiness of the fish. While the squash blossoms have a mildly sweet vegetal aroma on their own, I'm not opposed to getting a punch of garlic with each bite, either, with chunks of tender garlic that I did let go to waste.

ChIJX1yxUAAtdTERcq4dLSVNxoI.text:
Follow @bredgyeats on instagram for more food posts!

My thirst for Cơm Niêu and caramel braises continues, but I spiced things up with a different fish, where its smaller size doesn't mean less flavour. The deeply caramelized sauce is rich from the pork belly strips, pleasantly sweet, and just salty enough to pair nicely with rice. The tender flesh easily flakes off the bone, coupled with the fatty skin that has absorbed the addictive sauce for a blissful bite. They also served a side of herbs and veggies, because they know you wouldn't want to waste a drop of this sauce. The "thousand miles veggie" has a refreshingly soft, crisp texture and a subtle sweetness, which is tossed in a wok with garlic-infused oil, onions and whole cloves of garlic, that'll lure any garlic lover from miles away. The seaweed soup has a pleasant aquatic savoriness that's sweetened with dried shrimp for a clean tasting soup.

ChIJzV9a_L0vdTERvnha71r2Al8.text:
I had a very pleasant lunch at this charming restaurant. The standout dish for me was the crunchy rice mixed with seasoned minced pork. The texture of the crunchy rice perfectly complemented the flavorful, well-seasoned pork, creating a delightful combination. Each bite was a burst of taste and texture that left a lasting impression.

The other dishes we tried were equally well-cooked, each prepared with care and attention to detail. The flavors were well-balanced, and the presentation was appealing, adding to the overall enjoyment of the meal.

The ambiance of the restaurant added to the experience. The decor was cozy and inviting, creating a warm and comfortable atmosphere that made our lunch even more enjoyable. The staff, though not overly attentive, were friendly and courteous, ensuring we had everything we needed without being intrusive.

Several dishes were already out of stock by dinner, and while the staff explained they hadn’t prepared enough for the day (which I appreciated), it was still disappointing to adjust our order multiple times.

Service also felt a bit off: when I arrived alone, I was only told to scan the QR code and wasn’t offered a physical menu. Once my foreign friends arrived, a menu suddenly became an option. On top of that, drinks were served in paper cups with plastic straws, which felt more like a takeaway spot than a sit-down restaurant.

Good food, but improving service consistency and drink presentation would really elevate the experience.

ChIJK3Q-bP8ndTER2UKaXH9pWSE.text:
A Hidden Gem in Vietnam: Savoring Cơm Niêu Thiên Lý

Are you craving an authentic taste of Vietnam during your travels? Look no further than Cơm Niêu Thiên Lý, a restaurant whose very name evokes a sense of homely comfort and promises a true Vietnamese culinary experience.

1. Home-Cooked Charm with Franchise Convenience
Cơm Niêu Thiên Lý brilliantly combines the warmth of home-style cooking with the accessibility of a franchise. With locations spread across Vietnam, it's easy to find, yet each dish still carries the unmistakable touch of 'mom's cooking'.

2. Menu Diversity and Flavor
The menu here showcases the essence of Vietnamese home cuisine. From fragrant herb-filled pho to crispy yet tender fried dishes, every item is infused with care and attention. Don't miss their signature 'Cơm Niêu' - rice served in a sizzling clay pot - which the restaurant is named after!

3. Atmosphere and Service
The modest yet cozy interior makes you feel right at home. While the staff's English might not be perfect, their warmth and friendliness transcend language barriers. Consider this an charming part of your cultural immersion!

4. Value for Money
Enjoy generous portions and excellent taste at reasonable prices. It's the perfect choice for travelers looking to savor local cuisine without breaking the bank.

5. A Word of Caution
If you're sensitive to spicy food, remember to mention it when ordering. Vietnamese cuisine can sometimes pack an unexpected punch!

Conclusion: Cơm Niêu Thiên Lý is a must-visit eatery on your Vietnam journey. Here, you'll nourish not just your palate but your soul with the authentic flavors and hospitality of Vietnam. Highly recommended for all travelers seeking the true taste of Vietnam!

Rating: ★★★★☆ (4.5/5)
"Experience the essence of Vietnamese home cooking, served with love"​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Reasonable price, my family of 10 people ate for about 1 million.

ChIJ-YfQJNAndTERGJeZj04Xdos.text:
This restaurant seems to be a very good choice for family, friends or colleagues, especially for those who travel by car.
✨ Outstanding Advantages
* Space: Large and spacious, creating a comfortable feeling, not cramped.
* Parking Facilities: There is a free covered car park, this is a big plus, helping customers feel secure when parking, not worrying about the sun or rain.
* Cuisine:
* The signature dish is rich claypot rice.
* The food is deliciously seasoned, to the taste.
* Service: The staff is polite, showing professionalism and respect for customers.
* Price: Reasonable, suitable for the quality and service received.
📝 General Summary
This is a restaurant worth visiting with a harmonious combination of airy space, quality cuisine (especially claypot rice), good service and reasonable price. Perfect for anyone looking for a delicious, comfortable and convenient meal.

In general, the food is okay and clean, but the portion is a bit small and the price is a bit high. My family of 5 ate for nearly 1.4 million VND and was full.
Oh, I would like to suggest that the restaurant should let customers choose the dishes first and then when they need to order, they can raise their hand or call and the staff will come to order, because the staff standing and waiting for customers to choose the dishes and then order is a bit inconvenient. The rest is okay, the staff is lovely and enthusiastic.

ChIJjwEd5c0tdTER0gKPvC4fjlQ.name: places/ChIJjwEd5c0tdTER0gKPvC4fjlQ/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25KNVRVNHpNMFJzYlROVE4zaHJXa1F4TVZJd1JGRRAB

ChIJjwEd5c0tdTER0gKPvC4fjlQ.text: The restaurant has a popular name but the dishes are expensive. I would rather have a high price but a lot of food, then I'm ok, it deserves 5 stars. I've eaten at many restaurants but here I was quite disappointed and surprised. The burnt pork belly was 100/1 portion but there were only a few pieces, the rest was mainly stuffed with vegetables. The sweet and sour ribs were more than the other dish, about 1 finger joint, but at first I thought it was because the ribs had a lot of meat, but it turned out that the restaurant fried the outside with flour before stir-frying it or something?! The ribs looked big but in fact it was fried flour, the taste of the dish was no different from the fried chicken with sauce of some Korean restaurants, except for sesame. The sour soup was big, the taste was ok, for two people, 2 pieces of fish looked okay but the rest was a bowl of vegetables, all vegetables, maybe the restaurant was afraid that I would lack fiber😊 I also thank the restaurant for caring about customers like that. Overall, the claypot rice is ok, the taste of the dishes mentioned above is just right, but to evaluate whether it is worth the price is not, because there is too much stuffing. The seating area is clean, airy, the waitresses are also quite okela

ChIJpV_GgcAvdTERQyl-VgFo11Q.name: places/ChIJpV_GgcAvdTERQyl-VgFo11Q/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2s1YUxYWkhZMVJLVGpFMVZqaGpTa3g0VDNsNExXYxAB
ChIJpV_GgcAvdTERQyl-VgFo11Q.author: Olive Stone
ChIJpV_GgcAvdTERQyl-VgFo11Q.text:
Food is good. But the management has some serious issues.
I ordered the lunch set as in the picture, priced at 289k and confirmed with the waiter. Later they said one dish ran out so switched to another similar dish.

When paying the bill, the manager dramatically told me that the “set” we ordered from the picture is not a set, it’s just for “displaying the promotion”, so we need to pay at original price. After a few iterations of explaining, the manager finally agreed to let us pay the set price as in the picture plus price of the replacement dish (note that one dish is missing from the set but we still paid for it).

This is clearly a mistake of their side, although I’m not sure it’s intentional or not (hopefully not). But it’s really frustrating that the manager didn’t admit any mistake at all and just let the customer pay for the restaurant’s mistake. —— this is the wrong way to do business.

ChIJGYTfQkondTER6PIrpiBrHRQ.text:

A dish of climbing perch fish noodle soup is extremely fragrant and fantastic, thanks to the cool flavor of fresh water dropwort.

This store cooks the broth so well, which makes the bowl like great eating experience. The fried fish pieces are also well-flavored.

The only disadvantage of this place is the parking area, too narrow on the street while the guests are too crowded. We have been stuck sometimes for car, hence, Motorbike is highly recommended.

ChIJCZnbKAApdTERVRobUM1AcHc.text:
So glad to find this new southern family style comfort food place. I'm told there are several around HCMC but this location has been open around 2 months.

They have great meat and fish dishes but also many vegan options. There is both a large indoor AC area and a smaller outdoor open air area. Free parking by attendant in front. Plenty of friendly, helpful staff. We got there around 11:30 and the place quickly filled up with the lunch rush. Food came out quickly and I was surprised how FRESH everything was. And super clean. Fantastic meal!!! We will be back often.

The food was delicious and service matches its quality. This soup really got me emotional because of how much it reminded me of my grandma back in my hometown.
An only little criticism is that it says on the menu ‘canh rau đay’ but i got served ‘canh rau mồng tơi’ perhaps a bit of ‘rau đay’ was in there but not too noticeable.

ChIJldFENV0hdTER-KRq0-rrklY.author: Adam Luong
ChIJldFENV0hdTER-KRq0-rrklY.text:
What a great claypot meal!

The rich taste of home from the claypot rice bowl in the small claypot, the fragrant sticky rice grains mixed with the crispy burnt layer is excellent! Then add a piece of goby fish braised with pepper in the claypot, the fish meat is firm, rich in spicy flavor.

The indescribable sweetness is the bowl of pumpkin soup with shrimp, the shrimp is fresh, the broth is refreshing. The stir-fried vegetables are fresh and green. Everything blends together perfectly!

Truly a complete, heartwarming meal!

So delicious, just one bowl of the standard claypot rice set is enough for 2 people, full but still craving more 😂

ChIJldFENV0hdTER-KRq0-rrklY.name: places/ChIJldFENV0hdTER-KRq0-rrklY/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2s1VE16UXRVa3BLYkhWeE9FcDRja0U1VldwTmRVRRAB

ChIJldFENV0hdTER-KRq0-rrklY.text: I had a wonderful experience at Thien An claypot rice restaurant with my family and some friends this weekend. The restaurant is clean, decorated gently and cozy with lovely lanterns, the dishes are delicious, rich and authentic, especially the braised fish dishes. The rice is soft and sticky and has crispy burnt rice. The staff is very cute, enthusiastic and takes great photos. The owner is friendly and cheerful! 😊 Although the grand opening discount program ended when I arrived, the owner generously gave away a set of lotus seed sweet soup for dessert. Another plus point for the restaurant is that the restaurant is very spacious and has plenty of parking. I really like this restaurant and will come back many more times!

You do need to know what to get here.  We went for snails in salted egg sauce, some beef, and deep fried fish, boiled snails, and clams in Thai broth.  The food here was definitely better than the popular snails places in District 4.

Service was great!  This would be a good place to catch some soccer game as well.

YES I would definitely come back!

ChIJRd-SVNQodTERSC3YPdhnoOw.author: Manpreet Kaur
ChIJRd-SVNQodTERSC3YPdhnoOw.text:
I had the pleasure of dining at this amazing seafood restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City along with my husband and his office colleagues. Though I’m not familiar with Vietnamese dish names, every item we tried was absolutely delicious, fresh, and full of flavor!

🦪 We started with a beautifully presented razor clam dish topped with crushed peanuts, spring onions, and herbs – a unique and tasty combination that instantly set the tone for the meal.
🦑 The fried baby squid was crispy, well-seasoned, and cooked to perfection.
🦀 We also enjoyed another fried seafood dish (possibly soft shell crab or another variety of squid) that had the perfect crunch and went so well with the dipping sauces provided.
🍜 The highlight for me was the glass noodle stir-fry with seafood – light, flavorful, and packed with vegetables and juicy seafood bites.
🥗 We ended with a refreshing seafood salad served with rice paper and fresh greens – a healthy and flavorful end to a fulfilling lunch.
🍹 The mocktails and drinks were not just refreshing but also beautifully presented with cherries, herbs, and fun straws – definitely Instagram-worthy!

💯 The ambience was calm and inviting, perfect for a leisurely lunch. The service was prompt and friendly.

Even though I couldn’t catch the names of all the dishes (thanks to my husband’s Vietnamese colleagues who ordered), I thoroughly enjoyed everything. A must-visit for seafood lovers in Ho Chi Minh!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ – Highly recommended!

Ran Bien 5 is a great spot for fresh, high-quality seafood in a lively, local setting. You can choose your seafood straight from the tank — the selection is impressive and everything is cooked to order.

Highlights include the grilled fish, lobster with garlic, and sea grapes. The giant lobster sashimi was unique and refreshing. Everything was flavorful and well-prepared.

ChIJ06gXoi0vdTERqnMZRbp8ey0.name: places/ChIJ06gXoi0vdTERqnMZRbp8ey0/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUN2NWR2dGlBRRAB
ChIJ06gXoi0vdTERqnMZRbp8ey0.author: Min Min
ChIJ06gXoi0vdTERqnMZRbp8ey0.text:
Ran Bien excels in showcasing the best of seafood with its carefully crafted dishes.

### Steamed Crabs
The steamed crabs are a highlight, boasting sweet and tender meat that melts in your mouth. Cooked to perfection, they are often served with a side of zesty dipping sauce that enhances their natural flavors.

### Grilled Squid
The grilled squid is another standout, offering a delightful char that complements its tender texture. Marinated in flavorful spices, it’s grilled just right, making it a perfect appetizer or main dish.

### Hotpot Sturgeon Fish
The hotpot sturgeon fish is a must-try for those seeking a comforting and flavorful experience. The rich, flaky fish is simmered in a savory broth, infused with aromatic herbs and spices, allowing diners to customize their bowls with fresh vegetables and noodles.

### Steamed Shrimps
Finally, the steamed shrimps are impeccably fresh, served simply to highlight their natural sweetness. Paired with a light garlic sauce or enjoyed on their own, they are a delightful treat.

Overall, Ran Bien’s seafood offerings provide a delicious journey through the ocean’s best, making it a top destination for seafood enthusiasts!

ChIJr_6wlhsvdTERe8DZY6TzM_g.author: Ray Tan
ChIJr_6wlhsvdTERe8DZY6TzM_g.text: Pretty expensive live seafood place. Decor is pretty nice and comfortable. Suitable for occasions. The menu is pretty extensive. Thankfully there was a waiter who could speak mandarin to help us out. Ordered a papaya salad with fish cake (Vnd380k) that’s recc by the staff. I think the taste is alright. The fish cake is pretty interesting. They retained almost the whole shape of the fish and the body is made up of fish cake slices. Also ordered a pumpkin soup (Vnd220k) also recc by the staff. It’s not bad. Has plenty of ingredients inside the pumpkin soup. The soup tastes abit on the sourish side tho. Main highlight here has to be the salted egg lobster that’s about 500gm (~Vnd1.2mil). Because it’s fresh lobster, the lobster meat pops out of the shell easily with the fork. Dip the lobster meat into the salted egg sauce and go straight to the heavens. The sauce is creamy with hints of salted egg that’s not too heavy. Also ordered a shrimp fried rice (Vnd250k) that ended up abit too much for 2 pax. Didn’t manage to finish the fried rice which was kinda wasted. The fried rice tasted alright but i like they were generous with the shrimps. Total dmg for 2 pax comes to Vnd2.5mil after taxes. Pretty darn pricey if you ask me. Felt the recommendations fell kinda short.
