ChIJQSfN0kQpdTERbO0_ug2hJ30.author: Alan Huynh
ChIJQSfN0kQpdTERbO0_ug2hJ30.text: One of my favourite omakase restaurants in Saigon. The service is spectacular and they also let you know what it is and where it’s sourced from. It’s also an interactive experience which makes it so much more worth the amount you spend. They also have an a la carte menu that’s worth checking out and they have recommendations for what to get. I got the diamond set which I believe is good value.

ChIJQSfN0kQpdTERbO0_ug2hJ30.name: places/ChIJQSfN0kQpdTERbO0_ug2hJ30/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xSd1JuTnpaM2M0VTFwRk1UUmphV1JFYld3eVptYxAB
ChIJQSfN0kQpdTERbO0_ug2hJ30.author: Phuong Duy Ngo
ChIJQSfN0kQpdTERbO0_ug2hJ30.text: Recently visited Omakase Raichi restaurant and was very satisfied with the experience. The food was great, and the selections were truly impressive. We chose the Experience Menu and the Journey, and I feel that for the price, we received exactly what we should have. Everything was well-prepared, flavorful, and worth it. Overall, I’m very happy and would definitely recommend it.

ChIJQSfN0kQpdTERbO0_ug2hJ30.name: places/ChIJQSfN0kQpdTERbO0_ug2hJ30/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2tFemFHVXdOemhWT1hOamVrWnNVRmxuVVVGWVZYYxAB
ChIJQSfN0kQpdTERbO0_ug2hJ30.author: Paul Tran
ChIJQSfN0kQpdTERbO0_ug2hJ30.text: We had a wonderful experience here at Raichi Omakase. The staff were very professional and provided us with a memorable dining experience. The food quality was top notch and presentation was amazing as well.

ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.name: places/ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2kxVWNYcENVamt6ZVVGdU5tOXpSSHBCYVVwUFZIYxAB
ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.author: Co
ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.text:
Very good experience. I booked by calling the number. I wish they had a WhatsApp instead. Arrived at 5pm on a weekday so it was empty. Only one person showed up at 5:45. I suppose you can wing it by just showing up during opening.
A lot of plates were good. I quite like the tempura which is the only item I didn’t photo thinking it was too basic.
The sardines from the appetizer was good as well. It’s strange that the most basic things tasted the best. They had some fish I didn’t even recognized but it was average. The wagyu was also basic. I would probably order the 1 mil meal instead of the 1.5 mil one next time.
The chefs there didn’t interact much.the server was the only person that explained things to me. I wish the chefs would be a bit warm.
Overall not bad with room for improvements. This is a franchise apparently so they stuck by the guidelines.
The only item I didn’t finish was the miso soup.

ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.name: places/ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2tNeFNWSmZUbXh2VVZSVmFHOTJVWE5NVW1nellYYxAB
ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.author: Felix
ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.text:
We tried the omakase premium here at Kiyosa.

A packed menu with a lot of different varieties of fish.
I think from our personal experience we didn’t love or hate it. I think we preferred less white fish and that could have changed the overall rating much more.

But if you are interested it’s really worth trying.

Our favourite were the bluefin tuna, soup & fried cod.

Try it you won’t be dissapointed. Our chef was kind and listened to our preferences too ☺️.

ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.name: places/ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2tGRGFFZ3hWWGR6U1VkelQwSmxPRWg0UVZaV1ZFRRAB
ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.author: Philip Dao
ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.text: No frills! Just solid Omakase experience. The top set will be enough for a grown man with big appetite. My daughter couldn’t handle the 1M vnd set. Oishikatta desu!

ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.name: places/ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUN2bGE2djRRRRAB
ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.author: Trang Nguyễn
ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.text: If you're a true sushi lover, this omakase experience is a game changer. Every dish was meticulously prepared, showcasing an incredible balance of flavors and textures that just melt in your mouth. The freshness of the ingredients was unparalleled, and the chef's attention to detail made every bite feel like a work of art. The atmosphere was intimate yet sophisticated, making it the perfect place for a special night out. Absolutely a top-tier dining experience that’s worth every penny. Highly recommended for anyone looking to indulge in an unforgettable culinary journey

ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.name: places/ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUR2bm9TelNBEAE
ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.author: Binh Nguyen
ChIJt8HYcDEpdTERWjiTDfYwaqI.text: My best omakase experience ever!! The best bang for the buck. Cost was only $80 per person and you get a ton of dishes which were all delicious. Small intimate place so make sure to reserve if you can. My girlfriend is in love with omakases now haha. This experience in a large US city would cost $300-400! I will definitely come back next time.

ChIJDXGIZXovdTERFfW60vIVcJo.name: places/ChIJDXGIZXovdTERFfW60vIVcJo/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2pKMmFuUmlZelpFUWxkWWRIaGlkVkF0Y21KcVVIYxAB
ChIJDXGIZXovdTERFfW60vIVcJo.author: martina teo
ChIJDXGIZXovdTERFfW60vIVcJo.text:
Is linh fish sauce served in the Omakase set? Pure egg coffee without vanilla? Or sashimi served with sorbet-like cream sauce? Steamed eggs with pho broth? Dessert cakes using wagyu beef fat as fat instead of butter? Do you think I said it wrong? No!!!! That's right, in the Omakase set by Uchi at Uchi Sushi District 4 branch, which has just opened for 1 week, there is a dish with sauce made from linh fish sauce that has been skillfully processed to no longer have a fishy smell, or the dipping sauce is condensed into sorbet-like cream to be used with sashimi instead of using traditional soy sauce. The ingredients are completely fresh, dry-aged sashimi is also a novelty. I have used Omakase in many places, but this is the first time I have enjoyed Omakase that uses food processing techniques to elevate it to a new level, more classy, ​​and more sophisticated. I chose Omakase by Uchi to celebrate my birthday and it was well deserved, I was praised to the skies. In addition, right at the central location of District 4 with a very affordable price, you should come and try it!!! In addition, there are 2 chefs who are very cute, attentive and humorous 🤣🤣🤣
A very strange and unique experience!!!

ChIJDXGIZXovdTERFfW60vIVcJo.name: places/ChIJDXGIZXovdTERFfW60vIVcJo/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT21aNk1HRmpjemhtV0V0V1lUVkxZVlU1Vm00dFUyYxAB
ChIJDXGIZXovdTERFfW60vIVcJo.author: nguyen duong
ChIJDXGIZXovdTERFfW60vIVcJo.text: Enjoy delicious food while the chefs prepare and introduce each dish one by one. Have a wonderful birthday experience at Uchi Omakase ☺️☺️

ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.name: places/ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT214WExVZGphM0U0UzJOd1NIaFVWMFZaTVVoNVZWRRAB
ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.author: Hamerline Daniel
ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.text:
Leave the chaos and noise behind and step into a warm, welcoming place — just sit back in your chair and enjoy the good food. Let go of your worries and soak in the cozy atmosphere inside the restaurant.
The chef is prepared every dish with great care.
I truly enjoyed the evening with a well-priced omakase dinner. Don't rush, take your time, eat slowly, and savor each flavor. If you’re unsure about anything, just ask — the chef will happily explain with a good voice and won’t hide anything.
Good price, good food, good dinner. The last dish felt like a special gift. Thank you, chef.

ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.name: places/ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT21WWVh5MVpOVEpyV1d4eFpHeDVibkpZUkVKalpYYxAB
ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.author: Ha Pham
ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.text: Have great time at Tumaru tonight. My husband and I have such a pleasure to be hosted by the owner - anh Tu'. The fish is amazingly fresh with unique taste. The sake pairing is in another world. We love the stories behind every little things here. The restaurant is a cozy and lovely place. We tell the owner that it feels like visiting his home kitchen and we are treated like friends. Definitely come back.

ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.name: places/ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xjdFJVTXRja2QyV0VwVUxYVnRjelpKYUhCSVRHYxAB
ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.author: Exzer Geas
ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.text:
First omakase in VN – mixed feelings at this cozy, 10+ seats counter spot. We booked the top-tier **Chef Care (899k/pp)**, advertised as an exclusive monthly selection.

**What went wrong:**
1. **Drinks ambush** – Chef Tu asked “alcohol?” without prices or menu. We said yes; he poured a sake that rang up at **800k**. Only after I questioned it at the end, he gracefully offer 50% off. **Pro tip: drinks are *not* included – ask upfront.**
2. **No perceptible upgrade** from Chef Choice (699k). Both are 15 small plates; most prep done by assistants, with Chef Tu adding final touches. Expected the premium tier to be chef-led.
3. **Minimal storytelling** – “Fish from Nha Trang… shrimp… OK?” No origin, cut, or technique shared. Felt like eating fresh but basic ingredients, not elevated omakase. Dont expect special tuna cut, beef kobe or premium pieces.

**What worked:**
- Intimate vibe, beautiful plating.

At **2,2M+ for two** (post-discount), value doesn’t match the price. Fine-dining elsewhere delivers more value for the spend. Wouldn’t recommend unless you love experimental bites and clarify every extra cost. And choose chef choice combo 699/ pax.

ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.name: places/ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VLVDlyS2lQeWR2b0RREAE
ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.author: Frederic Fayard
ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.text: Nice little restaurant in a japanese - fusion style. Decoration and atmosphere is very pleasant , quiet and pretty. The food is nicely prepared with a good sense of presentation. I only regret that with the course option chosen the main dish is only pasta in a creamy sauce with little seafood , even if it was well done. Also the tea service is not at the expected level with tea bag dropped in a cup, dropping to 4 star a service otherwise very good.

ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.name: places/ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25sd2FFRTRXbGg0T0ZoV2IxSXpTRGR0Y25GTWJFRRAB
ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.author: Huyen Thuong
ChIJJRl5t8QvdTERPKGBAog9k_Y.text:
If you’ve ever fallen for Midnight Dinner or the unmistakable charm of eateries around Tân Định, Tumaru is your next stop.
A quiet space where the tattooed, soft-spoken chef hosts, cooks, and shares stories — whether you’re dining solo or not.

Tumaru doesn’t try to impress. It simply connects.

Come by. Let Tumaru do the rest!

Plus:

If you’ve followed Chương Đặng’s culinary journey — from Ru Phở Bar to Fish Sauce, Ghém, Nhà Anh, Nhà Tôi — you’ll sense the same quiet precision and intention here at Tumaru.

Lighting is gentle, music is just right, and each dish is thoughtful without being showy. The chef’s quiet presence anchors the space — turning a meal into something deeper. Whether you’re alone or with friends, Tumaru holds space for you.

ChIJ9w8arSsvdTERlI51IhKYnoc.name: places/ChIJ9w8arSsvdTERlI51IhKYnoc/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2tSdWRYSnBkbTl0T1ZJeE1tbEVlV0oxZDJaYWJYYxAB
ChIJ9w8arSsvdTERlI51IhKYnoc.author: Nguyễn Ngọc Khánh Ly
ChIJ9w8arSsvdTERlI51IhKYnoc.text: Luxurious space, fresh food, enthusiastic chef. Worth the experience!

ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk.name: places/ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25oUlpYWnpZWEpHZWtOeFJHMDNlR05CTldGbVMzYxAB
ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk.author: Ross Hwang
ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk.text:
I was invited to the newly opened Niku Fella, located just above Rokafella, and it was truly an unforgettable experience. This was my first real five-star yakiniku meal, and it set a whole new standard for me. I’ve dined at several Michelin-starred restaurants, and honestly, I wouldn’t be surprised if Niku Fella earns one in the near future.

The quality, the service, and the overall atmosphere were absolutely mind-blowing. If you want to impress someone who thinks they know food, this is the place to bring them.

ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk.text: An unforgettable dining experience! The ingredients were incredibly fresh, beautifully presented, and full of flavor. The chefs were skillful and attentive, and the staff made us feel truly welcomed. Highly recommend for anyone looking for an elevated omakase experience in Saigon. Will definitely come back!

ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk.name: places/ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25RM1ZVTkVlWFJUVEZGSWJUQmFlblpMTUVWUlQxRRAB
ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk.author: Michael Phạm
ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk.text:
We had the absolute pleasure of celebrating our anniversary at Roka Fella, and from start to finish, everything was exceptional. The food was nothing short of incredible.

The atmosphere was intimate and inviting, striking the perfect balance between elegant and relaxed.

What made the night truly unforgettable, though, was the amazing staff. They went above and beyond to make our celebration feel personal and meaningful. From the thoughtful touches to the genuine service, we left feeling not just satisfied, but genuinely cared for.

ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk.name: places/ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VLMjYyZGplc1l6SG93RRAB
ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk.author: Mỹ Uyên Bùi Lê
ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk.text:
We visited Roka Fella for my birthday and we reserved the table one day before arriving. The service was still nice at the beginning but it kept being weird and quite disappointed for me. From the moment we arrived, there were 4 guests including my bf and I, the manager introduced us the set menu with 2 options and recommended the beverage. After that moment, he completely forgot us and constantly chat with his friends ( the other 2 customers). Yes it was definitely an awkward feeling since the main chef did not say a word to us until the end of the meal. There were two Viet chef, one for the first haft and one for some final dishes. The only chef shared us the information about food and asked us feeling was the young one whilst the manage and the others randomly stared or eventually ignored ☹️ If the store was too crowded to manage, that’s fine. However, there were 4 clients but the service was still not good as our expected.

The food was very mouth-watering and fresh, giving the actual mouth feel and we could identify the taste and texture of every single dish.

The staff were quite well-noticed but with the experience of an omakase restaurant, comparing to others in SG, I think they can do better.

ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk.name: places/ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25CeU4xaEtMVzV3WWtkUFZua3RjVVZLWm1RelluYxAB

ChIJC_2LkuYvdTERWGgNpWZ1ruk.text:
One of the best omakase spots in Saigon! Roka Fella delivers a creative, modern take on Japanese fine dining—with top-notch ingredients flown in from Japan and a vibe that blends 70s Tokyo cool with an intimate chef’s counter. I had the premium set and every dish—from the uni nigiri to the foie gras and smoked oyster—was beautifully executed and full of flavor.

It’s not cheap, and some dishes are on the rich side, but for a special night out or a sushi lover's splurge, this place is absolutely worth it. Make sure to book ahead—seats are limited!

ChIJ-4cpfvUudTERd6IQ0W2UGTM.text:
45,000 VND/bowl includes 3 tongues, 3 stomachs, 1 blood, 1 intestine.
15,000 VND/1 bone. In terms of price, I think it's not cheap but not too expensive. Includes 1 glass of iced tea.

The first spoonful is really wow, the broth is delicious and has a fragrant smell of fried garlic and light five-spice powder. The tongue and stomach are lightly braised with coconut water to absorb the flavor and are delicious. As for the pickled cabbage, I don't really like it because the taste is a bit sweet and the sour taste feels unnatural.

The older uncles and aunts take a while to serve.

The sidewalk space is small but very neat and extremely clean.

ChIJ-4cpfvUudTERd6IQ0W2UGTM.name: places/ChIJ-4cpfvUudTERd6IQ0W2UGTM/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VQYjgtYW4xd2R6OVN3EAE
ChIJ-4cpfvUudTERd6IQ0W2UGTM.author: TuyetNhung Nguyen
ChIJ-4cpfvUudTERd6IQ0W2UGTM.text:
I came here on a rainy day, it was almost time for her to close the stall but luckily she still accepted the last group of customers. It was raining but luckily the porch was high so the tables and chairs were extremely dry. 

My first impression was that the tables and chairs were extremely clean, stainless steel chairs, long and large stainless steel tables, I thought she was selling on the sidewalk but invested too much in quality tables and chairs, but when I sat down to eat, I observed that her house was opposite the sidewalk where she put the tables and chairs, there was a floor of dishwashing liquid on the side of the house. So I was very assured about the hygiene. 

I ordered a full bowl without bones. I gathered all the toppings on top so everyone could easily visualize. A portion of 45k includes Ho noodles (quite a lot), 4 slices of stomach, 3 slices of pig tongue, 1 blood clot, 1 piece of intestine and pickled cabbage (put together in the bowl). 

💥 The tripe is quite clean, cut into large, long pieces. Because it is a tripe stew, it is more fragrant than the tripe stewed in soup at noodle shops. Next time I go out to eat, I will definitely order more tripe to enjoy it.
💥 The pig tongue is also delicious, not fishy. I saw in the review that someone said there was duck meat. I think that person mistook the pig tongue for duck meat because it is chewy. The noodles here only have intestines and bones.
💥 The tripe is also delicious, but I think it was only one piece because it was all gone. Because the table after me said it was all gone.
💥 The blood is soft and sweet, but I'm not sure if it is duck blood or pig blood because now there is a method to make pig blood as soft and smooth as duck blood.
💥 The bowl of pickled cabbage costs an additional 5k. Because I ate it near closing time, I found the soup a bit salty, so I ordered more pickled cabbage to balance the taste. But personally, I found the pickled cabbage a bit sweet. I expected it to be bland, not too sour, not too sweet.

I think many people will feel that 45k for this bowl is a bit high. But personally, I think the price is reasonable because the stomach, tongue, and small intestine are all expensive parts.

Are there fried garlic and pork fat or something? When I arrived, they were probably all gone, only a little fried garlic was left.

Free iced tea. There is a separate tea pot and a separate glass of crushed ice. I think it is very delicate 😍

SHE DOES NOT SELL ON SATURDAYS AND SUNDAYS. OPEN FROM 11:30 AM - 6:00 PM

ChIJYReesPMvdTERN-_WDkVR_8k.text:
Honestly, what universe does this restaurant live in that they charge such prices? A sidewalk restaurant, not even a decent table, from the pickled chili to the spice jar, you can tell they don’t respect their customers. Ordered a bowl of noodles for 70k but they brought out exactly 3 beef balls, 3 noodle chopsticks that could be counted on one hand. The broth was as watery as vegetable washing, without any soul of bone broth – probably mixed with trust and tap water. 

I ate and thought I was being trolled, like the “eat poor and be classy” or “pretend to be rich for 5 minutes” challenge. After eating, I just wanted to ask: “Huh, is this also called selling food? Or are you filming with a hidden camera?” The money spent felt like it was thrown in the trash, I’ve never seen anything 70k can buy… a lesson in illusion. 

Please, if you don’t have a heart – at least have a vision. If you don’t have both, don’t make people pay to eat a dish that doesn’t deserve it.

ChIJ3Tp-pIYndTER5Ubj4kXTwyQ.author: Liza Ngo
ChIJ3Tp-pIYndTER5Ubj4kXTwyQ.text:
If you are looking for an interesting culinary destination in the Western region, Sa Dec noodle shop and crab noodle soup are suggestions not to be missed. The restaurant not only stands out with its signature dishes but also brings unforgettable culinary experiences. 

Distinctive flavor: 

The noodle soup here is prepared with clear, refreshing broth, not too fatty but still very rich. The noodle soup is chewy and delicious, blending perfectly with meat and spices. You can choose to add ingredients such as shrimp, pork, or even quail eggs to increase the appeal. 

Crab noodle soup is also a highlight. The naturally sweet broth from fresh crab combined with soft, chewy noodles creates a dish that is both delicious and nutritious. In particular, the freshness of the ingredients makes the dish even more attractive. 

Specialty dish: 

A special feature that the restaurant brings is the noodle soup, which is skillfully prepared. The intestines are cleaned, crispy on the outside but still soft on the inside. The delicious flavor of the intestines adds richness to the meal, making it hard for you to resist. 

Space and service: 

The restaurant has an air-conditioned room, suitable for families with small children. The female staff are enthusiastic and quick. 

In short, Sa Dec My Tho noodle restaurant is an ideal destination for those who love Western cuisine. With rich flavors, especially delicious intestines, this place will definitely bring you wonderful culinary experiences. Visit the restaurant to feel this attraction yourself!

ChIJm6lIUrIodTERm_yDITnKCeQ.text:
This duck noodle shop in the bustling heart of District 2 is always packed—whether it’s breakfast, lunch, or dinner—and for good reason! I ordered the dry duck noodle and a salty egg bun bao, and the flavors were incredible. The duck meat was so tender and cooked to perfection, and the authentic taste of the dish really stood out.

The bun bao was hearty and satisfying, leaving me so full I struggled to even think about dessert afterward! I love places like this where the constant crowd guarantees a high turnover of fresh ingredients. It’s a true gem for anyone craving authentic flavors and a lively atmosphere. Definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area!

ChIJm6lIUrIodTERm_yDITnKCeQ.author: M
ChIJm6lIUrIodTERm_yDITnKCeQ.text:
[Update Jan 23, 2025] I finally tried this again. I had only tried it once, and that was around a year ago. It continues to be extremely popular. All the tables are taken pretty much during the entire evening rush. For me, they wanted my money enough, they put me at an occupied table of a father & young daughter. There is more seating on the alley side of the restaurant.

The taste of the duck was real before. This is probably going to be either the best or of the best duck you will have in Vietnam - I have had it a few places around HCMC. The meat is juicy and flavorful; it just falls off the bone (I should have taken a video splitting off the drumstick, not just flipping it over...).

That being said, I noticed the worker wrote down 110K for the bill, even though the menu states 108K/$4.30. It's a matter of pennies, but it's the principle I care about. I intentionally did not use the wetwipe they gave me, knowing it would cost 2K (I believe that should be free for a 100K+ meal). Upon paying the bill, it was explained to me that she gave me sauce + the radish (?) side dish, and that costs 2K/$0.10. The radish wasn't great, and I forced myself to eat half because I didn't want to waste it, but I did use the sauce. Had I known the sauce wasn't free, I wouldn't have taken it. The duck is good enough without sauce. It's the fact she forced me to pay for it when it wasn't what I ordered. I ordered specifically the 108K duck (pointing to the menu). I did not point to or indicate I wanted the sauce, which is on the menu at the bottom, which she pointed out to show me it's listed.

You don't need the sauce, but it does taste good (teriyaki/soy based sauce).

--

If you check my reviews on Google or Naver (kimchi4dinner), I rarely use words like "best" or "ever." This place is so popular when I walk by, I wanted to try it, but I get dissuaded when I see too many people in such a tight space... I passed on it the night before, so I waited this time (a few minutes). I got a seat across another (Korean) gentleman eating alone (the only seat available).

I don't know if there are multiple duck dishes here, but if you've never tried duck before... this is the place to try it; specifically, you need to try the duck noodle soup. This may be the best duck I've ever had. I've had duck in multiple countries and it's usual prepared the same (baked, roasted, maybe grilled), however this duck is prepared, it's juicy, flavorful, and the meat pretty much falls off the bone - which is how you want any meat, whenever/wherever you have it.

I don't know how to say it, so I pointed to the guy's food across from me. It's 108K ($4.45), which is maybe 2.5 or 3 meals in this area, but it's worth it. Presumably, it's 108K specifically because they assume you don't bring your own napkins/wet wipes (like I usually do, but didn't this time) and will use it... and like most places, they cost money (not a lot, but...); 2K ($0.10). It would have been 110K, but I got water because they don't serve or give tea water (which, for a place as popular/that makes as much money as this, they can't give that away for free, like a lot of other places...?). Regular size Aquafina is 12K ($0.50) - the same price as a 1.5 liter bottle at most convenience stores.

**The noodles are from across the street.**

****

There's a noodle place almost across the street that doesn't appear to have a name or I can't find it on Google Maps [I've tried to add it several times, but it won't be accepted despite my Maps reputation and activity]. But the guy makes good noodle dishes for cheap. I ate there a few nights ago and had two dishes (mostly because I was hungry and they aren't the biggest servings). If you are facing the street outside of this place, look for a guy with a noodle stand and his wife has a juice/beverage stand (they are to the nearest left, across the street).

The noodle photos are from there; most are [35K/$1.40]. The top one, mi xào bo are ramen noodles with beef and the second one (nui xào bo) is long macaroni noodles with beef; both are good.

ChIJ_dqk9NEpdTERmYeQZoe3Hi0.author: Baljeet Singh
ChIJ_dqk9NEpdTERmYeQZoe3Hi0.text:
Tried Cháo Ếch Singapore – Tân Định, and honestly, this roadside spot surprised me in the best way. The frog porridge was rich, flavorful, and cooked perfectly — that thick, silky porridge with the clay-pot frog hitting just right. The seasoning was balanced perfectly, not too salty, not too sweet, just that classic Singapore-style taste.

The vibe is different — very casual and down-to-earth, right on the roadside, which somehow makes the meal feel even more authentic. Service is quick, and the food comes out piping hot.

If you love comforting, homestyle dishes, this is a spot you shouldn’t miss. Definitely a place I’d come back to for that warm, flavorful experience.

ChIJFwuPZkYvdTERU09XCwNUHV8.text:
I was quite surprised by the poor service at this restaurant, especially given its prime location in District 1. The staff’s attitude was indifferent — when taking my order, the server spoke unclearly, without complete sentences, and offered no recommendations. I found the service to be unprofessional and borderline disrespectful.

Although the restaurant was not busy, the staff seemed more focused on chatting among themselves than attending to guests. As for the food, the porridge was decent. However, the kumquat tea was quite odd: it was served hot with ice added directly into it, which melted almost immediately. I had to request more ice afterward. Overall, the drink felt poorly thought-out and far below what I would expect from a proper restaurant.

ChIJ5YxUDHwvdTERPejI8cN6xjU.author: Tuong Truong
ChIJ5YxUDHwvdTERPejI8cN6xjU.text:
A place to eat that tastes okei but I won't choose to come back because of the service.

- TIME: I went twice on Sunday morning and Saturday morning

- LOCATION & PARKING: located in the bank residence so the road is clear, parking on the sidewalk next to the wall of Phu Dong Primary School, comfortable to drive and park on the sidewalk. Free parking

- SPACE: cute, open in a private house, cool, there is a table inside the living room, a bit stuffy because of the narrow width. The table is high and the chairs are comfortable. The only thing is that the pink plaid tablecloth is very cute but the color fades a lot, those of you wearing white shirts or long-sleeved shirts should be careful not to lean or rub too hard.

- SERVICE: the sellers and waiters are middle-aged women around 50 years old, the style of the shop is similar to the way of communication and service in indoor markets such as Ben Thanh market, Xom Chieu market. Young people and people of the younger generation will not be familiar with this way of service.

And I really don't like going to shops where the sellers discriminate when I look young and am not with an elderly person. When I went with my sister, the owner's attitude was different from when I went with my mother. Even though I went with my mother, the owner was only warm and enthusiastic when my mother praised her for being young :)))
In terms of service, I do not appreciate it. The ladies did not come to the table to take the order and I proactively called, and asked again many times even though I had given full information.

- THE SPECIAL THING that made me not choose to come back is the key is the PRICE is not transparent and clear. In the photo I took of the menu, the prices are in the form of "approximately" 10-20k, 3-10k, 25-45k. When it comes to calculation, she only says the final price, doesn't explain how much, and she calculates whatever price she wants
The most recent time my sister went with her friend, she ordered the beefsteak with the price she wanted, but when it comes to calculation, she calculated it at the highest price, my sister asked and she said that dish doesn't have the price my sister said, that price is the price...

- TASTE: I find it very tasty, I've tried beefsteak, stir-fried beef noodles, grilled pork noodles, broken rice
The flavors all have the typical pan flavor of a cast iron pan, seasoned very well, the amount of oil is just right, not too much oil, the beef is soft and delicious
The broken rice with ribs is well marinated, the fish sauce is delicious, the rice is fluffy and standard
I ate those dishes with my relatives, and the stir-fried beef noodles was my main dish, it was very delicious, the noodles were not mushy, just moist, the sauce coated evenly, the beef was delicious and not tough.

But for me, eating out is a comfortable experience without cooking and going out with family. I can cook delicious food. But I choose to eat and come back because of the comfort, kindness and service. So I will not choose to come back because of the bad experiences of myself and my relatives. 

If you choose to eat, I think you should order carefully and ask for the price when looking at the menu, agree and clearly then order and can order with the price like the 30k pasta to avoid confusing experiences.

ChIJsc1jBdPZdDERtwhA_tUaWhw.text: Just the first morning of the year, I went to eat beef and avoided that food, and it ruined my morning. I ordered a 4-course beef course to eat everything, and the dish I wanted the most was meatballs. When it was brought out, there were no meatballs, so I asked the staff why this 4-course course had meatballs on the menu but they didn't come out. The staff mumbled and said they didn't have meatballs yet. I was like, "What do you mean, no meatballs? It's on the menu?" Then the staff didn't answer and turned around to continue taking orders for other tables?? Ok, I waited for the order for the other guests to finish, I asked again, the answer was still "no, probably in the afternoon" and then turned around and walked away in my surprise. Why did you say you only have meatballs in the afternoon when I had breakfast? At least I just needed an answer that if there are no meatballs now, can you compensate me with something else? Why don't you have any yet? The money was paid in full, but you said it's not good enough? It's not worth much, but hearing the staff answer me like that, I'll give it 1 star. It took away a whole fun morning, thank you staff ^^

ChIJj-xCXxEmdTERrS28ElM7q7M.text: Texas Chicken at Vincom Megamall serves hot, crispy, and flavorful food that really hits the spot. The fried chicken is perfectly golden and juicy inside, especially the one topped with sweet soy glaze and sesame seeds which adds a delicious touch of savory sweetness. The fries are thick, crispy, and well seasoned, while the biscuit is soft inside with a nice buttery crust and just the right hint of sweetness. I like that they also include rice with the meal which makes it filling and satisfying. The service is quick, the staff are friendly, and the place is clean and comfortable. Overall, it’s a great spot to enjoy a tasty and hearty meal when you’re at Vincom Megamall.

ChIJn0t-km0vdTERS_syK3aG0sk.author: Bảo Châu
ChIJn0t-km0vdTERS_syK3aG0sk.text:
Contribute a small loving review to the long-standing Guot restaurant. The address is on Khanh Hoi street, under the Kenh Te bridge, when you get close, you can slow down to avoid being tricked. The restaurant is not too big, but on average, most of the customers are regulars, so I think it's okay. And the restaurant uses fans, not air conditioning, so the number of customers who dine late, around 7-8pm, I think it would be better. In addition, there are some female employees who are also cute. And the special thing that you may not like about this restaurant is that because there is usually 1 main lady and 1 assistant, it usually takes a long time to serve the dishes. If you are not patient, you will probably be annoyed, so you can try to order all at once to avoid waiting. The owner's service attitude is cute, so you guys can come and support, I'm used to eating so I'm also used to waiting for food, if you're a little confused about this for the first time, you can happily ignore it 🥹
Regarding the amount of food for each dish, I feel it's easy to match the price and for groups of 2 people, you can enjoy many dishes. On average, I order about 3 dishes at night and feel ok. I can eat quite a few dishes, the 3 dishes I usually order the most are Spaghetti with minced beef sauce 35k, Chicken with cream sauce 40k, Toast lava with salted egg 35k and for water, I like the melon black tea 15k. For a group of 2 people, if you usually don't drink too much, you can order a shared cup of soup, most of the time I will do that and if you don't have a sweet tooth, you can tell the owner to make it a little less sweet. If you have a big appetite, you can tell the owner to make a lot of noodles, but if you usually eat for 2 people, that's enough.
According to my preferences, I usually choose toast with salted egg lava or salted egg cheese for 40k, which is better than sweet toast because it's delicious but easy to get bored. Shaved ice no longer sells black pearls like before and I find it a bit too sweet for me so I don't order it anymore. I find hotdogs a bit dry for me so they're not too good. This June, it seems like the shop is promoting hotdogs with milo milk for bills over 100k. My favorite old dish of the shop is super delicious fried pork rind rice paper, but I asked because the quantity of rice paper can't be sold in time, the quality is not guaranteed and it's easy to dry out so she doesn't sell it anymore 😢 If possible, I hope the shop can sell it again 🫶🫶🫶

The owner is quite cute and enthusiastic. Oh, the restaurant also has plantain and Singaporean tofu, which you should also try, because the owner cooks them himself... eating in one go, you'll want to finish the entire menu at the restaurant, making it worth the effort to go so far, and not forgetting to buy a bunch to bring home... after eating, I thought... maybe I'll move to District 7 to visit the restaurant often.... in short... ChIJzfWyaiMvdTER_OBWmI4onDc.text:

Nice local vibes, friendly atmosphere, and great value for money. Definitely recommend stopping by if you’re around HCMC!

There a lot type of beverages u can select. For me i chose "Rau má đậu" to feel less heat in the room as well as foods

ChIJzfWyaiMvdTER_OBWmI4onDc.text: Tasty food, especially the summer roll. They offer two versions of the rolls- the usual pork and shrimp and pork skin rolls. The highlight was the panfried Chinese carrot cake with egg with a side of papaya salad (very fibrous), taste of the original flavour of charred egg and carrot cake but there’s seasoning and sauce that can be added if you prefer. The service is nice, people are helpful even if you do not speak Vietnamese but the cleanliness can be improved as the floor is littered with trash.this is a common practice in many local shops but is a bad practice that can be corrected easily at no cost.

ChIJAzYqnCEvdTERjoi4SmDXq80.text: My usual Banh Trang Nuong lady no longer has her stall on Cao Thang Street. I did a google search and found this cool place. To start they have a massive area and very roomy for their customers. I was very impressed that they were able to have this much land and space to serve their customers. It’s also street view so you can just watched the motorbikes go bye they were super busy, so I’m very happy for their business overall. The banh trang was average. Wasnt as good and crunchy as my previous go to spot. Price was affordable.

ChIJAzYqnCEvdTERjoi4SmDXq80.text:

Note that they have two locations. One is in an alleyway next to The Coffee House, and the other is in front of the Ford dealership across the street. Usually just one of the two spots is open.

ChIJAzYqnCEvdTERjoi4SmDXq80.name: places/ChIJAzYqnCEvdTERjoi4SmDXq80/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNBd1lhcjJ3RRAB

ChIJAzYqnCEvdTERjoi4SmDXq80.text: This is some kind of pizza that can't never be found elsewhere around the world. It's a flattened rice cake with a very thin layer of fried scrambled eggs, onions, scallions and a few toppings like dried beef and minced octopus. It's spicy and crispy. Highly recommended. And one more thing, you will most likely have to queue and wait for your dish (usually around 10 mins), and the seat is a very small chair. If you're a tall guy like me, it might bother you a bit. Enjoy.

ChIJWaXCK38pdTERjb9HHLlZTR4.name: places/ChIJWaXCK38pdTERjb9HHLlZTR4/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTUR3eGJPWlBBEAE
ChIJWaXCK38pdTERjb9HHLlZTR4.author: M
ChIJWaXCK38pdTERjb9HHLlZTR4.text:
They have a very large menu.

I thought what I had was pretty good. Mapo Tofu is one of my favorite Asian dishes. I still have a hard time understanding why it doesn't come with rice in Vietnam (some places it does come with it, but most do not). I had to order rice (20K/$0.80) after seeing the tofu.

This version (108K/$4.20) is pretty good. The portion size was good. The meat in it was good. Good amount of spices.

Adding the one cup of rice into the bowl was a perfect amount.

The wings are cheap (36K/$1.40 ea), but they are small (2 per order). Tried the honey verison; they were good.

20K/$0.80 for water, I wish more restaurants in Vietnam provided free water/tea water... especially when we're paying 8% VAT, like here.

ChIJWaXCK38pdTERjb9HHLlZTR4.text: Skewers here are freaking delicious 🤤 The Sichuan fried chicken is on the top of favorite list from this restaurant. The grounded spices are so good to go with any skewers. They do have the canned herbal tea it’s perfect to relieve the summer heat. This place is good for hanging out with large group with fresh beers and handful of skewers. I went here for lunch, it’s so hot. I would recommend dinner would be a perfect occasion. We ordered several dishes in that grilled egg plant, pork skewers are lasting taste. 👌🏻🤩 I would like to come here again.

ChIJ3-tpreEudTER-taj1HegQwE.text:

The taste was the same as when I ate it at the restaurant in District 2 and it was very good.
Apart from the hotpot, there were many other tasty dishes and the portions were large, so I was very satisfied.
When I visited, the residents of the house opposite had a large speaker outside and were singing karaoke.
It was extremely noisy, making it difficult to eat in peace and difficult to have a conversation with the people I was with.
This was not the restaurant's fault, but it was very unpleasant.

ChIJ1YY0ogIvdTERKYE0D0foqVA.text: Sometimes you stumble on a business which just nails it, Teos bakery or ABC bakery is ones of those places. We wandered in and had a look and were impressed with the cleanliness, the extensive variety of pastries, cakes etc, and the eatery which is on the left side of the bakery. We decide to grab a bite to eat and a cold iced tea each and WOW, were we impressed, extremely happy with the dishes served, the attentive staff and service. Prices were good, food was quality and tasty. Couldn't been happier. Highly recommend this establishment for locals and especially for foreigners. Thanks Teo for being a place where I can trust the food to be of high quality. And thanks to the staff who were all helpful and pleasant to interact with.

ChIJr0wsUkcvdTERMAP_2H5EOXA.text:
Terrible buying experience - I went in with my mom and my aunties as they were craving for ice cream after our dinner.

My mom wanted a Vanilla/ Matcha soft serve (with a cone), I read it off their menu “Soft Cream Mix” and pointed at the picture simultaneously. She then ansked ice cream or soft serve, I thought that she didn’t hear me, I repeated it again “soft cream mix” and pointed at the picture again. And she’s like “So you want ice cream or soft serve, it’s different!”, I don’t even understand why she’s getting so annoyed. I replied “I just said what’s written on the menu (see menu in the pictures I attached)”.

She insisted that I have to specifically tell her soft serve or ice cream even when I already read what’s written on their menu and pointed at the product I want. I do understand the difference between soft serve and ice cream 😅, I found myself flexible enough to go with the name of their menu, but received an unacceptable attitude.

With that being said, my mom and my aunties did like their ice cream and soft serve, but won’t come back with this terrible service.

ChIJk4dbgeUvdTERUB-JzpQqAXY.author: Jenny White
ChIJk4dbgeUvdTERUB-JzpQqAXY.text: We enjoyed our meal here. The place gives us an authentic vibes of Northern Vietnam. Though it’s a bit costly, the foods are worth the money. Every dish we had was really tasty and the portions are big enough to share. The “cha ca la vong” was so good and the tofu in scallion oil is highly recommended. The staff are attentive, accommodating and polite. The best part is the ambiance and comfortable seats. The menu also offers a wide variety of sumptuous local Northern cuisines to choose from. The drinks menu includes healthy options. The only reason for 4 stars is hoping to have smaller portions for affordable options later on. We’ll be back!

ChIJk4dbgeUvdTERUB-JzpQqAXY.name: places/ChIJk4dbgeUvdTERUB-JzpQqAXY/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURiODlqa3VBRRAB
ChIJk4dbgeUvdTERUB-JzpQqAXY.author: Scott Nguyen
ChIJk4dbgeUvdTERUB-JzpQqAXY.text:
My experience at this restaurant was disappointing from the moment I walked in. It took several minutes for the staff to acknowledge my presence and show me to a table, during which the owner was audibly yelling at the staff, creating an uncomfortable atmosphere. Once seated, I was left waiting without a menu, which was frustrating, especially given the extremely loud music that made it nearly impossible to call over a server.

After finally receiving the menu, the service continued to be slow and inattentive. The chaotic environment overshadowed the dining experience, leaving me feeling more stressed than relaxed. The food, while acceptable, was far from memorable. It was simple, and while it tasted fine, it did not justify the high prices. For a lunch that was meant to be straightforward, the cost felt excessive, particularly when considering the poor service and unwelcoming atmosphere.

Overall, the experience was underwhelming and not worth the price. The chaotic environment, inattentive service, and overpriced food made for an unpleasant visit. I would hesitate to return, especially with so many other options available that offer better service, atmosphere, and value for money. This is not a place I would recommend.

ChIJBxJudLgvdTERRYD9jSs8atE.text: This is a great place to come for a typical Vietnamese meal.  We had Thịt kho trứng, canh rau cải, and rau muống.  Pork, egg, greens, soup with more greens, and rice.  Everything was delicious.  This isn’t a fancy meal but it feels like home.  The restaurant is hard to find, there is a garage off the street and you’ll need to take the elevator or climb the steps up to the 3rd floor.  The staff is welcoming, but there were no tourists here when we came which I’ll take as a good sign!     Their English here is limited but the menu is easy to navigate.  Give this place a try if you’re looking for a traditional casual and nutritious Vietnamese meal.

ChIJBxJudLgvdTERRYD9jSs8atE.author: Weinnie Ho
ChIJBxJudLgvdTERRYD9jSs8atE.text:
This restaurant had me cursing under my breath while climbing two flights of stairs, still half-recovering from a fever. My friend swore it was worth it, so I dragged my weak body along, ready to judge. Tucked in what looked like a very questionable old shoplot, on the second floor (if my dizzy memory serves me right), we finally found it. And to be fair… it actually looked quite decent once we got in.

The vibe is very Vietnamese, cozy and unpretentious, like someone’s home turned into a restaurant. We ordered a bunch of local dishes—not your usual pho or banh mi, but more unique, traditional items you don’t see everywhere. I have to say, the food surprised me. It was tasty, different, and felt pretty authentic. My sick grumpy self was slowly converted into a full-bellied happy customer.

Now, I’m a total clean freak, and this place passed my test. The cutlery was clean, the table wasn’t sticky, and I didn’t feel the need to sanitize everything twice. If you’re up for a little adventure with good food and a hidden gem vibe, I’d recommend giving it a go. Just maybe go when you’re feeling healthy enough to climb.

Review of fried chicken thigh rice

The restaurant serves fried chicken thigh rice very well. The chicken is native chicken, the meat is firm but still soft and sweet, not the type of chicken that has been rejected, so it feels natural and much more delicious. The skin is fried to a moderate crispiness, when bitten it makes a crackling sound but the meat inside is still juicy and not dry.

The fried rice is fluffy, the portion is just right, accompanied by a beautifully presented salad, very suitable to eat with. There are also young lemongrass leaves cut a bit large but still create a pleasant flavor. The plus point is that there are braised chicken giblets, which is quite unique and makes the rice dish more special. The dang leaf soup is cooked to a delicious taste, balancing the fatty taste of the fried chicken.

Service: polite and quick staff. There are gloves for customers to hold the thighs. The restaurant has a spacious car park and a clean restroom, quite comfortable for customers.

👉 Overall, this is a choice worth trying if you want a delicious chicken rice dish, with good taste and good service.

ChIJOR2EZqvZdDERvxJ1oZZ3p9Y.text:
The restaurant "Am Thuc Me Nau" on the Ring Road, Ho Chi Minh City National University Village is a favorite destination for many students and locals, thanks to its cozy space, diverse menu and reasonable prices. Below are some detailed reviews of the restaurant:

### 1. **Space**
- The restaurant has a cozy and simple space, family style, with simple tables and chairs, creating a cozy feeling like at home.

- The restaurant's decoration is quite comfortable and airy, suitable for simple and not too fussy meals.

### 2. **Menu and food quality**
- The restaurant is famous for traditional Vietnamese family dishes, with rich flavors and familiar, easy-to-eat seasoning. Rice, soup, braised, stir-fried dishes... are all prepared simply but retain their delicious taste.
- Some of the outstanding dishes are sour soup, braised fish in clay pot, braised pork with pepper, stir-fried vegetables, fried chicken with fish sauce... These dishes are often rated as having a familiar flavor, full of the taste of home-cooked rice.

### 3. **Price**
- The price is affordable, suitable for students. Meals usually range from 20,000 to 50,000 VND, depending on the dish and portion.

- This is a big plus for the restaurant, because many students and workers around the National University Village area choose to come here to have a nutritious, delicious meal that is not too expensive.

### 4. **Service**
- The staff are friendly, enthusiastic and serve quite quickly. Although the restaurant is often crowded during peak hours, the waiting time for food is not too long.

- The restaurant is also very flexible in serving take-out customers, convenient for busy students.

### 5. **Clean space**
- The restaurant is kept clean and tidy. The dining table and serving area are often cleaned thoroughly, creating a comfortable feeling for customers.

### Summary
- "Am Thuc Me Nau" is a suitable choice if you want to find a simple, cozy family meal at a reasonable price. Delicious dishes, stable quality and friendly service attitude have helped the restaurant become a familiar destination for many students and residents of the Ho Chi Minh City National University Village area.

ChIJwRZq7vsudTERovOIsztOAPA.text:
All around very decent seafood restaurant in Vietnam. You pick the seafood from the tubs or live fish tanks, and they’ll cook it their way or the way you recommend.

What stood out here was how fresh the seafood was. I wouldn’t say I liked all the flavour combinations that came with the seafood, but the seafood itself was very fresh and cooked to a moderate to good standard. The whole concept of Vietnam being shaped around the seafood we had this night was quite expensive, around 500 AUD all up, but it was a good experience to try everything.

The style of cooking their veggies, especially the bean sprouts, tasted really good. The other veggies lacked a bit of greenness and had a lot of stems, but that’s alright. Staff were very attentive, refilling glasses, topping up ice, and staying on top of everything. They definitely encouraged cash payments more than cards, but they came around and took the card we wanted to pay with.

Favourite dish was probably the blood cockles. I think that’s what they’re called. They were very nice and fresh.

ChIJ98k-SyQvdTERDU8T9bdMkpo.text:
Updated to 3 stars: Unfortunately our last visit here, we got advised a fish dish costing VND 4 Million / Portion. The pricing is unreasonable and should have been clearer.

Prime location, fresh and decent food, diverse but pricey menu.

This place is a local favorite as they are well-positioned on a relatively large street. Spacious parking lot, security folks will have guidance for those parking their car on the busy street of CMT8 so that's a plus.

The menu is very diverse, as they walk you through all of the available seafood options, fresh catch, and seasonal favorites (which is decent for seafood Quán Nhậu).

Food: The crab are splendid, their tamarind sauce crab is savory, sour, and sweet, highly recommend to order for some side bread to dip in the sauce; Salted Garlic Fried Crab is mid - lil bit dry; crispy fried rice is always nice; other sea snail are ok (Spotted Babylon snail (ốc Hương) steamed with lemongrass - not too chewy, light, sweet, and fresh; lemongrass Steamed Clams - ok, expected taste; Pepper grilled Imperial Snail - tbh it tastes odd for me - chewy, like traditional Chinese medicine...

Overall: you will like the food here, but expect to pay a fat bill to experience everything.

He came back after the girl went to the bathroom to clean herself, and he came back without a towel, just a mop for the floor. That was just odd - no urgency to make sure the customer was ok.

The prices are probably standard for the type of place and food. The chicken was a whole chicken for around 300K ($12.30). The frog legs were about 80K ($3.30). The hot pot was probably around 300K as the total was 737K ($30.25). There was other seafood, lobster, shrimp, etc. on the menu that was 400K~1 mil.

ChIJt2SrTVIpdTERnm6Bl7aTagk.author: Nickolas Ho
ChIJt2SrTVIpdTERnm6Bl7aTagk.text:
Here's the translation and review in English for the restaurant "Nhà Hàng Biển Đông 10" in Ho Chi Minh City:

---

I’ve visited this restaurant many times. It’s a favorite of my family. The space is spacious with air-conditioned rooms. The seafood here is very fresh, with many options available in the tank. Today, we ordered grouper fish with pickled mustard greens, grilled shrimp, garlic butter shrimp, Thai-style steamed clams, grilled giant clams with scallion oil, and stir-fried vegetarian noodles. The shrimp was fresh, although it was grilled by the method of “boiling first and then flame-grilled,” so while it was sweet, it wasn’t particularly special. The seasoning was tasty, with a strong garlic fish sauce flavor, but not too salty or greasy in the garlic shrimp dish. The giant clams were large, tender, and delicious. The Thai-style broth for the steamed clams was quite flavorful, rich in Thai spices but adapted to the Vietnamese style. However, the clams were a bit chewy, although they were large and firm.

The standout dish today was the grouper fish with turmeric and pickled mustard greens, which was very delicious. Despite the fish not being super fresh (since it was cut the day before), the turmeric broth had such a rich flavor that it masked the slight lack of freshness in the fish.

The service was attentive, with staff available at the table. The space is spacious, making it perfect for family gatherings or hosting parties. I’ll definitely return to try the fish again when I’m in the mood for seafood.

ChIJCdtAJp4ndTER_x5VCnLYkyY.author: Hà Trang Minh (Bryan Trang)
ChIJCdtAJp4ndTER_x5VCnLYkyY.text:
Ốc Sam, located at 203 Hoàng Diệu 2, Linh Trung, Thủ Đức, is a popular spot for seafood lovers, but my recent weekend visit left much to be desired.

The restaurant’s lively atmosphere draws a large crowd, especially on weekends, with tables packed and a bustling vibe.

However, this popularity comes at a cost. The staff, overwhelmed by the crowd, seemed perpetually busy and struggled to keep up with orders. I waited nearly 30 minutes for my drink despite multiple reminders, which was frustrating and disrupted the dining experience.

The menu boasts a variety of seafood dishes, from grilled snails to stir-fried clams, but the quality doesn’t match the steep prices. For instance, the sò huyết (blood cockles) were lukewarm, and some felt undercooked, raising concerns about freshness.

The sò điệp phô mai (scallops with cheese) was a highlight, but at 50,000 VND for seven small pieces, it felt overpriced compared to similar spots nearby.

The noise level was another downside—conversations were drowned out by the chaotic chatter and clatter of dishes.
While the open-air setting is spacious and parking is convenient, the overall experience was underwhelming.

For the high prices, I expected better service and consistent food quality. I’d recommend visiting on weekdays to avoid the rush, but proceed with caution and manage expectations.

In general, it is not called too excellent but this snail shop has ok food, the price is relatively
.
📌 6:00-7:00 pm is the right time for customers, so it's easy to miss dishes, get the wrong dishes, or wait for a long time, so go eat early for comfort

ChIJR_a6CqIvdTERDJM-ayAreuM.author: Bella Sie
ChIJR_a6CqIvdTERDJM-ayAreuM.text:
Ambiance and service was absolutely impeccable. Food was OK.

My favourite bite was the Salmon Mozzarella Sushi because it was playful and had fun flavours.

I had high expectations for the Crab Spaghetti, but it was clearly made from boxed pasta, was unfortunately bland upon first bite, and desperately needed extra seasoning. Thankfully there was chili oil, salt and pepper at the table to bring it up to a better level.

Re Pizza, I love that you can order 1/2 and 1/2. The burrata itself was the best I’ve ever had, and the first bite of the Burrata Parma Ham was nice and crispy, but the Spicy Seafood half was unfortunately soggy. I also wish the pizza was served after we finish the pasta so that we could have enjoyed it hot instead of cold. The service was so fast and attentive that if anything, it could have slowed down a bit for better pacing of each plate, but that’s just my personal preference.

Overall, I can see why this place is a hit for locals, but as someone coming from North America where incredible pizza and pasta are abundant, the food was not as remarkable as what I can access at home. Regardless, I do think this brand is a vibe and I would come back for a special occasion because the service and atmosphere make up for what I felt the food lacked.

ChIJR_a6CqIvdTERDJM-ayAreuM.name: places/ChIJR_a6CqIvdTERDJM-ayAreuM/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT214bGFITjVWa1kwZFhsMk1USkVOWFZRY2xwUmIzYxAB
ChIJR_a6CqIvdTERDJM-ayAreuM.author: Brewforone
ChIJR_a6CqIvdTERDJM-ayAreuM.text:
People often raise an eyebrow when I tell them one of my favourite spots in Saigon is a Japanese-founded fusion Italian restaurant  but Pizza 4P’s has been consistent since my very first visit in 2019. Starting from their amazing architecture and great interior design, it’s simply a place that’s mastered the balance of great food, warm service, and an amazing overall experience.

This visit was extra special, two birthdays, good friends, and the kind of meal that reminds you why you love eating out. From the fresh salads to the comforting pastas, everything was just as I wanted it to be. The crab pasta was a standout, rich yet balanced, and the mushroom soup was pure comfort (should have ordered more tbh). But it’s the pizzas that always steal the show  that doughy, slightly crisp crust, with the creamy burrata.

We came on my friends’ last day in Vietnam, and by the end of the meal, they were genuinely bummed they hadn’t discovered it sooner. Pro tip: make a reservation. It’s popular for a reason. It’s not uncommon to have to wait 30-60 minutes if you didn’t make one.

ChIJR_a6CqIvdTERDJM-ayAreuM.name: places/ChIJR_a6CqIvdTERDJM-ayAreuM/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25RelNVZHFWak0zUlRrNWNHRnFPRmx3Um1zek1GRRAB

ChIJR_a6CqIvdTERDJM-ayAreuM.text:
Being honest, I don’t know what was better — their food or their customer service. It’s a highly welcoming place where everyone does their best to make your visit as pleasant as possible. I really love that, even though they don’t speak perfect English, they make every effort to ensure you have an amazing experience and delicious food.

Talking about the food — oh my goodness! You have to try the plate in the photo, I could easily say that dish is their best seller. We stayed in the city for only one night and went there twice just because of it. We also loved their tiramisu — it was really good.

The restaurant’s architecture is absolutely gorgeous, which makes enjoying your meal even better — and it’s very photogenic too!

ChIJR_a6CqIvdTERDJM-ayAreuM.name: places/ChIJR_a6CqIvdTERDJM-ayAreuM/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25KSmVXeEdabm8zWTJrM1JteEZSRlJEWjNWRFIxRRAB
ChIJR_a6CqIvdTERDJM-ayAreuM.author: K T
ChIJR_a6CqIvdTERDJM-ayAreuM.text:
The taste just doesn't match the price and the expectancy of all the high praise reviews. Despite the pleasant to look presentation the food was to many degrees overpriced for portion's content and taste. The crab pasta was rather bland and did not stand out in either terms of taste or aroma. Pizza wasn't crunchy, rather thin and chewy plus the lacks of toppings for a pizza with the price ~220+. Drinks are really expensive even for the standard of imported goods. The only thing that was amusing to enjoy was the burata fruit salad. Staff service was quite alright though being a bit too enthusiastic with really fast speech giving customers a hard time to take to process information. The place was cozy, murky suitable for couples on special occassions and those that enjoy dim lights and "baby-care service with a fee". If you are rich and would like to show off go ahead and make reservation
But if you are looking for REALLY good food with reasonal price this is definitely not your destination.

P.S: The following noon after the date that this review was written I was reached out to by 4P's management staff and asked about points that the restaurant can make improvements on. I was vaguely given a general question and replied with a preciprocal inquiry of which exact areas of concern that they would like to hear more about. By which point I was asked about the specific listed items reviewed above & the term "baby-care with a fee" to clear out any misunderstanding. For those that wonder the same I'll put it plainly the term is meant as being highly taken cared by staff members with service fee included in food&drink that is ordered and for sure isn't low for a high end place. The call wasn't the best with staff management complaining about poor connection and having a hard time  listening to answers through out. It made me wonder whether it was a genuine reply regarding the fact that from where I was to the site is only roughly 1.3 km and both places are positioned in dense urban area. It was an akward experience BUT despite all kudos to Pizza 4P's for actually reaching out for better communication regardless of different opinions&experiences.

ChIJIy0x28YndTER7utjXIAfciA.text:
Tucked right in the center of Thảo Điền, District 2, iBiero is a spacious, open-air craft beer spot that’s perfect for a relaxed night out. The outdoor seating is super chill – ideal for catching up with friends or winding down after work.

Price-wise, it’s actually more reasonable compared to other craft beer places in the area like Belgo or Pasteur Street. A 600ml glass is just around 80k VND, which is a great deal for the quality.

The dark beer is super aromatic and smooth – definitely a standout. The passionfruit beer, on the other hand, didn’t really leave much of an impression – drinkable, but nothing special.

Food-wise, it’s okay but not amazing – pretty average, so don’t expect too much there.

Staff were friendly and helpful, which always adds to the experience.

Just a heads-up: last order is at 11:00 PM and the place closes at 11:30 PM. There’s a small surcharge if you stay late, so plan accordingly.

ChIJIZJKIdohdTERiwK82VzF7Fo.text:
First time trying Domino's VN. Compared to Korea or the US, the most notable difference is the M size I ordered. M here is an S in Korea/US. Bigger than a personal pan, but it's definitely smaller than I anticipated. However, that isn't bad, because I choose not to eat much pizza anymore due to how unhealthful it is... seeing the size made me feel better about eating them. I ordered the BOGO (2 mediums) for myself. *To their credit, it does say "9 in" next to the size.

Overall, the prices are cheaper here than in Korea (for a medium, it's more comparable for the US) 235K/$9.45 ea. For the promotion, I had to order 2 sodas 25K/$1 ea, but for the two med pizzas and 2 sodas, I paid 354K/$14.25. That also includes a special crust for one of them. So, it was a good deal.

The habanero cheeseburger was something I've never had. It was pretty meaty; good. I tried it with a sausage parsley crust (something I've never heard of in Korea or US - maybe they have it now?). That was 69K/$2.75. It was interesting, but not what I expected. I thought it was going to be regular Domino's sausage, but it was closer to a salami stick.

I've also never had a seafood lime pesto. Lime pesto sauce is common for VN, and it might be my favorite sauce for chicken and burritos.

Both pizzas were good.

ChIJRwa4wvAudTERdSwp1eH5m98.author: Betty
ChIJRwa4wvAudTERdSwp1eH5m98.text:
[5 Stars] The Dim Sum Dictator: Incredible Flavors, But They Don't Wait for Anyone! 🥟⏰
The Good: The food quality here is exceptional. Every single dim sum we tried was fresh, meticulously prepared, and burst with flavor. The Siu Mai is perfectly juicy, and the Steamed Rice Rolls (Bánh Cuốn) are a masterpiece—delicate and savory. This place delivers on the promise of high-quality, traditional điểm tâm. The staff are fast, efficient, and clearly masters of handling the morning rush.
Suggestion: This is a crucial note for first-timers: Show up early! The kitchen operates like a well-oiled machine, and once they run out of a popular item, they simply don't make more. For a place with this level of demand, slightly extending the production window or better communicating item availability would be fantastic. They need a warning sign: “The Early Bird Gets the Har Gow!”
Bottom Line: This is a fantastic place for top-tier, authentic dim sum that will change your morning. Set your alarm and don't be late—this place does not mess around! Totally worth waking up at dawn for!

ChIJSXOEKEkvdTER2RWY5v7PfAU.text:
I stopped by Sushi World on Le Thanh Ton for a quick lunch after finishing some work nearby, and overall it was a pleasant experience. I hadn’t planned to eat there—it was more of a spontaneous choice as I was walking down the street. The first impression was actually very positive. The security guard at the entrance was incredibly warm, polite, and helpful, which immediately set a welcoming tone. Small gestures like that make a difference, and I really appreciated the friendliness right from the start.

For lunch, I decided to keep things light and ordered a seaweed salad and avocado sashimi, both vegetarian options. The seaweed salad was fresh, crunchy, and seasoned nicely. It had the right balance of tanginess and umami that you would expect from a Japanese-style salad. The avocado sashimi was simple but satisfying, presented neatly and with just the right texture. While it was not overly elaborate, I liked that the food felt clean, light, and refreshing—exactly what I wanted for a quick midday meal.

The service inside the restaurant was decent. Staff members were polite and efficient, though not overly engaging. Given that I was just there for a short lunch, I didn’t mind, but compared to higher-end sushi places, there is still some room for improvement in attentiveness and overall refinement of service.

The atmosphere of the restaurant is casual and comfortable. It’s the kind of place where you can stop by for a quick meal without too much fuss, but still expect a certain level of quality. Prices seemed reasonable for the location, especially considering it is right in the center of District 1.

Overall, I would rate my experience four stars. It wasn’t the most exceptional sushi lunch I’ve ever had, but it was a satisfying and enjoyable stop. If you are in the area and want a quick, fresh, and light Japanese meal, Sushi World is definitely worth a try

ChIJgZxVyz4vdTERaPz33y1E_gk.author: The Laughing Lion
ChIJgZxVyz4vdTERaPz33y1E_gk.text:
This place is a slice of Tokyo in the Heart of Saigon.
Sushi Tei, nestled in the bustling heart of District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, offers a truly delightful dining experience that's well worth seeking out.  You're transported to a contemporary Japanese haven. The multi-level dining space adds an element of intrigue, creating distinct atmospheres perfect for both intimate dinners and larger gatherings. The trending design, with its clean lines and subtle Japanese accents, adds a touch of modern elegance without feeling overly trendy.
My recent dinner at Sushi Tei was nothing short of fantastic. I was particularly impressed by the freshness and quality of the fish.
I loved the tuna and the salmon. Beyond the sushi, the menu boasts a wide variety of Japanese dishes,
What truly elevated the experience was the attentive and friendly service.  They were quick to refill drinks, clear plates, and genuinely seemed invested in making our dinner enjoyable.
From the moment we were greeted to the moment we left, every detail was carefully considered.  The presentation of the dishes was beautiful, adding to the overall sensory experience.  Even the chopsticks and tableware felt thoughtfully chosen.  This level of attention to detail, combined with the delicious food and excellent service, made for a truly memorable dining experience. All of this came at a surprisingly reasonable price.  For the quality of food and service offered, Sushi Tei provides excellent value for money.  Its prime location in District 1 makes it easily accessible, adding another point in its favor.
If you're looking for a top-notch Japanese dining experience in Ho Chi Minh City, Sushi Tei is a must-visit.

ChIJgZxVyz4vdTERaPz33y1E_gk.name: places/ChIJgZxVyz4vdTERaPz33y1E_gk/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTUNRam9YVDBnRRAB
ChIJgZxVyz4vdTERaPz33y1E_gk.author: Frank Adams
ChIJgZxVyz4vdTERaPz33y1E_gk.text:
We’re in the area and came across Sushi Tei. What a pleasant surprise. They were very welcoming and polite. The place was extremely clean and we were seated right away. You know you can always tell if a restaurant is clean by looking at the bathroom. The bathroom always reflects the kitchen. And the bathroom was very clean just like the restaurant. Our server Thans was very pleasant. She spoke very softly and politely. Thans did not rush us. We had a lot of questions and she politely answered them. Thans had great recommendations from food choices to drink choices we had the guava mocktail and passionfruit mocktail they was so delicious,It was one of her recommendations. The food did not come quickly, but in a reasonable time and that’s very important. That means they take the time to make it fresh and you can really tell the quality of food is good. All the sushi tasted delicious and I’m definitely coming back. If you’re in this area, I recommend you stop by and get some great food with great service. Hopefully you get Thans because she’ll make you feel like you’re at home and always have a smile on her face. Thank you so much for the great service and I can’t wait to come back.

PS I forgot to mention the cute sushi doughnut, made with sushi rice we had the salmon sushi doughnut. Great for a picture and tasted delicious.

ChIJ89fACMAvdTERZVAAAAlanMc.text:

Salad is fine, just the dressing is bland.

Green tea is the easiest drink to make, also bad, and I was disappointed when they served in a plastic cup like for buffet, so from hot turned cold quickly.

All of the above would be 1 star.

I think the reason why I give 2 stars is because of the Okonomiyaki, it's good.

Oh yes, if receipt above 500k will have a free sashimi plater (not so fresh), which I will give another 1 star as an encouragement.

Pricing is not cheap so of course customers deserve to expect a better quality and better service.

ChIJ-cFjHgMpdTER8E4QPeI0ciU.author: Richard Levy
ChIJ-cFjHgMpdTER8E4QPeI0ciU.text: I love to eat. I normally don’t enjoy leaving a bad review about any restaurant, I normally only rave about the good things simply any place can have one bad night. But, this restaurant screamed for a terrible rating from me. To start : 1/ this place has a nice ambiance. I understand it is Friday night but to scram in so many people into one small confined is fire hazard and caused the look of the place feels hectic and chaotic. 2/ employees are poorly trained and understaffed. I ordered Udon soup and never came with a spoon. I had to ask different staffs several time for a spoon. Until then, 7 minutes past, soup went cold. The employees don’t clean table after different courses, my table was stack with empty plates which normally would be acceptable but after too many, it is overwhelming. As for food, everything came out late. A normal dinner should be 90 minutes to 120 minutes. It took the chef 90 minutes for broiled abalone and baked lobster. 90 minutes came, we received our broiled abalone but not seen our lobster. We ask the staffs, four staffs, but no one gave a straight answer. We waited another 30 minutes, we learn that the restaurant ran out of lobster and trying to track down another location. This is 100% WRONG. I felt misled! I wish the staffs told us so that our time was not wasted. 3/ well, everything was poor because it took too long and I didn’t feel that chef place so much efforts into my dish. Every dish felt chefs rushed to send out of kitchen. For a restaurant of this caliber, it failed to deliver a half way descend meal.

ChIJQZmOvBovdTERQoUdgZkn-xw.name: places/ChIJQZmOvBovdTERQoUdgZkn-xw/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2twRmFYVnFPRFF0YzFack9XaDVhRVpKYkc5ZmVXYxAB
ChIJQZmOvBovdTERQoUdgZkn-xw.author: Allen Nguyen
ChIJQZmOvBovdTERQoUdgZkn-xw.text:
I rarely ever post my comments. This was my first Omakase experience in Vietnam after others in Japan and the states. We were a party of 3 trying the discounted $5M menu. Originally we opted for the Omakase K fish specialty menu but was substituted to Omakase Niku K meat specialty menu due to the other restaurant not ready for opening until December time.

The menu was well put together with emphasis on premium meat & fish dishes. Overall the portions were very good and a bit larger than past Omakase. The sauces were tasty but some on the saltier side if eating much. More tastes contrast between dishes would be well appreciated as some of the dishes include similar flavors/ingredients. Overall the dishes are good and quite filling at the end of the meal.

The services are very good. The staffs are very attentive and tries very hard to accommodate a good experience. My mom is 85 and my aunt 74 and the staffs went out of their way to assist and explain the dishes with patience. Minor misses exist although more perfection is appreciated such as clearing food bits…etc

The atmosphere is a big miss with much desire for  serious improvement. The place seats approximately 10. This night there were 3 groups of 2 couples and a 3 people group.
- First, the background music was a light jazz which sets up more like for a bar lounge atmosphere. I found the music distracting and too casual for the fine dining for traditional Omakase. - Second, the first group including a Viet lady and an American man talking business nonstop throughout the 1.5 hour meal with audible noise level. It was very disturbing and rude. The other Viet couple came to talk business as well, not to enjoy the Omakase. At one point one of them order a Coke and continue the conversation.
- I have twice asked the staffs to request the other couples to lower the volume but to no avail. The rude customers seem to feel entitled to their behaviors as they spend any money here.

I felt this is ghetto, quite uncultured and disrespectful to the chef and the dining experience at Omakase Niku K. I didn’t expect to pay for a fine experience and getting a clearly subpar one.

I ask the restaurant management to set clear rules for the customers
1)to keep conversation to very low volume or find a cafe elsewhere & take phone calls only outside 2) If the customer choose the seating they must order the menu. Management should not ever allow soda & Omakase clients in the same table.

The value of the Omakase depends on the traditional experience not the Vietnamese street style please. It may not be the fault of the restaurant of the customer behaviors but without firm rules you lower your standards and chase away quality customers. Not sure if I will return.

ChIJQZmOvBovdTERQoUdgZkn-xw.text: This is my first omasake experience in Vietnam and I'm glad I chose Niku by K. :) Atmosphere was very warm and welcoming. ChIJIUCP17MvdTERj3pwpsof5JQ.text:
Went for dinner for 3 ppl
My mom loves the truffles chawanmushi

Last time I went the uni was not fresh, made the feedback for the chef already, this time the oysters were not fresh (didn’t try uni this time, still have the fear of that not very fresh taste) , tried to ask staffs for lime to squeeze in, but it didn’t help and my brother had stomachache after that when we came home.

But, I will keep coming back and back to this place because, overall it still an outstanding sushibar in HoChiMinh with good sources of seafood and the chefs are also good, the first time I came Chef Trung was the most impressive one, not only his skill in cooking but also how he spiced the environment up in the counter area.

We had Khang as our main serving man, recommended good drinks, very helpful and gave my mom a bandage when her finger got cut by the oyster shells.

Amazing, keep improving!

ChIJpwNVRfgpdTERmSIgF0Fsnhs.text: This is Kiyota’s third branch. The sushi and sashimi maintain their high quality, and the addition of robatayaki elements makes it very unique. It’s worth a visit and reasonably priced.

ChIJpwNVRfgpdTERmSIgF0Fsnhs.name: places/ChIJpwNVRfgpdTERmSIgF0Fsnhs/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTUNJcnRHeThnRRAB
ChIJpwNVRfgpdTERmSIgF0Fsnhs.author: Sonie Megia
ChIJpwNVRfgpdTERmSIgF0Fsnhs.text:
Wow! What a unique and unforgettable experience! While I was dining I was already thinking about writing a review to praise this place.

My guest and I had a private dining room, from the moment we stepped inside, the friendly chef and staff created a welcoming and comfortable environment. Each dish was crafted with precision, from delicate, buttery sashimi to expertly grilled selections bursting with amazing flavor.

The presentation is stunning, emphasizing the freshness and quality of every ingredient. What sets this restaurant apart is the personal touch—the staffs engagement makes the meal feel truly special because they would let us know about the dish and recommended way to eat it.

I’ve dined at many places in Las Vegas, Texas, California, Hawaii, and Florida with prices ranging from a few hundred to a thousand dollars for a similar experience, and this restaurant easily belongs in the top-tier category. In my opinion, it even surpasses Nobu in terms of quality and taste with similar dishes. Whether you’re celebrating or simply exploring Japanese cuisine at its finest, this a great place to go!

A top-notch dining experience, I will be back again for sure!

ChIJpwNVRfgpdTERmSIgF0Fsnhs.name: places/ChIJpwNVRfgpdTERmSIgF0Fsnhs/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xORVdtVnJVRGw1VEVwNmRFSndTbmhYWkd4RWFsRRAB

ChIJpwNVRfgpdTERmSIgF0Fsnhs.text:
Great value of money.
While there are plenty of overpriced Japanese eatery’s out there, this place is just doing the right thing. Approximately 1.6mil to fill up a couple with sashimi, nigiri, some grills, a miso soup and drinks.
Great feeling sitting at the counter and you get to choose your own chopsticks.
