ChIJpwNVRfgpdTERmSIgF0Fsnhs.name: places/ChIJpwNVRfgpdTERmSIgF0Fsnhs/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTUNnbnBieldBEAE
ChIJpwNVRfgpdTERmSIgF0Fsnhs.author: Scott Nguyen
ChIJpwNVRfgpdTERmSIgF0Fsnhs.text:
Robata Kiyota delivers an exceptional omakase experience, combining top-quality ingredients with outstanding hospitality.

The chef and staff are incredibly warm, making guests feel welcome from the moment they arrive. Each dish is masterfully crafted, from fresh, melt-in-your-mouth sashimi to perfectly grilled selections.

The sushi is beautifully presented, highlighting the natural flavors of premium ingredients. What makes this place special is the personalized touch—the chef’s interaction adds depth to the dining experience.

Whether for a special occasion or a culinary indulgence, Robata Kiyota is a must-visit for lovers of authentic Japanese cuisine.

Highly recommended!

ChIJaxNSIwAndTERMUeNz4mcQpw.name: places/ChIJaxNSIwAndTERMUeNz4mcQpw/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2pFMGVrRjNaMDloVlRSdWVHOVdZMlJ3TTBkcFpGRRAB
ChIJaxNSIwAndTERMUeNz4mcQpw.author: Phi Huynh
ChIJaxNSIwAndTERMUeNz4mcQpw.text:
Rankai distinguishes itself through creative fusion presentations that delight both the eye and the palate:
• Seasonal Elegance: The dish featuring fresh Uni, Caviar, and a sliver of toast topped with glistening green grapes showed daring and mastery. The bright, acidic crunch of the grape provided a brilliant counterpoint to the richness of the seafood, showcasing intelligent omakase fusion at its best.
• Whisky & Wagyu Perfection: The plated Wagyu dish, served with a perfectly roasted eggplant and a jewel-like grape, demonstrated a sophisticated modern Japanese steakhouse approach, meant to be chased by the complex notes of the finest Japanese whisky you provided.
The Verdict: Rankai is more than a restaurant; it is a culinary tour de force. It blends the rigorous standards of traditional Edomae with a bold, international sense of luxury and flavor pairing. For those seeking a genuinely overwhelming, world-class dining experience defined by peerless sourcing and elite craft, Rankai is the ultimate destination

ChIJ7faHw2UndTERBLCPt8qzfxw.name: places/ChIJ7faHw2UndTERBLCPt8qzfxw/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT21sMmVrOXNibUpzVDFCRFJrOWxVMFpoY1dKSVVrRRAB
ChIJ7faHw2UndTERBLCPt8qzfxw.author: Anna Nguyen
ChIJ7faHw2UndTERBLCPt8qzfxw.text:
Passed by this area many times and never had a chance to explore and glad we finally did.

Food 1.8 🌟
10/10 Agedashi Tofu - Love the texture, the sauce soaks well, and makes everything flavorful, especially the veggies
7/10 Beef Gyoza - Yes to the meat and flavor. The extra slice of beef is tender with the spicy (not really) sesame dipping sauce is a great mix. Separately, the 2 pieces are good, just not the overall wow effect together.
10/10 Wagyu Beef Claypot - Love this dish, from the self-preparation dish to the flavor, add that pepper, you'll love the kick (not spicy, just a kick)
10/10 Grilled Hamachi - Now this was an experience. The torch show in the kitchen to the fishhead presentation on the table. Yes, this will test your chopstick skills. The scent, flavor, and texture, top-notch, maybe add a bit of salt & Jap spice if you like it stronger.
6/10 Pistachio Ice Cream - this one was a bit meh for the ending. The ice cream came out a bit too hard and stayed hard until the last bite. Yes to pistachio flavor but not my cup of tea overall after the first 2 courses.
10/10 Fruit plate - This was a better choice to end the meal. Great presentation, cleanse your palate, nice refreshing end touch. It was cleaned (by us) before I realized I needed a picture 🫣

Service 1.0 🌟 Attentive and friendly staff even when we came in for a late dinner

Price 1.0 🌟 700+ / 2-pax
Price matches the quality of food & service

Environment 1.0 🌟 Nice spot, nice vibe, for a full meal and a walk before leaving the area

Overall 4.8 🌟 Great Value for a full 3-Course meal for 2, thanks to DiningCity Restaurant Week. Will be back to try your lunches soon!

ChIJF6a9EiIvdTERh5jXhcbC4-Y.author: Genevieve Vox
ChIJF6a9EiIvdTERh5jXhcbC4-Y.text:
The place is usually packed, so it is a good idea to book a table beforehand or aim to get there right when they open at 5 PM. When it is busy, the smoke can get pretty annoying, so maybe it is best for parents to leave the kids at home.

Some people complain about the service, but I have always had a good experience. The staff are friendly and efficient, and they are quick to bring out dishes and take care of any extra requests. The owner might seem a bit strict, but she is clearly on top of things. She is always keeping an eye on everything and making sure everyone is happy.

The menu is not huge, but the food is really good and reasonably priced at around VND 100.000. One thing to note is that the marinade is quite bland. The fermented bean curd is served as is, quite salty, not pre-processed (not mixed with other ingredients such as garlic, chilli, sugar) so I had to ask for some sugar and kumquat. There are other dipping sauces like fermented fish sauce, chilli sauce, and pepper salt, feel free to ask for them. The rice noodles, rice paper, and veggies are extra and cost about VND 15.000 per plate.

The only real downside is the parking. Even if you park your motorbike right outside the place, you will still have to pay a VND 5.000 parking fee.

ChIJxQUjKtsudTERO_KVgjmipAk.author: Bredgy L.
ChIJxQUjKtsudTERO_KVgjmipAk.text: I almost thought I was walking through a theme park, as I marvelled at the endless sight of tables, full of joyful people and colourful plates of food. It's a common theme at Vietnamese-style BBQ for me to go crazy over any of the whole fish. Brushed with a generous amount of oil and fermented soy beans and grilled to a meaty but tender texture, what was left was only the bones. The soft grilled eel brought the smoky aroma I expected, along with a fragrant lemongrass chilli mince on top. Acting like a sponge, it allows for the fried tofu to soak up the slightly sweet, scallion oil-infused fish sauce pooling on the bottom, with a scattering of fried pork fat on top for increased indulgence. The deep-fried soft shell crab is also battered into a sponge, soaking up tons of flavour and oil, with a subtle sweet crab aroma. Finally, a sweet and healthy fruit plate is the best ending to a large meal.

ChIJxQUjKtsudTERO_KVgjmipAk.author: Ching San Lim
ChIJxQUjKtsudTERO_KVgjmipAk.text:
If you’re looking for an unforgettable grilled meat feast in an authentic, no-frills setting, **Làng Nướng Nam Bộ** is an absolute must-visit. This place left such an impression on our group that we ended up having **both our dinners here** during our **3D2N boys’ golf trip**—because why fix what isn’t broken when the food is this good?

### **The Star of the Show: Roasted Pig with Crispy Skin**
The **whole roasted pig** was a masterpiece—**crackling crispy skin** that shattered with every bite, revealing **juicy, flavorful meat** underneath. The perfect balance of fat and lean made each piece irresistible, especially when paired with their tangy, herbaceous dipping sauce. Hands down, one of the best roasted pigs we’ve ever had.

### **Awesome Roasted Pigeons – Small but Mighty**
Don’t let their size fool you—these **roasted pigeons** were packed with insane flavor. The skin was **glazed and slightly smoky**, while the meat remained **tender and rich**, almost gamey in the best way possible. A must-order for anyone who loves bold, savory bites.

### **Live Sturgeon Two Ways – Grilled & in Soup**
The **live sturgeon** was another highlight, prepared **two ways**:
- **Grilled sturgeon**: Firm, meaty, and smoky, with a beautiful char that enhanced its natural sweetness.
- **Sturgeon hotpot (soup)**: A light yet deeply umami broth, with silky sturgeon slices and fresh herbs—perfect for balancing out the heavier grilled dishes.

### **Local Vibes, Zero Tourist Traps**
What made the experience even better? The crowd was **almost entirely locals**—always a good sign. No gimmicks, no inflated prices, just **honest, incredible food** that keeps people coming back. The lively atmosphere, paired with cold beers, made it the ideal spot for our post-golf feasts.

### **Final Verdict: 10/10, Will Return**
Làng Nướng Nam Bộ isn’t just a restaurant—it’s a **culinary experience**. From the **crispy roasted pig** to the **succulent pigeons** and the **two-way sturgeon**, every dish was a winner. If you’re in Vietnam and want **real, unfiltered flavor**, this is the place. We’ll definitely be back on our next trip!

ChIJ4axTm0gvdTERaUD-tFK3jVM.author: Sven
ChIJ4axTm0gvdTERaUD-tFK3jVM.text:
Worst meat I have ever eaten, first time I stopped eating buffet without being full. I feel that their concept is to make you stop eating from the buffet because of the bad taste, not because you are full.

Because of the bad meat 1 star.

Food - Neko Buffet 349K:

We tried a broad range of beef, pork and chicken.

Some of the beef was very hard to chew, some had so much tendon inside that I almost had to vomit because it got stuck. Other parts had barely any taste and I felt like I was chewing paper.
We tried all cuts, none was even remotely tasty.

The pork was not as bad as the beef, but also had barely any taste.

The chicken was the best as it was easy to eat and had some taste. Still definitely not worth the price tag.

The chawanmushi was nothing special.

The takoyaki were the best dish we had. However you can get better takoyaki anywhere else cheap. This shows how bad the meat is, considering it is a BBQ restaurant.

I tried over 5 different BBQ buffets in Vietnam, this was by far the worst.

Dessert buffet claims to have 20+ toppings, as seen on the pictures the options are far below that. Also I can‘t find any of the desserts on the pictures. The ice cream had no vanilla taste at all. The yogurt tasted horrible.

Some drink options in the drink buffet: (milk) tea with toppings, detox water, pepsi, mirinda, 7up (self-service)

Service:

Service was attentive and changed the plate even without asking.

Atmosphere:

It felt like a warehouse (not in a good way), some walls had no decorations at all. Some walls have at least some Japanese letters. It was very hot inside although it was empty.

ChIJZ7nKTwApdTERT_MLcjxPbyc.name: places/ChIJZ7nKTwApdTERT_MLcjxPbyc/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2s1c1oxWkhhbk5yTnpSRE4wOU5PRVpmVDBKalQzYxAB
ChIJZ7nKTwApdTERT_MLcjxPbyc.author: David Mack
ChIJZ7nKTwApdTERT_MLcjxPbyc.text:
I arrived to OM - Authentic Vietnamese Grill at 7:54 p.m on a Thursday, and the place was packed! I had been advised by a local friend to visit this location. I arrived and walked to the host stand where three employees were standing. Knowing ahead of time they may be too busy and should make a reservation, I asked if seating was available, and a young lady kindly asked me to have a seat and give her five minutes. She even offered me a flavored beverage while I waited. Just three minutes later, she invited me to follow her to my table.

As I walked behind her, I looked around—the restaurant was full, with great, recognizable music playing in the background. The establishment has an open-front layout with a covered roof, balanced lighting, which gives it a unique and inviting atmosphere. I loved the design!

I was seated at a great table with a nice view of the locals enjoying themselves. I noticed all staff members working seamlessly as a team, moving with purpose and care to ensure excellent service.

Tuyền was assigned to my table, and she had the perfect personality—professional, kind, and attentive. She presented the menu and pointed out the beverage options, which consisted mostly of beer and some chilled flavored wines. I chose a wine and a bottle of water.

(Important note: No full bar here.)

Tuyền brought the water and wine quickly, along with a mixed salad that they place on all tables, accompanied by different sauces. You can see the photo of my meal. The wine had an unexpected kick that I really enjoyed! I poured it over ice, and one was definitely enough—it was refreshing and flavorful.

She gave me space to review the menu “book,” which includes clear, detailed photos—something I appreciate as an American guest. I decided on the beef, sautéed corn, and fried rice mixed with pork and seafood. I added the rice because the entrée plates are small and, frankly, I was feeling a bit greedy.

Within ten minutes, all my dishes arrived. Tuyền explained which sauces paired best with each item and how to use them—excellent service mentality! The food was delicious and flavorful. Surprisingly, the chilled bottle of wine I ordered ended up being the highlight of my meal. It tasted like a fruity wine cooler with a stronger kick, served in a short, unique corked bottle.

When I was finished, I signaled to Tuyền that I was ready to wrap up my meal. The entire experience—from the fantastic staff to the happy crowd—was wonderful. While Tuyền was getting my bill a manager came over to ask if the food and service was ok. You can see the receipt attached; the meal was well worth the cost, including the 200,000 VND tip I gave Tuyền for her excellent service.

In conclusion, this spot is a gem.
If you travel to Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, make sure to visit—and ask to sit in Tuyền’s section!

Because I did not know that, the staff served a lot of food at first and for the rest, 1 skewer at a time, which made me feel a bit embarrassed. ChIJuwxW2cYvdTERPTCO8zmg740.text:

The food comes out quickly, the menu is diverse and sold by the gram so it is easy to order.
Each dish has vegetables to go with it, grilled dishes have grilled okra, steamed dishes have alcohol stoves at the table so the dishes are always hot.

ChIJn1j7VCsndTEROFm7rEgSCZE.name: places/ChIJn1j7VCsndTEROFm7rEgSCZE/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25CU2RsTndXR05GY1VOT1lraENUbGQ0Y0c1aFprRRAB
ChIJn1j7VCsndTEROFm7rEgSCZE.author: Min Min
ChIJn1j7VCsndTEROFm7rEgSCZE.text:
If you are a fan of grilled dishes, especially lamb, Nhat Thuy Phong Grilled Lamb Leg is definitely a place worth trying.

⸻

🌿 Space

The restaurant has an outdoor space, so it can be a bit hot at noon, but in return it is quite airy and feels like eating grilled food in a very natural "street" style. Tables and chairs are arranged spaciously, suitable for groups of friends or family.

⸻

👨‍🍳 Service & style

The staff here are very cute, enthusiastic and cheerful, true to the Southern style: friendly, welcoming and always willing to support customers.

⸻

🍖 Food

The restaurant's special highlight is the whole grilled lamb leg, skewered in a 1.5 kg block and grilled directly on hot coals. The lamb is well marinated, the outside is golden brown, the inside is still soft and juicy. When eating, the restaurant serves vegetables, so it doesn't feel greasy like when eating lamb in Beijing. 

After grilling the whole leg, the staff will cut the meat into small pieces and skewer it for customers to continue grilling on the table, while eating and enjoying the aroma of the meat and charcoal. The flavor is rich, the meat is not smelly, the skin is slightly crispy, dipped with lemon pepper salt or spicy chili sauce, very delicious. 

A 1.5 kg leg of lamb is a relatively large portion - if there are four people, you have to "eat a lot" to finish it, because the meat is quite a lot and firm. 

⸻

💬 Summary

Nhat Thuy Phong is a unique barbecue restaurant, bringing a new and fun experience. Although the outdoor space is a bit hot, the fragrant aroma of grilled lamb, enthusiastic staff and friendly service make the meal complete.

ChIJ-zadCJ4vdTERZY62mpg7ov0.author: onevay (onevay)
ChIJ-zadCJ4vdTERZY62mpg7ov0.text:
We visited this place based on a local Vietnamese friend’s recommendation, and it turned out to be quite close to our hotel. The food quality was impressive — fresh ingredients, well-grilled pork, and flavorful dipping sauces. The signature nem nướng (grilled pork sausage) was tasty, and the combo set came with a wide variety of toppings, veggies, and crispy spring rolls. The soft rice paper wrap made it a fun, interactive meal.

However, as foreign visitors unfamiliar with this style of dining, we found it a bit difficult at first. There were no English explanations available, and the staff seemed unsure how to assist us in the beginning. Once our Vietnamese friend arrived, the communication improved, and the staff became more attentive and welcoming.

The restaurant itself is small, clean, and has a relaxed, local vibe. It’s a good place for a quick and authentic Vietnamese meal, especially if you come with someone who knows the food.

ChIJiy9J3xQvdTERRV9CXNqVCvw.text:
The eatery makes the most of the pavement, setting up two tables outside. It is a lovely spot to sit and eat on cooler days, but things can get a bit toasty when the sun’s out. Plus, the grill right outside means you might end up smelling a bit smoky after your meal.

Nonetheless, the food here is absolutely delicious. The spring rolls and meat are packed with flavour, and the prices are very reasonable.

What is really cool is that you can either have your noodles in a bowl, or you can get creative and roll your own spring rolls with rice paper. If you are feeling lazy, they will happily roll them for you (order pre-rolled ones).

Just a heads up: the eatery is closed on the 1st and 15th of the lunar month. If either of those days falls on a Sunday, they will stay open on Sunday and close on the following Monday.

ChIJocOmccovdTER8APaRJZ94bg.text:
When it comes to Japanese food in this area, it’s hard to go wrong, and NIKUTARO is no exception. It’s a decent Japanese BBQ restaurant that serves up fresh, quality meat at a fair price.
The beef tongue was a highlight — tender, flavorful, and grilled perfectly. The meat platter was also good and reasonably priced, offering a nice variety to share. The only part I didn’t enjoy much was the chicken skin, which was too tough for my liking.
We also tried the cold noodles, which were refreshing and not bad at all, making for a nice balance to the heavier grilled meats.
One thing to note: if you’d like the staff to do the grilling for you, they’ll add an extra 5% charge to your total bill.
Overall, NIKUTARO is a solid choice if you’re in the mood for Japanese BBQ — fresh meat, fair pricing, and a reliable experience.

ChIJm05ZtmkvdTERVZ9iJRO40Z8.text:
Let me tell you about this hidden gem I found in Ho Chi Minh City called Quán Nướng Chị Hai. It's not fancy by any means, but that's exactly what makes it charming. It's a local spot, tucked away on a side street, and you can tell by the way everyone seems to know each other.

I ventured in because I was craving some grilled goodness, and let me tell you, they did not disappoint! I ordered the đậu hũ trứng non (beancurd with egg and preserved egg) - it was massive! Like, the size of a takeout container!  The texture was perfect, soft and creamy from the tofu and eggs, with a savory kick from the preserved egg. And the dipping sauce? Don't even get me started. It was this sweet and spicy concoction that took everything to a whole new level.

Now, I have to be honest, the grilled vú heo (pork udder) wasn't quite my thing. The meat itself was a bit tough, but the chao (fermented soybean paste) they served with it was surprisingly delicious. Really rich and flavorful, but definitely on the salty side.

Overall, Quán Nướng Chị Hai is a fantastic spot for a casual and authentic Vietnamese BBQ experience. The atmosphere is friendly and welcoming, the portions are huge, and the prices are incredibly reasonable. Just maybe skip the pork udder unless you're feeling adventurous!

ChIJ-VjzGgApdTERBk0lacmVlGA.author: Hải Phùng
ChIJ-VjzGgApdTERBk0lacmVlGA.text:
Megumi Japanese BBQ Rice Restaurant is a familiar destination for many diners in Tan Binh who want to enjoy Japanese cuisine in a cozy and friendly space. The restaurant is located on Hoang Ke Viem Street, the location is quite easy to find, the space is not too large but is neatly decorated, clean and has the typical minimalist style of Japanese style. 

The most popular dish here is BBQ Rice. The meat is carefully selected, marinated to taste, grilled to perfection to retain its softness, natural sweetness and attractive aroma. Hot sticky rice, served with vegetables, kimchi, miso soup and rich sauce creates a balance of flavors, making the meal complete and not greasy. In addition, the menu also has many other familiar Japanese dishes such as udon, donburi, katsu ..., suitable for both single guests or groups of friends and family. 

Another plus point is the reasonable price, compared to the quality of the food, it is quite pleasant, affordable for many customers. The staff is friendly, quick, and always ready to help customers have a comfortable experience. 

👉 Overall, Megumi is a place worth trying if you want to find a delicious, authentic Japanese restaurant with reasonable prices right in the heart of Tan Binh.

But was in the area, so I gave it a go.
Tried the Kimchi and meat soup for đ190.
At first, I thought it a bit on the higher side. BUT.. then the freebies arrived !! That felt like a meal on its own before I even gor my soup. Value for Money... it's actually really good !!!
Staff are friendly and attentive.
The meal was delicious.. as good as I had in Seoul.
Toilets are super clean.. and the mouth wash was just a brilliant touch !
I was even offered a free coffee, but I was just too full..
Great place visit on your own.. or would be mind blowingly awesome with a group.

My favorites in order from favorite to least favorite is:

- Matchandeul BBQ
- BBQ Plan-K
- Bros BBQ

Matchandeul BBQ easily has the best sides out of all 3 places. Their Kim Chi salad is delicious. They also have private rooms here that you can reserve to have a less noisy experience while you eat with your family or friends.

I will say it is a very busy and often crowded place so I would recommend that you make reservations in advance before you come here.

I went to the restaurant to buy take-out because I thought it would be cheaper, but in fact, the app code also gave me a pretty good discount, only a few thousand dong difference. When I go to the restaurant to buy take-out, I can choose more dishes from the menu; but waiting for a long time in a busy, complicated atmosphere like this is tiring. 

I don't think the food is very special, but the rate on the app and Google Maps is very high. The chicken skin is soft, the chicken meat is loose, the seasoning is not unique. I tried cheese chicken and fish sauce chicken, but I couldn't feel the difference between the two chickens. 

Just a one-time experience, I'll probably go back to the familiar restaurant on Le Van Tho street.

ChIJVcLxJQAvdTERxtO-R3pQFFs.text: I ordered a portion of broken rice with ribs, pork skin, sausage, and fried egg for 47k. Overall, the food was average and not delicious. The rice was dry, the pork skin had no taste, the ribs were marinated normally, and the sausage was nothing special. The restaurant had few tables on the sidewalk, the utensils were not clean, and there was only a place to park motorbikes in the alley, but parking space was very limited.

The first time I went to eat and felt discriminated against. Too bad!!!!!

ChIJVcLxJQAvdTERxtO-R3pQFFs.name: places/ChIJVcLxJQAvdTERxtO-R3pQFFs/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNMNUpmMnpRRRAB

ChIJVcLxJQAvdTERxtO-R3pQFFs.text:
Popular broken rice sold in the evening.

- The rice grains are just small, not really broken, cooked fluffy, with a few lumps.

- The ribs are delicious but the ribs are thin at this price.

- The sausage is well-made, not dry.

- The fat is crispy, but a bit salty, if it's bland it will be more delicious.

- The fish sauce is diluted, with enough salt and sweetness.

The price is very affordable when the owner starts from 25k. Free iced tea. The only annoying thing is that the sisters in the same house sell broken rice but sometimes they talk too loudly.

ChIJVcLxJQAvdTERxtO-R3pQFFs.text: Everything was just okay, the rice was not fluffy, it was lumpy so it was not delicious, the ground chili smelled like old chili, the pork ribs and ham cost 42k, just tried it but not good enough to come back.

The best broken rice restaurant in District 7.
The owner is enthusiastic and cheerful, the price is also affordable, so it is always crowded. The rice is scooped up based on the feeling that it is too big, and there is free pork fat 👍
The grilled ribs are soft, marinated with a light scent of mai que lo. The eggs are just fried when ordered, so people tend to order egg ribs rather than pork skin ribs and sausage.

The coffee is good, you should try it.
The broken rice is quite good, just after crossing the ferry, you can eat it and continue. Not excellent but acceptable.
The restaurant is a bit dirty and the grilled meat has a lot of burnt edges but the owner doesn't cut it.

ChIJ96W6FCMvdTERpheV7i8RGy0.text: My wife and I came here for our first meal of our 4-day vacation and everything was great. The food is fresh and flavorful and the service and staff were great. ChIJ96W6FCMvdTERpheV7i8RGy0.name: places/ChIJ96W6FCMvdTERpheV7i8RGy0/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNwajRXSnFBRRAB

ChIJ96W6FCMvdTERpheV7i8RGy0.text:
noodles were simple and on its own did not really have any taste, but i wouldn’t have it any other way because it was a perfect complement to the perfectly grilled meat and the meat spring roll looking thing. Everything went well together and I only regret not being able to stuff more of this lovely dish into my belly. the ice lemon tea is also not the usual taste you get but really good!!

this stall is a good symbol of street food, because you are literally on the street with a small table and toddler chairs (I’m 6”2 but I was still happy), i read another review about red ants in the area but i didn’t encounter that.

MUST TRY! Highly recommend if you are in district 1!

ChIJ96W6FCMvdTERpheV7i8RGy0.text:
Best dishes we had in Saigon! Run by family, nothing fancy but simple food made very well with kind service and warm smile. We had one dish with grilled pork chops and other dish with pork chops, pork skins and meat pie. Nouc Sam sauce and cooked chives are really good with the dish! They even included iced tea before the meal and fresh banana after!

We came at around 10am and they were consistently busy with local people doing takeaways. We walked 20mins and it was worth visiting!

[8:30 06/29/2025 • HCMC]
Passed by many times, saw the restaurant was crowded so today stopped by to try it

The ribs are to the baby's family's taste, the skin is delicious. The baby doesn't like spring rolls, so the taste is normal 😅 in summary, it's okay

The restaurant looks clean and tidy.
Worth experiencing, everyone
#FoodTourByAnhAnh 😋

ChIJ76mvTywvdTER1kJYbhHPOgU.text: Roadside restaurant, true to quality: delicious - cheap - self-service. Free iced tea. At noon, you should come a little early because when there are many customers, the service will take a bit longer. Rice prices range from 35-50k depending on the dish. The broken rice is delicious, the ribs and sausage are a bit greasy (healthy team will not like this, hehe). In general, it is a cheap rice, reasonable price in District 3 area.

ChIJtTbOOcYodTERzMnxzsJNht4.name: places/ChIJtTbOOcYodTERzMnxzsJNht4/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2t4aFltVm9jbEUzWW1GdFFrZ3ROa3hVZUhGWkxVRRAB
ChIJtTbOOcYodTERzMnxzsJNht4.author: Hiep Nguyen
ChIJtTbOOcYodTERzMnxzsJNht4.text:
Cơm Tấm Huyền is a true hidden gem in a small alley, packed with locals every night. The broken rice is flavorful, served with crispy shredded pork skin, fried egg, grilled meat, and pickled vegetables. The side dish of braised pork with bitter melon is tasty and well-seasoned. Portions are generous for the price, making it excellent value.

Despite being a street-side eatery with small plastic tables and chairs, the atmosphere is lively and authentic. The owner is friendly and quick, even when the place gets crowded. A great spot to experience real Vietnamese cơm tấm in a local neighborhood setting.

ChIJ2wwqQqopdTERoGZcVJ872vo.author: James Hunt
ChIJ2wwqQqopdTERoGZcVJ872vo.text:
I have no idea why people complain about this restaurant. I've been here a couple of times, and will continue to do so. It's legitimately some of the (if not THE) best cơm tấm I have had in Saigon, and I eat a LOT of cơm tấm. The price point is better than other places, the food is better than other places, and the people are nice to me. Not only that, but they give food to the needy! They had a cart set up outside with vegetarian food for those who need it!

I will continue to go to this restaurant, and I hope they're successful, and these reviews cannot be legit.

ChIJ1-eCD1fYdDERUvYgqOIyp7M.text:
One of the familiar broken rice restaurants of Di An people. The space of the townhouse on the front of a crowded street makes it a bit stuffy at noon and afternoon. The food cabinet looks clean. Only sells broken rice. 

Broken rice with loose grains, ribs with ribs, and chicken, grilled continuously so the meat is fresh. The plate of rice with ribs and eggs is served with a bit of skin, the ribs are marinated fragrantly, rich in aroma; the skin is also fragrant with rice powder; the soft-boiled egg flows out to cover the rice and makes it rich to eat. The fish sauce has the right amount of sweetness, delicious. 

The service is fast and enthusiastic. There is convenient bank transfer payment. The price is affordable, the portion is a bit small, even those who eat a lot will not be full.

ChIJZ0rJv_IvdTERjTf_T23zAEY.text:
"Cơm gà 2 chị em" is a popular dish in Vietnam, consisting of steamed rice and chicken cooked in a special sauce. In this review, I will share my experience of trying this dish and give my personal opinion.

I recently had the opportunity to try "Cơm gà 2 chị em" at a local restaurant, and I must say that I was impressed. The dish came with a generous serving of rice, which was perfectly cooked and had just the right amount of moisture. The chicken was tender and flavorful, and the sauce was simply delicious. It was a combination of sweet and savory flavors that complemented the rice and chicken perfectly.

One thing that stood out to me about this dish was its simplicity. It wasn't overloaded with too many ingredients or spices, but it still managed to pack a lot of flavor. This made it a great option for a quick and satisfying meal.

Overall, I would highly recommend "Cơm gà 2 chị em" to anyone who enjoys simple yet delicious meals. It's definitely worth a try if you're in the mood for some comfort food.

ChIJYwohlSUvdTERbJfDx4-b6ug.author: yumz
ChIJYwohlSUvdTERbJfDx4-b6ug.text:
su su waterfall fried chicken is bringing the crispy goodness

THE ORIGIN STORY
this spot started as a local secret and grew into a legit phenomenon, all built around their one-of-a-kind frying technique that's pure genius.

THE STAR OF THE SHOW
the fried chicken is an absolute serve - perfectly seasoned, incredibly tender and juicy inside with that iconic crispy skin. it's the kind of chicken that hits different.

THE WATERFALL METHOD
they fry their chicken using a unique dripping technique where hot oil cascades over the meat like a literal waterfall. this creates the most insanely crispy yet non-greasy crust you'll ever experience.

THE STAFF SITUATION
the team here stays super helpful and friendly, guiding you through the menu and making sure your experience is straight fire from start to finish.

THE PRO TIP
they often run out of thigh meat, so if you want the premium cuts you better get there early. the early bird gets the thigh, as they say.

THE VIBE
this no-frills spot keeps it 100 with plastic stools and focused chicken craftsmanship. the constant sizzle and aroma will have your stomach screaming yes.

don't forget to ❤️.

ChIJYwohlSUvdTERbJfDx4-b6ug.text: Took a Grab out here and was dropped off (did not know it at the time but the drop off was across the street to the tiny alley - between the green Bach Hoa Xanh supermarket and a Juice Me) we needed to go down!). It wasn't easy to find but got there and was glad we did. The fried chicken was amazing and you would do yourself a favour if you tried it. The thigh+drumstick 'piece' is not large (you should get an extra piece as an additional menu item - either breast+wing or thigh+drumstick) but it was juicy and flavoursome. There's not much else on the menu, apart from drinks and seaweed soup, but that's always a good sign for me.

ChIJYwohlSUvdTERbJfDx4-b6ug.text:
ORDERED:
🍚 Cơm gà đùi: Tam Hoang Chicken thigh with rice (55,000 ₫  / $3.19 aud)
🍵 Trà đá: Iced tea (2,000 ₫ / $0.12 aud)

REVIEW:
💛 Delicious chicken. The meat is moist, the skin is paper thin and crispy, the rice fragrant. Slices of tomato, cucumber and laksa leave/ rau ram.
It's everything I would want in a fried chicken & tomato rice dish.
🫙 Sauces on the side include a home made sauce/ restaurant special which is heavier in flavour, or my personal favourite - sweet chilli sauce.

Overall, the service is friendly and full of banter. It's a casual place with great food. I would recommend!

ChIJ5SzduzIvdTERrTznKHgNxPM.name: places/ChIJ5SzduzIvdTERrTznKHgNxPM/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUM1b3RfMWZBEAE
ChIJ5SzduzIvdTERrTznKHgNxPM.author: Reardon
ChIJ5SzduzIvdTERrTznKHgNxPM.text:
Walked past here a few times and thought it looked like a cool restaurant. I really wanted to go here for dining upstairs on the balcony as i always see people up there. When I went near 4pm, the restaurant was empty and the staff said it wasn’t possible to sit upstairs. Bummer!

No AC, which is ok for me. I ordered the Hoi an chicken rice which was tasty but to be honest, they could have reheated it because it arrived almost cold. And after just a few minutes with the fan blowing on me, it was cold. At least the broth was warm. The other bowl was a bit unexpected for me but I tried the meat in it. Good flavor but not for me. Overall, the price is good and the staff are friendly, but they should really serve the food hot and fresh, reheating it is better than not.

Give it a go and hopefully you can sit on the balcony.

ChIJvSFVkvovdTER2Lx5evhENto.author: Tri Tran
ChIJvSFVkvovdTER2Lx5evhENto.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
One of the best Hainanese chicken rice spots in Saigon!
I’ve visited “Com Ga Hai Nam (Singapore Style)” on Calmette Street a few times, and it never disappoints. The chicken is perfectly poached – tender, juicy, and flavorful with smooth skin. The rice, cooked in chicken broth, is aromatic, fluffy, and rich – just like how it’s made in Singapore.
The dipping sauces are a big plus: soy sauce, ginger, and chili – all well-balanced and enhance the dish perfectly. The restaurant is clean, service is quick, and the staff are friendly. Although the space isn’t too big, it’s tidy and well-organized.
Prices are very reasonable, ranging from 40,000 to 60,000 VND – a great deal for such quality. They also offer catering and delivery services, which is super convenient for office workers nearby.
Located near Ben Thanh Market, it’s easy to find and perfect for both locals and tourists.
I’ll definitely come back again and recommend it to friends. If you’re a fan of Hainanese chicken rice, this spot is a must-try in Ho Chi Minh City!

ChIJvSFVkvovdTER2Lx5evhENto.text: Definitely can feel the Singapore hawker vibes when approaching this joint. Even the cooks give off an aura. Smooth, silky poached chicken. I wasn't sure what to get so I got the triple meat combo for 90k which had crispy pork belly, char SIU and poached chicken.  Came with 2 dipping sauces and hainan rice and come cucumbers and green onions. A little smaller on the food scale but I'm a thicc boiii from the states so I got a chicken to go since I didn't want to occupy more space 😂

ChIJ15BkBUkvdTERshQIDU8zlQs.author: Phương Khanh
ChIJ15BkBUkvdTERshQIDU8zlQs.text: I love eating at Cơm Gà Xối Mỡ Thanh in District 5. The crispy chicken skin is perfectly fried, juicy inside. The rice is fragrant and flavorful. The side soup is tasty and refreshing. Service is quick and friendly. Highly recommend!

ChIJ15BkBUkvdTERshQIDU8zlQs.name: places/ChIJ15BkBUkvdTERshQIDU8zlQs/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURYaHEtNXN3RRAB
ChIJ15BkBUkvdTERshQIDU8zlQs.author: Khôi D. Nguyễn (Tommy)
ChIJ15BkBUkvdTERshQIDU8zlQs.text:
One of the best dishes I have ever the honor to lay my hands on, no cap! The seating is either indoor or outdoor along the alleyway, which leaves a lot of room for improvement. Other than that, the menu is packed with Chinese Vietnamese dishes and the taste is impeccable to say the least. Personally, this is one of the OG eateries of the Chinatown area in Saigon, where the menu has remained the same after more than 30 years. The sauces and condiments are home recipes and basically free flowing, so there is absolutely no need to ask for more. All in all, a very satisfying experience for me and my lady.
P.S: It can get VERY crowded even before dinner time, so make sure to snatch a spot before long.

ChIJfUC-OfQ7dTEREQ69rOHWW6A.text:
**An Ky Fried Chicken Rice** at **183 Nguyen Van Tao, Hamlet 2, Nha Be, Ho Chi Minh City** is an ideal destination for those who love delicious, rich fried chicken rice. The chicken here is carefully prepared, with crispy skin, soft and sweet meat, and well-seasoned. The dish is fried in hot fat, with an attractive aroma, served with sticky white rice and some fresh vegetables to balance the taste. 

The restaurant has an airy space, quick service, and friendly staff. The price is very reasonable, consistent with the quality. If you are looking for a delicious chicken rice address in Nha Be, **An Ky** is a choice worth considering! 

⭐ **Rating:** 4.5/5 – Must try!

ChIJ9ZIpefgudTER7wG4inULlyY.author: Q N
ChIJ9ZIpefgudTER7wG4inULlyY.text:
This restaurant is amazing. If you’re ever in this area I’d recommend this place for lunch or dinner!

Parking is right across from the restaurant and is quite spacious.

Service is EXCELLENT!!! The waiter/waitresses are friendly and very quick with taking your order. The best part, your food arrives quickly and hot! I 100% suggest trying the garlic fried chicken. It has an incredible flavor, changing from sweet and salty, to extreme mouth watering savory. If you’re a fan of fried chicken, you’ll LOVE this place!

There are also plenty of other selections on the menu, but the chicken is the star of the show here.

ChIJ9ZIpefgudTER7wG4inULlyY.author: Allan Kamen
ChIJ9ZIpefgudTER7wG4inULlyY.text:
Been coming to this chicken place regularly since 2014. Food is basically crispy chicken and rice and it is inexpensive. There are four houses with seating areas for this place, all adjacent or on the other side of the road.

Don't expect anything fancy or extremely hygeinic but if you are in the area and have a strong stomach, you will probably enjoy it. The food is Ok, you won't get sick...  Don't worry.

I've never met another foreigner at the place in all the times I have gone, basically a few times a month.

The staff treats me and my guests well. Noone speaks English but it is easy enough to point at the pictures on the wall or other people's plates. They have a few dishes on offer but majority of people take the crispy chicken.

Best to come in the evening after dark when it gets cooler outside.

10% discount for group of 4. We were very happy with the dish the price and their service.

ChIJn7Oh56MvdTERXT2m5lSOnDw.author: Nam-Phuong Nguyen
ChIJn7Oh56MvdTERXT2m5lSOnDw.text:
To me and my family, this shop does the basics of Chinese cuisine very well.

The chicken, charsiu pork and stir fried spinach are all tender; so if you’re a fan of chewy meat or crunchy veggies, this might not suit your style.

I did not get to try the soy sauce steamed yellowtail catfish (basa in Vietnamese), as my 2-year-old son devoured the whole plate in minutes.

As Saigon locals, my family has been enjoying a variety of Chinese chicken rice since the 90s and I don’t recall other chicken rice shops having larger portions. We have no issue with the portion because this is what it has always been like.

The price is on the higher side but to be honest, this is to be expected. That’s just how the average price point is in Phu My Hung - a newer residential area for the more affluent population of the city.

The 1st floor has a nice nostalgic writing on the wall as a bonus for your check-in photos 🥰

So this might not be the right spot for a casual meal but I feel it is the perfect spot for a warm, familar, solid quality family meal.

ChIJ34fvR20vdTERZ9UYnAKs-pw.author: Jessie Lan Pham
ChIJ34fvR20vdTERZ9UYnAKs-pw.text:
There are many Singapore chicken rice restaurants in Saigon these days, but Twelve was one of the pioneers. Having lived in Singapore for seven years, I can say that the chicken rice here has been slightly adapted to suit local tastes. For example, in Singapore the chicken is typically very soft, but in Vietnam that texture is often seen as less tasty or less fresh. Twelve seems to strike a thoughtful balance, appealing to Vietnamese preferences while still preserving the essence of authentic Singapore chicken rice. I think they have achieved that quite well.

The portion was better presented than I expected, and to my surprise, I was even offered a complimentary freshly made soya milk (not the store-bought kind) along with what seemed to be a bottle of detergent. I enjoyed both the roasted and the boiled chicken, but for me the highlight was definitely the fragrant rice cooked in chicken stock.

ChIJa5GzQNQtdTERrWatRbmXz5Y.text: This restaurant has been in business for many years. It specializes in selling chicken rice and beef rice. I ordered stir-fried beef rice for 38k. The beef was freshly made when ordered, cut into dice, not sliced. The stir-fried beef was made with butter, so it was very fragrant, soft, and delicious. The soy sauce had ginger mixed in, which was a bit unusual. The service was fast and polite. Overall, I found it delicious and worth the money.

ChIJgxLJGAAvdTERel0IUmOuDYU.text:

Their Roast Duck is a bit of a let down though as compared to other places that offer the same item for the same or even lower price.

While the service crews are respectful, we were shocked that they insisted that the Blueberry Smoothie they gave us is the Kumquat we ordered. Aside from the look and the taste, it is really obvious that they got our order wrong due to the initial reaction of the waitress. Their response changed afterwards and insisted that the blue smoothie on our table is a kumquat smoothie. We opted not to spoil our lunch and not make it a big issue then but we will inform others of this unacceptable behavior.

ChIJ6-tqRVwvdTER8gKcBqu-XUQ.name: places/ChIJ6-tqRVwvdTER8gKcBqu-XUQ/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURyX2ViOHR3RRAB
ChIJ6-tqRVwvdTER8gKcBqu-XUQ.author: C
ChIJ6-tqRVwvdTER8gKcBqu-XUQ.text:
Con Gà Mái - Cơm Gà Phú Yên is a popular Vietnamese restaurant nestled in District 1 of Ho Chi Minh City, offering a delightful culinary experience. The restaurant boasts a fairly spacious setting with a bright, colorful ambiance, creating an inviting atmosphere for diners.

The menu showcases a nice range of Vietnamese dishes, with a particular emphasis on their signature Phú Yên chicken rice. One standout dish is the shredded chicken rice with gizzard, priced reasonably at VND60,000, which offers a satisfying blend of flavors and textures.

While the restaurant provides a comfortable dining environment, it's worth noting that the space is non-air conditioned, which may affect comfort levels during warmer days. Additionally, English-speaking visitors should be aware that the staff primarily communicate in Vietnamese.

Despite these minor considerations, Con Gà Mái - Cơm Gà Phú Yên has garnered a strong reputation and popularity among locals and visitors alike. Its authentic flavors and welcoming atmosphere make it a worthwhile destination for those seeking to explore the culinary delights of Phú Yên cuisine in Ho Chi Minh City.

ChIJyTw3GVMpdTERSuCQDdEe1e8.text: Today I went to eat chicken rice because of the review on gg map. If you pay attention to the portion + taste, you should try it. Ms. Chuc makes delicious food so I rate 5 stars for the food. However, I feel that the attitude of the couple towards me is not respected. First, I went to the restaurant, because it was my first time eating there, I asked the couple where to park the car, the couple scolded me and said "on the side of the road". Second, I ordered food, we went with 2 people and ordered 2 large portions, the couple didn't have any left and didn't explain, she just said verbatim "no more, no large portion left, only small portion, eat it". The food was brought out very slowly, I didn't pay much attention, but the third thing I really hate is the attitude of the couple towards us while we were eating, tapping the plate, being grumpy, doing everything loudly. I was really happy, I ate half of the plate of rice and left without wanting to stay. You know how it feels to sit and not be able to breathe or speak, so how can you enjoy the meal? This is my personal feeling, I'm stating my opinion. The food is moderate and cheap, however I won't come back next time. Thank you.

ChIJL77O-z4ndTEReFjBDibZNtA.author: Andy Gloria
ChIJL77O-z4ndTEReFjBDibZNtA.text:
Today I visited Ga Cung - Com Ga Tam Ky restaurant, I must say I was impressed with both the food and the service. I ordered a portion of shredded chicken rice and fried chicken with fish sauce, the chicken was chewy and delicious, flavored, especially the fried fish sauce was fragrant and not dry at all. The rice was cooked with chicken broth so the grains were golden, soft and chewy, served with a slightly spicy ginger, garlic and chili fish sauce, very appetizing. There was also free soup and pickles to help with the feeling of fullness. 
The restaurant space was spacious, clean, the tables and chairs were neat, the staff served quickly and friendly, always asking customers if the food was to their liking. The price was reasonable, compared to the quality of the food, it was more than worth it. The restaurant also had boiled chicken rice, roasted chicken, and roasted chicken to choose from, so I went many times without getting bored. 
Overall, I think this is a Tam Ky chicken rice restaurant worth trying, suitable for both lunch and dinner. Anyone who loves authentic Central Vietnamese chicken dishes will definitely like it. Next time I will come back to try some other dishes because they are really delicious and worth the money.

ChIJAYJoAQAvdTERIAj_-BaXOio.text:
I just tried Vietnamese Bún Đậu for the first time, and it was such a unique experience!
The platter came with fried tofu, fresh herbs, rice vermicelli (cut into little square blocks), and different sides. The fried tofu tasted very different from what I’m used to—crispy on the outside and soft inside, really delicious.
The rice vermicelli squares were fun to dip into the soy-based sauce.

I also had the orange & plum drink, which was super refreshing and perfectly balanced the meal.

Overall, it’s a flavorful dish, light but satisfying, and definitely something I’d recommend trying if you want to explore authentic Vietnamese flavors.

ChIJN2v31xkpdTER7vEYcvhcZBg.text:

Usually every time I eat elsewhere, I have to order more vermicelli and side dishes, but here I don't need to order more and I'm still very full.
The shrimp paste is more delicious than the average.
Another plus point is the iced tea is also very thoughtful, with very little ice.
The restaurant is clean, airy, and not hot from the stove.

It's been a long time since I've eaten at a vermicelli and bean curd restaurant that I had to leave such a detailed review. Everyone should try it here.

ChIJBZyMCt4udTERWy0UxVGcQNg.author: Ray Mak
ChIJBZyMCt4udTERWy0UxVGcQNg.text:
In Vietnam, sometimes the simplest roadside eateries serve the most unforgettable meals. Tucked away in District 10 is a small, humble restaurant that offers a truly traditional Vietnamese noodle dish. The noodles are uniquely clumped together, creating a comforting texture that pairs perfectly with an array of delicious accompaniments, various meats, tofu, fresh vegetables, fragrant herbs, crispy pork lard, and more. What truly elevates the dish is the accompanying fermented shrimp sauce, rich in flavor and complexity.

To complement this hearty meal, kumquat juice is an absolute must, its bright, citrusy notes balance the boldness of the noodles beautifully. We opted for the combination platter to savor the full variety of ingredients, and each bite was a delightful discovery.

For the fermented shrimp sauce, be sure to mix in the fresh chillies and a squeeze of lime provided; this simple addition transforms the sauce into something extraordinary. Affordable and bursting with authentic flavors, this meal easily ranks among the best I’ve had in Ho Chi Minh City on this trip.

ChIJ13BFg9YndTERZWGeX-WtLWI.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
A little Hanoi hidden in a Saigon alley! 🇻🇳

Got lost around Bùi Viện and accidentally found this hidden gem in a tiny alley — Bún Đậu Mắm Tôm Quán No. The space is small, cozy, and feels just like the little food corners in Hanoi. I was honestly surprised how authentic everything felt.

We ordered the phần đặc biệt with nem chua rán, and wow — the flavors were spot on. Crispy tofu, juicy pork, crunchy chả cốm, and that mắm tôm? Fermented heaven. If you know, you know 😎

The staff were super friendly, the vibe was chill, and for a second I forgot I was in Saigon.

If you're craving real Northern food and don’t mind a little alley adventure, this place is 100% worth it.

Xin chao, Anh yeu Viet Nam! 🇻🇳

ChIJpQre-XsvdTERPLegkB6UCbY.author: yumz
ChIJpQre-XsvdTERPLegkB6UCbY.text:
THE ULTIMATE VIETNAMESE TOFU NOODLE FLEX

·

THE DISH BREAKDOWN
bún đậu is that iconic hanoi street food combo of crispy tofu, rice noodles, and herbs that absolutely slays. the real star is the mắm tôm, that funky fermented shrimp paste that separates the pros from the tourists.

THE FLAVOR SITUATION
this spot serves up light, delicious, and easy eats that hit different. the textures and freshness create a vibe that's lowkey perfect for when you want something satisfying without the food coma.

THE MẮM TÔM REALNESS
keeping it a buck, the shrimp paste can be intimidating at first whiff. the move is to mix in some chili and squeeze in a lime until it becomes this magical pink potion. if you can't handle the funk, ask for fish sauce and create your own dip situation.

THE EATING RITUAL
once your sauce is properly slaying, start dipping everything and creating perfect bites. the combo of crispy tofu, fresh herbs, and that sauce is straight fire when you get the ratios right.

THE FINAL VERDICT
if you're ready to level up your vietnamese food game and try something authentically epic, this spot is a total yes. just remember to breathe through your mouth when you first open that shrimp paste.

The centerpiece behind each bite always returns to the addictive fermented shrimp paste dip, which packs a deeply umami, salty and funky punch that has hints of durian/red onions. You can adjust the taste with a squeeze of calamansi, sugar and chilli, but the crispy fried tofu, pork spring rolls, cured pork, pork shank, pork eat, various sausages are incomplete without the sauce. Savour each bite wrapped in rice vermicelli, tons of herbs and rice paper for the full experience.

ChIJpSgiVSwvdTERMBJuv7yKo5M.text:
We wanted to dine at Secret Garden but it was full for our group of 6 pax (4 adults and 2 children under 6 years old).

So we ended up at this place, which the staff told us that it's run by the same owner of Secret Garden.
In fact, this shop sells Northen food and Secret Garden sells Southern food.

Thus, we decided to dine here since it seems interesting to us as we peeked at what other diners are having.

The food did not disappoint. It was interesting and it was our first time trying out more types of Northern Vietnamese food.

The English speaking hunk was very helpful. He told us what to order and how much food to order. We were impressed with his service. He even went to dig out 4 cheese crackers for my 2 children 😆

Will definitely recommend.

The husband finds the Bun cha nicer here too.

The prawn paste was great. The staff told us to add sugar, lime and chilli to suit our taste.

ChIJ63eFecsvdTERywAYrHW1jNs.author: Gianni Nguyen
ChIJ63eFecsvdTERywAYrHW1jNs.text:
When the craving for Bun Dau Mam Tom hits, I went on a savory adventure and landed at this street-side spot.

The food? Flavor packed, the  fermented shrimp paste sauce was punchy (in the best way), and the portion was decent. That said, if you’re extra hungry or have a soft spot for one of the sides, I’d recommend ordering a side.

The vibe is classic sidewalk dining bamboo tables and stools on a lively, traffic-swooshing street. It’s not fine dining, it’s fun dining.

Shoutout to the staff for being attentive. I also grabbed a Bun Cha to go but sadly, they were out of eggrolls.

ChIJ63eFecsvdTERywAYrHW1jNs.text:
Tried this little place today. Was a cute little set up with bamboo tables and chairs. We tried the bun dau mam tom set dish and was pleasantly surprised that the sauce wasn’t too salty as most places. All the other little pieces worked well with the sauce. We had the tra tác tea which was also very refreshing and not too sweet.
Should try this place if you like this fermented dish.

ChIJq8N1Dxs7dTERk6c4M3DEjU8.text:
Anh Tuyet Bun Dau Mam Tom - Affordable, near Binh Khanh ferry!

The restaurant is small, located in an alley but easy to find. The restaurant space is affordable with plastic tables and chairs, mainly for students.
The bun dau here is generally okay, with all the ingredients such as vermicelli, tofu, cốm sausage,... but in my opinion, it doesn't have its own unique characteristics. Only the tofu is fried crispy and delicious. In addition, the restaurant has a good lemon tea.

With affordable prices and good quality, I rate the restaurant 7/10. If you like a budget, friendly space and want to enjoy bun dau mam tom at a reasonable price, Anh Tuyet restaurant is an option.

ChIJ5VJxm70pdTERGGhR_9CNUY0.text:
My experience at ĐẬU VÀNG - Bún Đậu Mắm Tôm located at 527 Nguyễn Văn Quá was exceptional. Upon entering, we were greeted warmly by the staff and seated promptly. The ambiance was cozy and inviting, perfect for a casual meal with friends or family.

We ordered their signature dish, Bún Đậu Mắm Tôm, and it exceeded our expectations. The flavors were authentic, and the ingredients were fresh and well-prepared. The dish was served promptly, and we were impressed by the generous portion size.

What made the experience even more memorable was the complimentary drinks they offered us. We were pleasantly surprised by this gesture of hospitality. The drinks were refreshing and complemented our meal perfectly.

Overall, our visit to ĐẬU VÀNG was delightful. The delicious food, welcoming atmosphere, and complimentary drinks made it a dining experience to remember. We left feeling satisfied and would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for authentic Vietnamese cuisine with excellent service.

ChIJYaLmeQAvdTERZxZCYVIe8vQ.text: It was delicious! The tofu was crispy on the outside and moist on the inside. The spring rolls were especially good, absolutely amazing. Everyone should order the spring rolls. They gave a bit too much shrimp paste; I had a lot left over, so it was a bit wasteful. I also wanted to try the banh goi (a type of Vietnamese dumpling) but they weren't selling it when I went. Overall, it's worth a try.

ChIJQ6I440AvdTERZl6zEfMf1r4.author: Phuc Minh
ChIJQ6I440AvdTERZl6zEfMf1r4.text:
Bun Dau Lang Vong - Pham Hung
Full combo but I "switched the wheel" to fish sauce!
Today I stopped by Lang Vong Bun Dau Mam Tom restaurant - a place that anyone addicted to shrimp paste will surely love... but I belong to the group of "smelling shrimp paste makes my soul leave my body", so I had to ask permission... to dip in fish sauce to be safe.
🧺 Super neat bun dau tray - just looking at it makes me want to eat it right away
The tray looked exactly like "neat like a teacher checking my homework", each dish was lined up in a straight line:
Bun cut into square pieces as if it had just come out of the production oven.
Fried tofu was crispy, picked up and heard the "crackling" sound, making me feel happy as if I had just received my salary.
Fried green rice sausage, fried sour sausage, pork leg, fish sausage... all in formation.
Cucumbers lined up like a ceremonial procession preparing for a parade.
Fried perilla, fish mint, and fresh green Vietnamese balm.
Looking at the tray, you can tell the restaurant is very "dedicated" and has a high aesthetic sense.
🫶 Moment of Truth: I asked for fish sauce
The restaurant serves vermicelli with shrimp paste, but I… can’t eat shrimp paste.
So when I said:
“Sir, I’d like fish sauce!”
At that moment, I felt like I had just announced that I was giving up on my shrimp paste class in the middle of the class. But luckily, the restaurant was accommodating, bringing out a bowl of garlic chili fish sauce that looked so delicious it was almost enough to make me faint.
The fish sauce was fragrant, rich, the garlic chili was so spicy that it tore my heart apart → each bite was a mood-booster.
🍃 Roll it up and you’re hooked
Roll a perilla leaf, add a piece of vermicelli, a slice of cucumber, a little squid sausage → dip it in fish sauce → put it in your mouth…
Oh my god, life is still beautiful when you eat vermicelli with shrimp paste without shrimp paste.
📌 Conclusion: The restaurant has good service - suitable for the "no shrimp paste" team
Delicious food
Beautiful tray
Saving fish sauce
Spacious, airy space
Fast service
For those who are addicted to shrimp paste, the restaurant is heaven.
For those like me - "fish sauce team" - you can still eat deliciously, without being discriminated against.

ChIJQ6I440AvdTERZl6zEfMf1r4.text:
I have to say this vermicelli and tofu restaurant is excellent and has many great plus points!
The first impression is that the restaurant has prepared fragrant fried onion paste on each table, you can take as much as you want, it is really delicious and very generous.
The thing I like most is the quality of the ingredients. The food, especially the fresh green vegetables, looks different from the vermicelli and tofu restaurants I have been to. Everything feels fresher and cleaner.
Another plus point is the space. The restaurant is spacious, clean and very airy, not stuffy like normal vermicelli and tofu restaurants.
The price is completely commensurate with the quality received. I ordered 2 trays and was very satisfied. It is worth a try!"

ChIJQ6I440AvdTERZl6zEfMf1r4.name: places/ChIJQ6I440AvdTERZl6zEfMf1r4/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT21kNVYwNDRkRWRsT1ZSWGNIVXdhRlZGTWtkV1ZYYxAB
ChIJQ6I440AvdTERZl6zEfMf1r4.author: Thảo Tô
ChIJQ6I440AvdTERZl6zEfMf1r4.text:
1. Phân tích chi tiết từng món ăn
• Đậu hũ chiên: Đây là linh hồn của món bún đậu và là điểm mạnh nhất của Làng Vòng. Đậu hũ được cắt miếng vừa phải, chiên ngập dầu trên chảo lớn. Vỏ đậu sau khi chiên có màu vàng ruộm, rất giòn nhưng bên trong vẫn giữ được độ mềm, béo và thơm ngon. Nhiều thực khách nhận xét rằng đậu được chiên xong ăn ngay sẽ cảm nhận được hết độ ngon, còn nếu để nguội một chút thì lớp vỏ có thể bớt giòn.
• Mắm tôm: Mắm tôm ở đây được pha chế rất "vừa tay". Nó có vị mặn nhẹ, không quá gắt, kết hợp hài hòa với vị ngọt và một chút chua của chanh, cay của ớt. Quán phục vụ kèm một chút mỡ lợn nóng rưới lên trên, làm cho mắm tôm có độ béo ngậy, dậy mùi hơn. Đây là công thức pha mắm tôm được nhiều người đánh giá là "dễ ăn", phù hợp với cả những người mới thử bún đậu.
• Chả cốm: Chả cốm có độ dai vừa phải, khi chiên lên có lớp vỏ hơi giòn, phần cốm bên trong dẻo. Tuy nhiên, một vài ý kiến cho rằng vị cốm chưa thực sự nổi bật.
• Bún lá: Bún được ép thành từng miếng vuông vức, sạch sẽ và tiện lợi.
• Thịt luộc: Đây là món có sự đánh giá trái chiều. Một số người khen thịt có đủ nạc, mỡ, ăn không bị ngán. Tuy nhiên, một số khác lại nhận xét thịt luộc bị khô và thiếu độ tươi do được luộc sẵn và để nguội.
• Các món ăn kèm khác:
• Dồi sụn: Món này được nhiều người khen ngon, dồi chiên giòn, bên trong có sụn sần sật, ăn rất vui miệng.
• Nem rán (chả giò): Vỏ nem giòn rụm, nhưng nhân bên trong có thể hơi ngọt, không hoàn toàn giống với vị nem chua ngọt truyền thống của miền Bắc.
• Lòng dồi: Lòng được làm sạch, chiên giòn, ăn không bị đắng. Đây là một món "ăn chơi" được nhiều người yêu thích khi gọi thêm.
2. Không gian và dịch vụ
• Không gian: Đây là một lợi thế lớn của Làng Vòng so với nhiều quán bún đậu khác. Quán thường được trang trí theo phong cách hoài cổ, với các vật dụng tre nứa, bàn ghế gỗ, tạo cảm giác gần gũi nhưng vẫn sạch sẽ, lịch sự. Ánh sáng vàng dịu nhẹ cũng góp phần làm tăng không khí ấm cúng, rất thích hợp cho những buổi tụ tập bạn bè, gia đình.
• Dịch vụ: Nhân viên ở Làng Vòng thường được đào tạo chuyên nghiệp. Họ nhanh nhẹn trong việc order, phục vụ món ăn và luôn sẵn sàng hỗ trợ khách hàng.

ChIJFzqZHAAvdTERSCGblpA53t8.name: places/ChIJFzqZHAAvdTERSCGblpA53t8/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2tGQ09EQXhWVEpxWlVvemRrNVdOVXQ0T1ZCSFpGRRAB
ChIJFzqZHAAvdTERSCGblpA53t8.author: Tom Wallace
ChIJFzqZHAAvdTERSCGblpA53t8.text:
We usually go for Bún đậu mắm tôm in Q7 but decided to try this place in Q4 even though it ís almost twice as expensive as other restaurants serving the same food.

The traditional style decor is very pretty and the food is good but half a million dong for one shared plate plus one drink each is pricey in my experience.

The tofu, roast meat and sausage were of very high quality and delicious. If you want more of anything, you must pay an additional fee, unlike some other locations (particularly in Danang) where they offer a self serve area for extra noodles, tofu, salad and mắm.

Overall, the meal was excellent, but I just want to point out that I consider the prices to be 'tourist' prices rather than 'local' prices - you can find the same size shared plate for 100,000₫ cheaper at other locations in Q4 and Q7. If this was a touristy Q1 location, I would understand, but Q4 is usually much better value for authentic Vietnamese food.

At the end of the meal they gave us 2 free icecreams even though we were 4 people - a bit odd, but apparently based on how much Tiền! Tiền! Tiền! you spend.

Finally, our experience was very much soured by the nasty motorbike attendant who shouted at us and wouldn't let us leave. It turns out he needed to retrieve the tiny paper ticket he had handed me 2 hours earlier and which I had in my pocket but had forgotten about. He was so rude to me and my family that we left in complete shock, and would never return to the restaurant or recommend it purely because of how rude and aggrssive the red faced parking attendant was.

ChIJGbv7XEUldTER-0rUpviT_8M.text:
I had such a great meal here! I tried the bún đậu mắm tôm for the first time — it was so flavorful and fresh. The fried tofu and herbs were really good, and the dipping sauce was strong but delicious (if you’re into bold flavors, you’ll love it!). Everything was well-balanced and came beautifully arranged.

I also had som tam with sticky rice and fried chicken. The chicken was crispy and juicy, and the som tam had just the right kick of spice. So satisfying!

The staff were super friendly and helpful, and the owner was just the sweetest — really made me feel welcome. You can tell they put care into both the food and the service.

If you’re into Vietnamese or Thai flavors, this place is a gem. Definitely worth checking out. I’ll be back for sure!

ChIJw8eACQAldTERg93o4DKcS00.text:
Bun Dau Mac Van Khoa – Huynh Tan Phat Branch: Eat and Laugh, Get Full and Roll! 🤣🥢
📍 Address: Bun Dau Mac Van Khoa – Huynh Tan Phat, District 7
⭐ Rating: 9.75/10 – Delicious taste, fast service, fragrant shrimp paste!

What is so special about bun dau that everyone loves?
Everyone knows Mac Van Khoa is a comedian, but few people expect him to be a "tycoon" of bun dau! He is truly dedicated, wherever the bun dau restaurant opens, customers line up.

And what about the Huynh Tan Phat branch? Wow, needless to say! The restaurant is always bustling, customers come in and out like going to a festival, anyone who hasn't ordered yet but smells the smell of fried spring rolls will have to rush in!

Space – Looks simple but has "power"!
🏡 The restaurant is decorated in a "popular but luxurious" style, with a striking yellow color that you can tell at a glance that it's Mac Van Khoa's vermicelli and bean curd.
🪑 The bamboo tables and chairs are in true Northern style, and you feel like you're in the middle of Hanoi's Old Quarter.
😂 In particular, there's a photo of the owner smiling at you eating, it feels like he's being watched but still happy.

💡 Tips: If you happen to sit across from Mac Van Khoa's photo, just eat slowly, he won't take any part!

Food - Rich, full, literally "fragrant" shrimp paste!
🥢 A plate of vermicelli and bean curd with fire, crispy tofu, chewy and fragrant green rice sausage, soft boiled meat, crispy fried intestines, eating is both delicious and fun!
🥢 The shrimp paste is mixed with the right flavor, you can nod your head while dipping. If you can't eat shrimp paste, there's fish sauce, but trust me, once you try it, you'll be "addicted"!
🥢 Fatty fried spring rolls, fragrant, just one bite and your soul will fly up to... Huynh Tan Phat!

💡 Small tip: If you go with a large group, order the biggest tray, after eating you will find this life more worth living!

Service - Fast, fun, professional, no less than a game show!
🚀 The staff serve as fast as lightning, order and get your food right away, no need to worry about waiting long.
🤣 The special thing is that the staff are funny, joking just like the owner. While eating, listening to the staff's comedy can make you laugh out loud at the shrimp paste.
🎥 Sometimes there are fun livestreams, whoever is lucky will be on air with Mac Van Khoa!

Summary - "Close the deal" right away or you'll regret it!
✅ Plus points: Delicious food, beautiful space, humorous staff.
❌ Minus points: If you come and eat too much, you risk being "addicted" to vermicelli and fried tofu for the whole week!

🔥 Conclusion: Bun Dau Mac Van Khoa Huynh Tan Phat is not only a restaurant, but also a real comedy stage! Come here not only to eat but also to laugh heartily. If you haven't tried it, you've missed a beautiful part of life! 🤣🥢

ChIJsc1U8oYtdTERTXEjDZ44ERo.name: places/ChIJsc1U8oYtdTERTXEjDZ44ERo/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT201eU0wWlFaVGwwWkdobVRWWnRaVUZITTNGVFpXYxAB
ChIJsc1U8oYtdTERTXEjDZ44ERo.author: Nguyễn Tuấn Thịnh Trần
ChIJsc1U8oYtdTERTXEjDZ44ERo.text:
Trước tiên về phần giá cả, mình gọi 2 phần bún đậu thập cẩm (bao gồm bún đậu, đậu hũ, thịt luộc, chả cốm, nem rán và chả chiên) trị giá là 62k. Một mẹt 62k nhưng đồ ăn lại khá ít so với số tiền bỏ ra. Và mình có xem thử menu thì thấy đa phần món nào cũng giá khá cao nhưng đồ ăn lại đều khá ít.

Về phần đồ ăn, bún và đậu là hai phần quan trọng nhất nhưng cả hai đều khá không ngon. Bún thì cắt miếng khá to, không đẹp, nhiều vụn. Đậu hũ thì nhỏ, không nóng, khá bột, không thơm mùi đậu và khô. Chả cốm thì bình thường. Nem rán và chả chiên thì không đậm đà, khá nguội. Thịt luộc thì cắt khá dày nhưng phần nạt ít mà phần mỡ và da khá dày, ăn dễ ngán và hơi tanh cũng như ăn cảm giác như đồ cũ để lâu.

Về phần thái độ phục vụ thì nhân viên khá hời hợt, thiếu sự nhiệt tình. Hôm mình đi thì trời mưa khá lớn, mình tấp vào quán thì nhân viên cũng không để tâm hay hướng dẫn, hỗ trợ gì. Kiểu khách vào thì kệ khách. Khi thanh toán thì do mình không có tiền mặt nên đưa tiền 500k mà bill của mình là khoảng 100k mấy nhưng nhân viên không chịu nhận, với lý do là không có tiền thối. Trong khi là quán có hệ thống, chi nhánh, cũng khá lớn mà lại không có tiền thối. Thật sự rất thắc mắc.
Nói chung thì trải nghiệm tại quán từ đồ ăn đến nhân viên đều khá không ổn dù là một quán có hệ thống và nhiều chi nhánh nhưng lại để như vậy thì chứng tỏ khá tệ.

-

First of all, about the price, I ordered 2 mixed vermicelli and bean curd dishes (including vermicelli, bean curd, boiled meat, green rice sausage, fried spring rolls and fried spring rolls) worth 62k. A plate costs 62k but the food is quite small compared to the amount of money spent. And I looked at the menu and saw that most of the dishes were quite expensive but the food was quite small.

As for the food, vermicelli and bean curd are the two most important parts but both are not delicious. The vermicelli is cut into quite large pieces, not beautiful, with many crumbs. The tofu is small, not hot, quite powdery, does not smell of beans and is dry. The green rice sausage is normal. Fried spring rolls and fried spring rolls are not rich, quite cold. The boiled meat is cut quite thick but the lean part is small and the fat and skin are quite thick, making it easy to get bored and a bit fishy, ​​as well as feeling like old food that has been left for a long time.

As for the service attitude, the staff is quite superficial, lacking enthusiasm. The day I went, it was raining quite heavily, I stopped by the restaurant but the staff did not pay attention or give any instructions or support. They just let the customers come in. When paying, because I did not have cash, I gave 500k while my bill was around 100k but the staff refused to accept it, with the reason being that there was no change. While the restaurant has a system, branches, and is quite large, there is no change. It is really confusing. In general, the experience at the restaurant from the food to the staff is quite bad, even though it is a restaurant with a system and many branches, but to leave it like that is quite bad.

ChIJsc1U8oYtdTERTXEjDZ44ERo.name: places/ChIJsc1U8oYtdTERTXEjDZ44ERo/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25GWVRtcE9WVWRRZFVndGFVRnplR3RVVWpOSlduYxAB
ChIJsc1U8oYtdTERTXEjDZ44ERo.author: Trinh Việt
ChIJsc1U8oYtdTERTXEjDZ44ERo.text: I think from now on, I'll have to go to Google Maps to see reviews when I go to a restaurant. I often eat at the Nguyen Tri Phuong branch. Today, when it rained so much, I stopped at the Ten Lua branch. The rain was so heavy that the staff sitting at the counter didn't show me where to park my bike, so I had to go in and ask myself. I took off my raincoat and helmet and stood there, not knowing where to put it so it wouldn't get wet. The staff also sat there looking. We had to run to the car to cover it ourselves to keep it from getting wet because we couldn't see a place to put it inside, and they didn't lend us any umbrellas to run out. When I went to the table and looked out, I saw that they had umbrellas to cover and collect other customers' hats. So the restaurant had umbrellas but didn't ask if customers wanted to borrow them to go to the car? The hats were left on the car, and the wind and rain were so strong that they accidentally knocked two hats down on the dirty, wet street, and when the staff went out to collect other customers' hats to keep them from getting wet, they didn't see them to "ask" them to pick them up for us. An extremely frustrating experience at this branch and now I see a lot of complaints about the staff. I wonder if the restaurant really listens to customers' opinions to train the staff. The last time I ate at this Rocket branch!

Regarding the food, I felt that the bean curd was crispy, the fried sausages and sour spring rolls were relatively better than other restaurants. I was not satisfied with the fried intestines because I wanted them to be a bit crispier
The crab spring rolls were quite delicious and fragrant, fried evenly and not too black. If you order, they will be fried for about 10-15 minutes
About the service staff, I found them quite friendly, they gave clear advice, the prices were not higher than the general level, so overall it was okay, so I tried it and will come back

ChIJMzaxYJMtdTERH-8wMu7hyXY.text:
5 stars for everything, this restaurant is better than Ms. Hai's:
- The restaurant has a wide sidewalk, a big road so you can park comfortably
- The location is easy to find
- The restaurant is clean, airy, the tables and chairs are comfortable and spacious
- The food is delicious, a lot and the price is cheap
- 2 people, ordered a mixed portion for 2 people + 1 lime tea + 1 apricot juice + 1 extra green rice sausage + 1 extra vermicelli = 175k to fill your stomach
- The lime juice and apricot juice are mixed well, very strong, not diluted like other restaurants
- The food is less diverse than Ms. Hai's nearby restaurant, but the quantity is large
- Free extra vermicelli
- The staff is enthusiastic, the food is served quickly, when the drinks are served, they explain which glass is which
- The lime tea here is made of salted lime, not fresh lime
- The restaurant does not smell of shrimp paste like other restaurants
- This is the first time I've seen vermicelli with shrimp paste and lettuce
- The restaurant also sells Hanoi vermicelli with grilled pork, I saw the table next to me eating also a big part but have not tried

The restaurant space is also beautifully decorated, near the outdoors so it is airy.

I just had to write a review about Bún Đậu A Chảnh! I stumbled upon this place while wandering around Ho Chi Minh City, and it was a delightful lunch discovery. Let me tell you, the first thing that hits you is the presentation. They serve this massive platter of goodies on a traditional sàng gạo, a woven bamboo tray lined with banana leaves. It's so colorful and inviting, with fresh rice noodles, crispy fried tofu, and all these different meats like pork belly and chitterlings.

But the real star of the show is the mắm tôm, the fermented shrimp paste. Now, I know this condiment isn't for everyone – it has a strong smell! But if you're open to it, it adds this incredible layer of savory, funky depth to every bite. They give you a little dipping sauce on the side to mix with the mắm tôm, and it helps temper the intensity a bit.

I went with the thập cẩm, which means a mix of everything, and it was perfect for sharing (although I confess, I could have easily devoured it all myself!). The tofu was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, the pork belly was melt-in-your-mouth tender, and the fresh herbs added a bright, clean counterpoint to the richness of the dish.

Overall, Bún Đậu A Chảnh was a fantastic lunch experience. It's a great place to try some traditional Vietnamese flavors in a casual setting. Just be prepared for the mắm tôm – it might surprise you, but in a good way!

ChIJnRnoBAArdTEReE1YUn8fGxE.text:
Review of Em Thuy's Bun Dau Restaurant in Tan Phu – A Great Choice for Bun Dau Mam Tom Lovers
🍜 General Introduction – A Delicious Bun Dau Mam Tom Restaurant in Tan Phu
If you're looking for a delicious Bun Dau Mam Tom restaurant in Tan Phu or a Bun Dau Mam Tom restaurant near Aeon Mall Tan Phu, then Em Thuy's Bun Dau Mam Tom is definitely worth trying. My family loves this dish, so when we heard about a new restaurant opening near our house, we immediately went there. And we were truly impressed with the food quality, the atmosphere, and the prices. The menu offers many choices, suitable for individuals, families, or groups of friends.

🥢 Food Experience – Rich Flavor, Hot, and Generous Portions
My family of three chose the Bun Dau combo for 169K, currently discounted to 159K. The set includes: soy milk, rice noodles, fried rice patties, tofu, fried offal, beef shank, fried spring rolls… It's truly a satisfying meal; every dish is hot, plentiful, and perfectly seasoned.

• The shrimp paste is perfectly seasoned in the Northern style, fragrant but not overpowering.

• The fried tofu is golden and crispy, and stays hot even after sitting for a while.

• The fried spring rolls are crispy and have a rich filling.

• The beef shank is thickly sliced, firm, and delicious.

A plus is that the food comes out quickly but still stays piping hot.

💸 Price – Affordable and more "reasonable" than larger brands
One factor that surprised me is the price, which is quite reasonable, even cheaper than many large bun dau (rice noodles with tofu) brands. Portions range from 35K to 169K, suitable for students, office workers, and families. With such quality, this price is well worth it.

🚗 Parking – Convenient for both motorbikes and cars
You can park right in front of the restaurant, just turn on your hazard lights for safety. The road is quite wide, so cars can easily park quickly before going in to eat.

👩‍🍳 Staff – Polite & enthusiastic
The staff are quick, polite, and handle requests very professionally. Although the restaurant is small, the service is quite pleasant.

🏠 Space – Small but airy and clean
The restaurant isn't too big, but the layout is well-organized, making it look very spacious. The tables and chairs are clean, tidy, and don't have a greasy smell. It's comfortable even during peak hours.

⏱️ Service time – Fast, no long wait
The food is served quite quickly, suitable for customers who need a quick, delicious meal. A big plus for those who are in a hurry to work or school.

🎯 Suitable for:
• Office workers for breakfast, lunch, and dinner

• Business meetings/clients

• People looking for a good restaurant near Aeon Mall Tan Phu

• Families with young children
⭐ Recommended Dishes:
• Rice noodle platter with meat and tofu (35K)

• Rice noodle and tofu combo 1 (159K – 169K) suitable for groups of 2-3 people

📝 Suggestions:

• Hot tea and chewing gum should be available for customers

• Paper napkins should be provided for customer convenience (some customers don't like using wet wipes)

It was my first time eating here but I was very impressed.

We ordered a special 110k platter for 2 people, the restaurant gave us free noodles (you can choose between noodles/extra vegetables/rice paper/something else that I forgot), and ordered a bowl of eggplant - 12k, a glass of sour plum juice - 15k.

The vermicelli and bean curd here was enough to wow me ✨ the tofu was crispy on the outside, moist and hot on the inside; all the other toppings were hot and delicious. As for the shrimp paste, I found it to be the same as other restaurants, but the food was extremely good, including the eggplant bowl - crispy and sour, making me faint. The sour plum juice I found wasn't sour enough and had a strong sour plum flavor for my taste, but it was okay.

The part that surprised me the most was when I pushed the cart. The restaurant has a full ground floor for parking, and I ate on the 2nd and 3rd floors. The staff were extremely enthusiastic 😆 They pushed the cart out and even put the footrests on both sides for me =)))))

The restaurant was always crowded but the operation was ok so as soon as the customers left, the tables were cleaned up very neatly. The tables and chairs were small but still enough to sit comfortably, cool and just right.

I hope the next time I come back, the restaurant will maintain this level 🫰🏻
