ChIJH9Z22YUvdTERgRLjANFVUSU.name: places/ChIJH9Z22YUvdTERgRLjANFVUSU/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2pJdFVreGFhRFJOUVdwclJsOWFMVGhWVFdNMGFXYxAB
ChIJH9Z22YUvdTERgRLjANFVUSU.author: Olivia Phụng
ChIJH9Z22YUvdTERgRLjANFVUSU.text:
If anyone is a fan of snail dishes, I recommend trying Oc Chu Linh at Tan Hoa Canal. I often go to many snail restaurants so my experience is quite good and I was really surprised because every dish here is good, rich, the flavor is very "homemade" and not industrial like many other snail restaurants. 

- The restaurant is located right on the front of Tan Hoa Canal, easy to find, has spacious and airy seats. The restaurant is not fancy but very clean and tidy. In the evening, the restaurant is quite crowded but the service is still fast, not making customers wait long. 

- Because the day I went, the dishes ran out early, there was no tamarind sauce, no oysters, so I ordered basic dishes to try, and each dish left its own impression: 

- Boiled duck eggs served with Vietnamese coriander, salt, pepper, lemon and a little fresh chili - the eggs are fatty, well-formed, the water is naturally sweet, dipped in salt and chili is super suitable. 

- Steamed lemongrass snails: Fresh snails, crispy meat, steamed water with fragrant lemongrass scent. The steamed water is sweet and refreshing, adding green chili salt is perfect.

- Stir-fried buttered snails with garlic: This dish is super fragrant, the butter is just the right amount of fat, the snails absorb the spices well. It's quite good.

- Stir-fried corn is extremely good, the corn is crispy and sweet, the shredded pork is sprinkled on top, just right, there's also a little shredded pork on top, it's very enjoyable to eat.

- Stir-fried morning glory with garlic - simple but "sure", the green vegetables are crispy, the garlic is fragrant, the seasoning is just right, not too greasy.

- Grilled clams with green pepper: This dish makes a strong impression. Fresh clams, grilled just right, the green pepper sauce is spicy but still retains the sweetness of the clams. Very good with rice (or beer kkkk).

- Price: The price is quite reasonable compared to the quality, ranging from 30k-79k/dish, depending on the type of snail.

- The owner and staff are cheerful and enthusiastic, order quickly, and bring out the food quickly. There is a bowl of delicious Southern-style chili salt and lime.

-I saw people comment that they got free fruit, but when I went, there wasn't any, probably because the food ran out early. I'll review more next time I come back 🫰

ChIJsfMYqiUvdTERppWgz_-zpo4.text:

The price is suitable for the quality, outdoor seating space, you will have to wait a bit for a table.
However, sometimes the garlic snails will have a few pieces that are smelly, depending on the day it will be delicious.

ChIJsfMYqiUvdTERppWgz_-zpo4.author: Thanh Hoàng Nguyễn Ngọc
ChIJsfMYqiUvdTERppWgz_-zpo4.text:
Food: stir-fried snails with garlic, snails with salted egg sauce, grilled oysters with cheese, stir-fried instant noodles with cockles, Thai-style clams, grilled shrimp, grilled octopus, grilled clams with scallion oil and lime tea.

Most of the dishes were delicious, seasoned just right, but the instant noodles were not cooked thoroughly. The dipping sauce (sweet and sour fish sauce) was very delicious.

We ordered one portion of all the dishes except for the stir-fried noodles which were 3 portions and about 4 glasses of lime tea with about 4 cans of Pepsi. Total bill was 800k. Delicious food, affordable price, decent portion size, so it's suitable for large groups to order many dishes and split the bill. The restaurant is crowded, sitting outside has a roof.

ChIJB-Ref7wvdTERW9RFeERl5PE.text:
-The restaurant is spacious, airy, with many tables sitting close together.
-Reasonable prices, 40k/portion or more. Snails are priced per piece, from 20k/piece.
-I ordered Thai steamed clams, the Thai sauce was rich and spicy.
-The butter and garlic snails were well-seasoned, with fried pork fat.
-The snail stir-fried noodles were a bit bland, dipping them in fish sauce was just right.
-The oysters were plump and big. The scallion oil was more delicious than the cheese.
-When I ate, the restaurant was empty, so the food was served quickly, it took 5 minutes to get the food.
-Park opposite the restaurant.
-Be careful when riding a motorbike because there are a lot of pikachu hiding in this section of the road

A lot of menu for you to select but I think it’s normal in here that snail/shell restaurant will have a plenty of different dish. Anyway, you will see in my uploaded photo that the price is reasonable.

Since we visit on Friday night so we need to wait a bit longer to let staff serve our dish and sometimes we need to follow up our menu. The food taste is accept but I’m the person who don’t like main dish with sweet taste so some menu for me is not that too good and that is the reason why I give 4 star for food. Anyway, if you are local people here, I assume that you may enjoy with the dish.

The atmosphere is a bit smoke from cooking because we sit inside and I deduct the star from this point too.

ChIJFbeQIwAvdTERKf5IZ7f_nQo.author: r.l. resle
ChIJFbeQIwAvdTERKf5IZ7f_nQo.text:
There was this cursed corner, where restaurant after restaurant would open, only to remain entirely devoid of customers for a few months and then fade away like it never even existed.

And then, it was OC TRUNG MUOI's turn and suddenly the street exploded with an unending choir of chewing, slurping, crunching beer cans: crowds of customers swarmed in: the curse was dispelled.

So, we had to try it. We just had to.
Stars followed, in descending order:

4 for the atmosphere: this is a textbook "nhau" place and you really can't beat that joyful, youthful, yet old fashioned.

3 for the food, generous portions, cheap price, perhaps not the freshest seafood out there but my guts didn't care too much.

2 for the service. Waiters are actually quick and nice. But their manager (or at least we thought she was their manager) yelled and cursed at them relentlessly all the time, sending unnecessary zaps of tension between the tables.

Verdict:
pack an imodium or two, earplugs, and give OTM a try.

ChIJ9bBIK5ovdTERXOUNNEW8YGo.author: Liz
ChIJ9bBIK5ovdTERXOUNNEW8YGo.text: Bánh Mì Huỳnh Hoa is hands down one of the best bánh mì spots in Saigon. From the moment you take your first bite, you can taste the quality in every layer. The baguette is perfectly crispy on the outside and soft inside, packed generously with a rich variety of cold cuts, pate, fresh herbs, and house-made sauces. Each component is well-balanced, flavorful, and incredibly satisfying. Despite being famous and often busy, the service is quick and efficient. One bánh mì is filling enough for a full meal. If you’re looking for an unforgettable, authentic Vietnamese bánh mì experience, Huỳnh Hoa is an absolute must-try.

ChIJ9bBIK5ovdTERXOUNNEW8YGo.name: places/ChIJ9bBIK5ovdTERXOUNNEW8YGo/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xkbVdsRm9ZM0F4UjJwaGFIY3lkbFJvTmxWaWMzYxAB
ChIJ9bBIK5ovdTERXOUNNEW8YGo.author: Christopher Wu
ChIJ9bBIK5ovdTERXOUNNEW8YGo.text:
From Melbourne, which already has a pretty strong banh mi game, I had to give this spot a try after seeing it hyped all over social media. Tried the mixed ham banh mi — I’ve never seen one packed with this much meat before, it was absolutely loaded.

Flavour-wise though, it didn’t quite hit for me. It was a bit too full-on and the balance just wasn’t there. They give you salad on the side to add into the banh mi, which helps freshen it up, but the bread didn’t have that signature crisp I look for. Probably because they’re pumping them out so fast, so the consistency can vary — still decent overall though.

Queued up for about 10 minutes — they’re efficient and move quick. The banh mi itself is massive, easily shareable between two people. Towards the end, the texture got a bit weird on mine, might’ve just been my roll, but I wasn’t a fan. Definitely could’ve used more chilli or a spice kick.

For around $5, you can’t really complain, but coming from Melbourne’s already strong banh mi scene, I was expecting a bit more given the hype.

ChIJPSwAMz0vdTERPs4NXMo-5UY.name: places/ChIJPSwAMz0vdTERPs4NXMo-5UY/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTUR3bjVEVm9BRRAB
ChIJPSwAMz0vdTERPs4NXMo-5UY.author: Nickolas Ho
ChIJPSwAMz0vdTERPs4NXMo-5UY.text:
Located right across from Bùi Thị Xuân High School, this famous bánh mì shop in Ho Chi Minh City is a must-try for anyone craving a delicious, satisfying sandwich. It’s easy to find and the shop is bustling from early morning until about 7 or 8 PM. The bánh mì here is generously filled, with prices ranging from 25k to 40k for a fully loaded sandwich.

What truly sets this place apart is the rich, homemade pâté, which adds a savory depth to the sandwich without being too heavy. The bread itself is larger than the typical bánh mì, with a wonderfully airy, crispy texture thanks to a perfect balance of flour and yeast. The cuts of cold cuts are thicker than usual, and the cured meats, especially the cold cuts, are notably flavorful and distinctive.

The attention to detail in how the sandwich is wrapped is also impressive. Each order is carefully packaged in a sturdy plastic bag, with the pickled vegetables and fresh herbs separated into their own packets for a perfect take-away experience. The pickles are perfectly balanced—not too sour or sweet—but complement the richness of the pâté and butter beautifully.

For those looking for a refreshing drink, the shop also offers traditional Vietnamese drip coffee. The cà phê sữa (iced coffee with condensed milk) has a strong coffee flavor but without overwhelming bitterness, making it a delightful pairing to your sandwich. The ice-to-coffee ratio is just right, so you won’t be left with diluted coffee.

Though the shop is often crowded, the wait is minimal—usually just 5 to 10 minutes—making it a perfect stop for a quick and satisfying meal. Whether you're a local or a visitor, this bánh mì spot is sure to leave you craving more.

ChIJOWPxdjQvdTERu6Iz3uH3sBQ.text:
As a keen fan of banh mi with the most basic of fillings, I was thrilled to hear about Banh mi Cu Ly. However, after sampling their offerings, I must admit that the banh mi here is rather ordinary, not even as tasty as many popular street vendor stalls. For VND 25.000, a loaf includes approximately 4-5 different types of pork rolls or ham, cucumber, onion, and a few seasonings such as pepper salt, soy sauce, and chilli sauce.

While the pork rolls are delicious on their own, the overall banh mi is rather bland and flavourless. I could not detect the slightest hint of the pepper salt or soy sauce. I am unsure whether the taste is inherently bland or if the vendor was in a rush and forgot to season my banh mi properly. The only strong flavour I could taste was an overpowering pungency from the onions, which were not well prepared and were simply spicy and pungent.

When I passed by, the owner told me that if I’m heading to the airport, I should buy it then because it tastes better fresh, so I asked for his phone number.

Before my flight, I called him to prepare the bánh and arranged delivery to my location. Both the owner and his wife were very helpful. The bánh traveled by air, and after two hours of flying plus transport time, it still arrived delicious. I really like the topping they use.

ChIJNV2Sg7QudTERnSGTNpu0Spc.text:
40-year-old sandwich shop in Ho Chi Minh City, crowded until midnight 🥵
The sandwich shop has a compact space, no elaborate display, only a signboard with the words "Ms. Diep's sandwich" and a small stainless steel table placed in front of the porch. On the table are neatly arranged fresh ingredients to stuff the sandwiches such as pate, butter, sausage, cold cuts, pork belly, shredded pork, meatballs, raw vegetables, sauce 🤤
The price of sandwiches here is about 12,000 VND - 25,000 VND per loaf. There are customers who are in difficulty and only buy a loaf for 7,000 VND, the shop owner is also happy to sell 🥰According to Ms. Diep, on average from 6am to 10am, she will sell 600 loaves. From 10am to 2pm, about 200 loaves. The rest of the time, the shop sells about 700 more loaves. On average, Mrs. Diep's bakery sells 1,500-2,000 loaves of bread every day.

ChIJJ4c9GkgvdTERv37sYGa3QA8.text:
A Must-Try Bánh Mì Spot in Saigon!

First visit to Saigon, and of course we were on the hunt for our first bánh mì. We came across My Banh Mi and noticed all the TripAdvisor Travelers’ Choice stickers on the window. We thought, “Okay… really? Let’s see if this place lives up to it.” We’re foodies back home, so we came ready to judge!

Walking in, the place is cute, cozy, and charming. We were greeted by three wonderful staff members who immediately made us feel welcome. My girlfriend is pescatarian, so we’ve been searching for tofu bánh mì options. They had two—fresh pan-roasted fish and fried tofu—and all three staff members enthusiastically recommended the tofu with spicy garlic aioli. So of course, we went with their suggestion.

While waiting, we took two shots of Jameson (why not?!), and our sandwich came out fresh. We ordered it to go but decided to take a bite while it was still hot… and wow. WOW. The bread was warm and crispy, the tofu portion was generous, and that spicy garlic aioli made this sandwich a star. It tasted like a mix of garlic aioli and chili oil—absolutely delicious.

Highly, highly recommend this spot. I only wish we were hungrier so we could’ve tried more options. We’ll definitely be back!

My sister also got a beef banh mi with the spicy garlic sauce and she said it was amazing. If you're vegan and you're torn on what to get (like I was), please get the pho nirvana, I have never tasted such amazing tofu before, the broth was perfect, and the charred brocolli went so perfectly in it.

ChIJLddkTxUvdTERHgi1DIl5qz4.text:
Chinese-style cooked noodles are like that, they may appear simple, but creating a broth with a flavour that lingers on the diner's palate and remains in their memory even after returning home is quite challenging.

The broth at 70 Ky Con is exceptionally delicious. Although it is clear and light, some may find the flavour unremarkable, but gourmets will immediately appreciate the exquisite harmony of simple salty and sweet tastes.

A complete bowl of dry noodles for VND 60.000 includes both meat and fish. The meat here is lean, cut in a batonnet style. The fish used is snakehead fish fillet, which, despite being a river fish, has no fishy odour. Even the fish fillet slices are both chewy and crunchy.

Enjoying a bowl of noodles, ordering a plate of youtiao (remember to request it be cut in advance), and a glass of milk tea constitute a satisfying meal. The restaurant is constantly busy from opening to closing. Despite the crowds, the staff remain courteous and attentive to customers.

ChIJVVVVVcoodTER2bnH-JyM448.author: Anh Nguyen
ChIJVVVVVcoodTER2bnH-JyM448.text: I ordered ”mì Mr.King 1 người” and “bông cúc nhãn nhục”. I felt really reminiscent of the fast noodle dishes when I saw this bowl. The sauce is amazing and the texture of the noodle was so alike to what I’ve eaten when I was little in Vietnam. Everything on the dish was great. The pork rib was tender and juicy but the sauce was a little sweet. I expected more heat from that but the rib in whole was decent. The egg yolk of the boiled egg was still runny and I loved it. I used that as a complimentary sauce to the noodle and it was the most clever choice. The soup aside was just a simple broth but this elevated the dish so well. The drink I ordered was also great. I love the fact that you can eat and still enjoy the street view+environment of Saigon without sitting too near to it.

ChIJVVVVVcoodTER2bnH-JyM448.author: Genevieve Vox
ChIJVVVVVcoodTER2bnH-JyM448.text:
Mr. Mì is a little eatery just off the main Le Loi street. We sat on the balcony overlooking Pasteur street while enjoying 2 bowls of "Mì Xá Xíu Hồng Kông" (Hong Kong char siu noodles), VND 45.000 each.

The eatery is located on the first floor (or second floor, correct me if I'm wrong) of a fairly shabby apartment, so on the way to get to the eatery, there would be some uncomfortable smells.

They were short-staffed, with only an old couple doing everything, so we had to wait a bit.

I heard they intended to close the place back in June 2022 due to short of expenses, but probably thanks to customers coming more and more, they were able to keep the place open. Therefore, each of the customers who come and eat here is a great support to the old couple to maintain their business.

ChIJXYJaGwAvdTERAmIexPxVV6w.author: Giang Pham
ChIJXYJaGwAvdTERAmIexPxVV6w.text:
"A unique bánh mì," they said. Sure, on paper it is. But if you were to blindfold me and ask me to tell a difference between this and any other cold-cut bánh mì, I wouldn't be able to tell.

I went early morning to grab one for breakfast so there was no wait. The prices seem to have gone up slightly for everything. The small is now 38K & the large is 59K. Honestly, the prices are not bad for how big the portion sizes are. The small is bigger than the average bánh mì you'd find in most street stalls & is more than enough (or even a little too much) for the average Vietnamese' appetite.

Taste-wise, however, it was a bit of a letdown. Was it bad by any means? No. In fact, I found it quite solid... as any other solid cold-cut bánh mì you'd find out there in HCMC (which are plenty). Its one advertised unique aspect, the cốm butter, absolutely did not come through at all, not even a hint, when eaten together with everything else as a whole sandwich. The pate was the dominant flavor. When I tried the cốm butter on its own, it tasted like the pork floss that was directly placed on top of it instead. Speaking of which, their pork floss was really good & apparently they have 2 kinds, a regular and a fried-shallots one which you have to specifically request since they don't tell you about it lol

Now, I ordered the regular bánh mì without adding anything extra so I thought maybe the problem would be solved if you ordered extra cốm butter. However, someone I know ordered theirs with extra butter and they still had the exact same experience except they could actually taste the nice cốm flavor when they tried just the butter on its own. What I'm gathering from that is that maybe the best way to experience this unique cốm butter on a bánh mì is to just get it separately on its own and put it on a plain bánh mì and enjoy.

For the price and the portion size, I wasn't mad at what I got. I would probably revisit just to do the hack I mentioned. But if you're hoping to experience a cool gimmicky bánh mì like me, this isn't worth it. Again, it's not bad, just nothing special.

ChIJ9-1JQtgvdTER5PwDWnWbXoQ.text:
Tucked away inside a small alley across from Ben Thanh market you can find the most amazing Bahn mi around.
From the original classic, to a full lobster Bahn mi, there is surely something that you'll like.
I chose the pork with crispy skin Bahn mi, and I pretty much inhaled it in a few seconds it was so delicious. The bread is exceptionally fresh with a crisp outside and fluffy inside and the filling is generous.

ChIJ9-1JQtgvdTER5PwDWnWbXoQ.text: Although both the Chicken and the Original Banh Mi's were tasty (Chicken was better) one of my biggest pet peeves is dishes coming out at different times. Its a good thing my wife likes to share because it was quite some time before my order came out. We also had to chase our server down for the change, after we paid our bill. ChIJ9-1JQtgvdTER5PwDWnWbXoQ.name: places/ChIJ9-1JQtgvdTER5PwDWnWbXoQ/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT21kNkxXUnZSbWRIVEc5Q2JrZFZPRE5pUmtGTk5uYxAB
ChIJ9-1JQtgvdTER5PwDWnWbXoQ.author: Paul Hutton
ChIJ9-1JQtgvdTER5PwDWnWbXoQ.text:
Awesome Banh Mi! I saw a comment suggesting that this is potentially a tourist trap, and when you first look at the menu and prices, you would be forgiven for thinking so.

I decided to do a little comparison between 3 different vendors in the area. The other 2 were considerably cheaper, but the Banh Mi here is seriously amazing and in my opinion totally worth the price I paid. I had the original and the mixed which are the two cheaper options on the menu. They were both huge compared to the other vendors and completely packed with delicious fillings. I can normally demolish two Banh Mi from the street vendors and in some cases could probably fit in a third. After just one of these I was completely full and satisfied. I will now have to go back to try one of the more premium options.

Admittedly I would find it hard to justify spending some of the prices advertised for a single Banh Mi, but as a treat and something a little different to the run of the mill Bahn Mi available on the street, why not? 😁

The service provided was warm, friendly and professional.

The atmosphere was great.

The packaging, separate sauce, plastic gloves, instructions for eating, toothpick and napkin are a great touch and definitely add to the value of the experience.

I absolutely recommend this place for an exceptional and unique Bahn Mi adventure!

ChIJY9slStkvdTERYO0HuGXismk.name: places/ChIJY9slStkvdTERYO0HuGXismk/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25WVWJIWnpNMnBJVVdGNFYydE9MVEpUUzBwV1gwRRAB
ChIJY9slStkvdTERYO0HuGXismk.author: Jessie Lan Pham
ChIJY9slStkvdTERYO0HuGXismk.text:
Bánh Mì Tăng is one of the oldest bánh mì brands in Saigon and has been ranked among the top 10 most well-known shops. I ordered the Tăng special with cold cuts, Vietnamese ham, meatballs, pâté and a bottle of soy milk.

The packaging was neat and thoughtful, they even included a wet tissue and toothpick. I also like that they don’t use onions so it doesn’t cause bad breath, and the chili comes separately so you can adjust the spice yourself.

The bánh mì was tasty but not really impressive. The bread was a bit soft while I prefer it crunchier. The soy milk was too sweet and had mung beans mixed in. Overall, it’s a classic bánh mì with a balanced amount of filling that doesn’t feel heavy, but I wouldn’t go out of my way to order it again with extra shipping.

ChIJY9slStkvdTERYO0HuGXismk.name: places/ChIJY9slStkvdTERYO0HuGXismk/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2pkTWFtcHRUVk50VG5ZeGJWTnlZM1F0ZVZwTVoyYxAB
ChIJY9slStkvdTERYO0HuGXismk.author: Bredgy L.
ChIJY9slStkvdTERYO0HuGXismk.text:
Follow @bredgyeats for more food posts!

Where there's banh mi, there's savoury sticky rice, and there's little reason not to try both. The fluffy baguette trumps the sticky rice for its subtle sweetness and yeasty aroma it adds to each bite, sandwiching a wonderful balance of ingredients that palates from across the globe have grown to love. The rich savoriness of the meats melded with the mayo, pate, pickled carrots and daikon, cucumbers, and cilantro creates a harmonious experience that's seldom found in Toronto. Sharing many common ingredients like sliced cold cuts and a savoury, rich pate. The addictive glutinous texture serves as an excellent vehicle for the rest of the toppings, too, including a fragrant scallion oil, subtly sweet pork floss, along with crunchy peanuts. I find comfort in knowing great banh mi can be found no matter what district you're in, as this location hits the spot too. It's up to you whether you prefer a coarser, stronger pate and a touch easier on the mayo. The sticky rice even includes Chinese sausage and quail egg.

ChIJS0g3UDwvdTERVnrWATZwqJM.author: Lorraine Bmor
ChIJS0g3UDwvdTERVnrWATZwqJM.text:
The other more famous shop has more queues over Bánh Mì Hồng Hoa, and is generally the popular spot for tourists, but don’t let fool you. Bánh Mì Hồng Hoa is far superior (atleast for me) and here is why:

1. Size:
Bigger isn’t always better. 🙈 The competitor offers just one massive size of banh mi while Hong Hoa gives you an option; one that is as big as the rival shop and one that is just the right size that’ll give you the perfect bite with everything in it (bread, veggies, and meat). Since the competitor’s is so big, it’s impossible to get that perfect bite, unless of course, you have an equally as massive mouth. Lol.

2. Variety:
The other shop has only one Banh Mi option which is the traditional “put every Vietnamese charcuterie” in a baguette. It’s tasty and the most traditional but you’d get tired of it easily. More options would be better. Meanwhile, Hong Hoa has 6 varieties to choose from with their Bread with Roast Pork option being the best!

3. Price:
The other shop’s pricing, as mentioned by many, is too expensive at 73K VND. Yes, it is big. But Hong Hoa offers the same size at just 55K VND.  🤷🏻‍♀️

4. Taste:
Not gonna lie, the rival’s is delicious as heck but there is a thing as over filling. It has too much meat, butter, and paté that it has become too overwhelming on the taste buds. They give you separate packs of fresh greens and pickled vegetables but even that isn’t enough to balance out the flavors.

On the other hand, Hong Hoa’s is perfectly balanced. We tried both their Roast Pork and Mixed Meat one which is similar to Huynh Hoa’s to give it a fair comparison.

For the Mixed Meat one, the slices of ham and paté taste better here although not as generous and the other shop. Again, Quality > Quantity. 😉 And for the Roast Pork one, it is hands down the best Banh Mi I’ve had in my life!!!!! The pork is nicely charred and its fattines goes really well with the pickled veggies. It meat is kinda reminiscent of Pork Sisig (a Filipino dish). It even has that spicy little kick from the chilies. It’s a sandwich worth the trip back to Saigon! 💯

Either way, both these Saigon banh mi shops made the most famous stall (for tourists) in Hanoi, Banh Mi 25, taste like utter crap. Lol. 🤣

Cons: The noodles are instant noodles (this explains the cheap price). ChIJ105Rz2gvdTERSi0aFdCZa8k.name: places/ChIJ105Rz2gvdTERSi0aFdCZa8k/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNCOFpDcl9BRRAB
ChIJ105Rz2gvdTERSi0aFdCZa8k.author: Thanh Hảo Lê
ChIJ105Rz2gvdTERSi0aFdCZa8k.text:
As a self-proclaimed noodle fanatic, I couldn't resist the allure of Mì Ốc Hến Dì Lan, a local legend in Saigon's District 4. The moment I stepped foot in the simple, no-frills setting, I knew I was in for a treat. The aroma of simmering broth and fresh seafood filled the air, instantly whetting my appetite.

I opted for the classic mì ốc hến, a comforting bowl brimming with springy noodles, plump clams, and perfectly cooked snails. The first sip of the broth was a revelation. Rich and flavorful, it spoke of hours spent meticulously coaxing out the essence of seafood. Each slurp of the noodles was a symphony of textures, the delicate strands contrasting beautifully with the chewy clams and the delightful bite of the snails.

But Dì Lan's magic goes beyond just the taste. The portions are generous, ensuring you leave satisfied but not stuffed. The prices are also incredibly reasonable, making it a fantastic option for a budget-friendly yet delicious meal.

Now, it wouldn't be a completely honest review without mentioning a few minor points. The seating is basic, with plastic chairs and tables. While perfectly functional, it might not be ideal for those seeking a fancy dining experience. Additionally, the wait time can be a bit long during peak hours, a testament to its popularity.

However, these minor inconveniences are easily outweighed by the sheer deliciousness and affordability of the food. Mì Ốc Hến Dì Lan is a true gem, offering a taste of Saigon's culinary soul. It's a place where you can savor authentic flavors, generous portions, and a genuine local experience. So, if you're looking for a no-nonsense yet incredibly satisfying bowl of noodles, Dì Lan's is a must-try!

The indoor space is modern and cozy, creating a comfortable atmosphere, while the outdoor area is open and close to nature, perfect for unwinding. It’s truly a great place to spend your time, whether for focus or leisure.

The drinks menu at Gé Cafe is diverse and of high quality, ranging from robust coffee to light and refreshing teas. Accompanying these are freshly made pastries, which pair perfectly with your choice of beverage.

With its combination of a relaxing ambiance, quality menu, and attentive service, Gé Cafe - Đỗ Quang is definitely a must-visit. Whether you’re looking for a productive work session or a friendly gathering, this place delivers. I’ll certainly return to explore more of what it has to offer!

The main idea was to order correctly and not change it or the owner would get mad. But when my friend ordered, she kept changing it. I was about to get mad at my friend, but the owner was very happy to fix it right away 🤣🤣🤣 The bread is also delicious. But I couldn't finish one.

ChIJradg09kodTER7pl-g0HCUjA.text: Long-standing restaurant known for their mì vịt tiềm (braised duck noodle soup). 100.000 vnđ for a bowl is pretty high but the quality justifies it. The rich dark broth was incredibly complex due to the fusion between medicinal herbs, mushrooms, and braised duck flavors. The duck meat was succulent and super tender. I absolutely loved the fermented papaya and the dark sauce that came with the bowl. They provided the much needed switch-up in flavors and textures so you don't get sick of all the meat. I didn't like the veggies that went on top of the noodles because they were bitter.

ChIJh3xVEMwpdTERkeNRISB8ksY.author: Tri Tran
ChIJh3xVEMwpdTERkeNRISB8ksY.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
I had an amazing experience at Bamboo Quán! This spot is conveniently located at 47/24/33, Bùi Đình Túy Alley, District 14, Bình Thạnh, and offers a cozy, comfortable atmosphere. While the place isn’t too large, it feels friendly and welcoming.
The food here is absolutely fantastic! I especially loved the bánh mì chảo and fried rice. Each dish is prepared with care, and the flavors are rich and satisfying. The bánh mì chảo is a standout, with perfectly cooked eggs and meat paired with crispy bread—truly a delightful combination.
Prices are very reasonable, ranging from 1-100,000 VND for a full meal. The service is also excellent, with attentive staff and quick service. The restaurant even offers delivery, which is super convenient if you can’t dine in.
I’ll definitely be returning to Bamboo Quán and recommending it to my friends! It’s one of the best places to eat in Saigon.

ChIJbUyNjrMudTERqgIdNSsFI_o.text:
Not a very easy-to-find place. However, they provide free parking and they do have a really nice area with lots of seats.

About 30,000VND for one bowl, and extra 3,000 VND if you want a slightly bigger one. One huge egg is added for 5,000 VND, but I don’t recommend it. Just have regular Mi Quang is enough.

The portion is very generous for the price. It’s very authentic how they have very little broth :) They also give you extra herbs for no extra cost if you do ask for some.

Nice service. Servers are friendly and welcoming. We don’t have to wait too long for the food, despite the great number of people ordering different dishes.

4 stars because the taste is not good enough, and I’ve had better. If this was my first time trying Mi Quang, I’d have given this place a 5-star :)

ChIJCfRP7YAtdTERndvfmxsDLcs.text: This bakery is Chinese. I have been eating here for 6 years. Every day, I have to have a few boxes of sticky rice, otherwise the kids won't let me in the house. As for me, I have 1 box of sticky rice and 1 loaf of bread. The sticky rice and bread at this shop are the best in Binh Tan area (in my opinion). Sticky rice and bread have 2 prices: 15,000 VND and 20,000 VND. The shop is always crowded but because there are many sellers, the wait is only about 5 minutes. I'm used to eating here so I can't eat at the neighboring shops. They also sell quite delicious wet rice cakes (22,000 VND), and they also sell steamed buns but they are only average.

Best Fried Duck Noodle Soup!
The duck is perfectly fried , crispy on the outside, yet juicy and tender inside, just the way a fried bird should be. The broth is well-seasoned and flavorful. The noodles aren’t the best I’ve had, but they’re still good, slightly chewy and not doughy. The dim sum is solid too, and even better when you consider the modest prices. This is the place that I would frequently return to.

ChIJGwlOaD0vdTERTvaxFiiQsN0.text: High price, good flavor. The traditional Chinese noodles shop with plenty of choices. The duck was not smelly, and shuigao was fully filled with pork and shrimp.

ChIJGwlOaD0vdTERTvaxFiiQsN0.text: Great duck noodles here. Can get it crispy (not in broth) if you prefer. Generous portion of duck, and well seasoned. Broth is great. Wonton soup was also excellent and the shrimp tofu skin with oyster sauce was decent too. Great lunch spot at a reasonable price for the quality. Nice a/c upstairs.

ChIJGwlOaD0vdTERTvaxFiiQsN0.name: places/ChIJGwlOaD0vdTERTvaxFiiQsN0/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURieXNmYVBnEAE
ChIJGwlOaD0vdTERTvaxFiiQsN0.author: C
ChIJGwlOaD0vdTERTvaxFiiQsN0.text:
Nestled in District 5, Mì Vịt Tiềm Thiêm Huy offers a charming culinary experience on the ground floor of its establishment. Despite being non-air conditioned, the restaurant maintains a simple, pleasant environment that adds to its authentic charm.

The menu features a nice range of Vietnamese-Chinese dishes, including dim sum, but the standout is their Mì Vịt Tiềm duck noodle soup. This signature dish features tender, tasty braised duck served with egg noodles in a flavorful, herbal broth, providing an ample serving of delicious duck meat.

Opening early for breakfast at 7:30 am, it’s a great spot for an early start. The prices are reasonable, making it accessible for all. Well regarded and popular with both locals and tourists, Mì Vịt Tiềm Thiêm Huy is a must-visit for anyone seeking a taste of traditional Vietnamese cuisine.

ChIJGwlOaD0vdTERTvaxFiiQsN0.name: places/ChIJGwlOaD0vdTERTvaxFiiQsN0/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUR0MHE2XzhnRRAB

ChIJGwlOaD0vdTERTvaxFiiQsN0.text: Crispy duck with fresh home-made egg noodles. Argubly the BEST SHRIMP HA CAO and open late. This is my Dad's favorite noodle shop. They serve a wide array of Chinese style noodles, soups, wok'd dishes, and dim sum. We have been coming here for over a decade and once you try the food, you and your family will enjoy it for years to come.

However, I find the taste a bit bland for me, I like to eat it a bit stronger with this dish, and the price is a bit expensive for that dish 🥹
The bowl in the picture is Mi rib stewed pork balls and Hu tieu rib stewed pork balls, the total is 166K for 2 bowls and 2 glasses of iced tea

Although I really love the banh mi pha lau here because it's delicious..

ChIJrRq88UUvdTERl1HaNjzXOfs.text: The banh mi was tasty and delicious. Meat was tender and juicy and the bread is crispy. Seller was friendly to show us the types of meat they are selling. We eat the beef and pork banh mi. Will definitely come back to eat again.

ChIJrRq88UUvdTERl1HaNjzXOfs.name: places/ChIJrRq88UUvdTERl1HaNjzXOfs/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURudk1uaF9nRRAB
ChIJrRq88UUvdTERl1HaNjzXOfs.author: Genevieve Vox
ChIJrRq88UUvdTERl1HaNjzXOfs.text:
Their speciality is the bánh mì sườn sụn (pork cartilage ribs bánh mì). Still, they also offer various other options, including grilled beef, beef wrapped in betel leaves, pork cartilage sausage, phá lấu, and meatballs - all cooked over a charcoal grill.

I tried two bánh mì sườn sụn and was pleasantly surprised by their generous size and abundance of cartilage ribs. The bánh mì itself was larger than usual and the price of VND 35.000 was very reasonable. However, the cartilage was a bit tough to chew. The bánh mì came with pickled mustard greens that had a sweet and spicy flavour. The owner also provided a generous bag of flavourful sauce to drizzle on top, enhancing the overall deliciousness of the bánh mì.

ChIJrRq88UUvdTERl1HaNjzXOfs.text: Their speciality is the bánh mì bo la lot - beef wrapped in betel leaves - all cooked over a charcoal grill .The bánh mì came with pickled mustard greens that had a sweet and spicy flavour and finishing it with a flavourful sauce to drizzle on top.

ChIJrRq88UUvdTERl1HaNjzXOfs.text: this has got to be one of HCMC best banh mi ! the secret sauce is stunning, the bo la lot banh mi, pork rib bangh mi is exceptional and the homemade preserved salted vegetables give the banh mi a nice edge to the taste. ChIJ7UKuVbcvdTERyK-SimF1X4k.text: Went to go to another Banh Mi spot which was closed, ended up stumbling across this unassuming place, absolutely delicious fresh bread, eggs, processed meats, onions and cheese all whipped up together, I had two of them, could’ve had 4! ChIJ7UKuVbcvdTERyK-SimF1X4k.name: places/ChIJ7UKuVbcvdTERyK-SimF1X4k/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUREdHRpX01nEAE

ChIJ7UKuVbcvdTERyK-SimF1X4k.text: You know its going to be good when even the locals come here for the brekkie. Love this viet take on a standard western breakfast. The banhmi here is just…. *chef’s kiss* with how crunchy the exterior is but the inside of the bread is fluffy and chewy. Pair that with the runny egg yolk, onions, cheese, and sausage from the pan and u have a flavourful bite of vietnam

ChIJ7UKuVbcvdTERyK-SimF1X4k.name: places/ChIJ7UKuVbcvdTERyK-SimF1X4k/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUROaTd2UllnEAE

ChIJ7UKuVbcvdTERyK-SimF1X4k.text: This is a breakfast like no other and it’ll only cost you 35,000 dong (about $1.50 CAD). Highly recommend for anybody looking for an authentic Vietnamese breakfast of eggs, sausage, fish, cheese and other delicious fixings paired with the softest bread ever.

ChIJgY7CZs0tdTER3x1nmKGagf4.text: Bought 2 boxes of sticky rice and asked for 1 small box and 1 regular box. They brought out 2 boxes and said the top box was small and the bottom was regular. When I got home, they looked at the 2 boxes and they were exactly the same. It's better to say at first they didn't sell the small box so people only bought 1 box. Anyone who buys sticky rice here, remember to check carefully.

ChIJgY7CZs0tdTER3x1nmKGagf4.name: places/ChIJgY7CZs0tdTER3x1nmKGagf4/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNjeDlmaXBRRRAB
ChIJgY7CZs0tdTER3x1nmKGagf4.author: bi tien
ChIJgY7CZs0tdTER3x1nmKGagf4.text: I've been eating at the restaurant since I was in school, it's been 4 years now. Today I spontaneously reviewed the restaurant. Because my house is close, when I'm hungry at night, I come here. I like to eat at Thu SG more than Du Muc because the food here is very delicious. There are many dishes. I often eat roasted chicken sticky rice with banh gio. A box of roasted chicken sticky rice costs 20k-25k depending on the dish. 20k gives me a super big chicken thigh, the roasted chicken broth is a bit sweet, 1 box is enough to make me full. As for banh gio, it's delicious, only 10k for a hot one, inside is minced meat with wood ear mushrooms, 1 quail egg, the cake is also very big, the taste is a bit bland, so it's better to eat it with chili sauce. The bread here is crispy, the meat and other ingredients are also delicious. In addition, the restaurant also has wontons, the price is about 3k/piece but the quality is very good, the wontons are very big. This restaurant is always my late night hunger pang saver.

ChIJgY7CZs0tdTER3x1nmKGagf4.name: places/ChIJgY7CZs0tdTER3x1nmKGagf4/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUQ3ckpuLVpREAE

ChIJa7E69BMtdTERiUngxofCXLM.text: Very delicious, been there for a long time, had to wait in line but still fast

ChIJa7E69BMtdTERiUngxofCXLM.text: I have been buying here occasionally for more than ten years now, not because it is delicious but because it is close to home, but the more I feel the attitude of the staff here is getting worse, I don't understand why? ChIJa7E69BMtdTERiUngxofCXLM.name: places/ChIJa7E69BMtdTERiUngxofCXLM/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUQzbW92RmxBRRAB
ChIJa7E69BMtdTERiUngxofCXLM.author: Long Đỗ
ChIJa7E69BMtdTERiUngxofCXLM.text:
The shop sells all kinds of breakfast foods such as bread, dumplings, sticky rice... all 3 dishes are delicious and clean. They sell very well, in the morning people line up to buy them in a long, orderly line. 

The shop has several branches scattered around, you can also order by phone. 

A few days ago I bought dumplings, today I tried sticky rice with chicken pate. The sticky rice is soft, a bit hard. The chicken is marinated in strong soy sauce, delicious and fragrant, but the texture is a bit dry, still edible; if there were crispy chicken skin or a young egg, it would be perfect, really. I ate the pate with it so the smell was too overwhelming, I couldn't feel the flavor clearly, but overall it was fatty and delicious. 

Reasonable price, have been in business for a long time so have a certain reputation. Only sell takeout, no place to sit down. Convenient payment by bank transfer, momo.

ChIJJ9GeS38tdTERsjEGhh9Ib1w.name: places/ChIJJ9GeS38tdTERsjEGhh9Ib1w/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xkWWExUnFVbGhwY0c1WmVYUlVWMDB4WjBSRWJWRRAB
ChIJJ9GeS38tdTERsjEGhh9Ib1w.author: Anton Kunin
ChIJJ9GeS38tdTERsjEGhh9Ib1w.text: I have finally found a place that serves "banh mi" with beef. And I mean genuine beef. Very rare in Vietnam! So, I salute them. Well done! It would be a pleasure to come again if I'm in Binh Tan again.

ChIJJ9GeS38tdTERsjEGhh9Ib1w.name: places/ChIJJ9GeS38tdTERsjEGhh9Ib1w/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2pSSlQxWTRjRTlzYWxaYU1XVkpPVEUzU0MxSE5GRRAB
ChIJJ9GeS38tdTERsjEGhh9Ib1w.author: Trần Tố Tố

ChIJtVlD9wgvdTERP3sGNcdAeHs.text:
The Shop got our attention after seeing an incredibly long queue that went on for ages. Every morning. It just had to be great, we thought.

Luckily for us, the long queue in the morning is pretty much all delivery drivers so we were able to order right next to them immediately.

You have a choice between a banh mi or s special banh mi. Lets be honest, who would even consider not going special. We chose the small version and took a seat inside. The food arrived before we could sit down. Incredibly fast. You get many side ingredients like pickles, Chili, cilantro & chives.

Although supposedly small we barely finished it. The sandwhich was packed to the brim. Whatever you expect in a banh mi volume wise, double it. So flavourfull and filling. A great place to start your day.

ChIJtVlD9wgvdTERP3sGNcdAeHs.text:
I have been a long-time fan of Banh Mi Ba Huynh and have always told my friends how good the banh mi here is. Sadly, the banh mi we bought on Sunday 18/11, made us very ill. My friend noticed that the butter cream in her banh mi smelled a bit off but didn’t think much of it. Two hours later, she developed the worst food poisoning of her life, with ongoing diarrhoea and vomiting. It is now day 2, and her symptoms have yet to subside. (I also have some diarrhoea just not as bad). We have had to cancel our plans because of this, and it has ruined the rest of our holiday. We are so, so disappointed, and we will never come back again.

P.S. It definitely could not have been anything else that caused the food poisoning, because we had bun bò Hue at an indoor restaurant (Bun Bo Hue Vy Da) with boiled vegetables and herbs, and nothing else until the banh mi.

ChIJGW7y3h0vdTERtzgoGRdR1CI.text:
Bánh mì Hanoi is one of the go-to places for bánh mì lovers in Saigon. The shop is located on Nguyễn Thiện Thuật street, a busy and lively area in quân 3. The shop is clean and spacious, with friendly staff and fast service. You can order your bánh mì to go or sit down and enjoy it with a cup of coffee or tea.

The bánh mì here is delicious and authentic, with a variety of fillings to choose from. You can have the classic bánh mì thịt (meat), bánh mì pate (pate), bánh mì trứng (egg), or try something different like bánh mì há cảo xíu mại (dumplings and meatballs). The bread is crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, the meat is tender and flavorful, the pate is rich and creamy, and the vegetables are fresh and crunchy. The shop also offers some sauces and condiments to spice up your bánh mì, such as chili sauce, soy sauce, or mayonnaise.

If you are looking for a satisfying and tasty bánh mì experience in quân 3, you should definitely check out Bánh mì Hanoi. It is a place that will make you fall in love with bánh mì all over again.

ChIJEZ_N7RksdTERjHaEDMSJvdA.text:
Follow @breadgyeats for more food pics!

The sinking feeling pulling up to a shuttered restaurant, as Google Maps lied to you about their opening hours. Luckily, a nearby noodle shop packed with locals came to save the meal with their familiar tasting bowls of rice noodles in a rich, sweet pork broth, with a mix of soft rice noodles contrasting the springy wheat noodles. Decorated with a bit of every topping they offer, there's no FOMO here. While my gluttonous palate prefers the giant HK-style wontons packed with shrimp, these humble wontons are delightful bites of tiny pork filling encased in a thin wrapper. Seemed only in Vietnam, the steamed siu mai was like a pork meatball in a slightly spicy and tangy sauce.

🥢: Special Rice Noodles, Wontons, Steamed Siu Mai, Ha Cao

ChIJT8RlgfkudTERWP__StT66QY.text: Meatballs 20k, meatballs with pork skin 25k. The bread here is delicious, the bread is from a good place, the meatballs are also quite okay. The shop is friendly.

ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok.name: places/ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2pkWFdITm5UVlpCVkhWT2JVdDNSV05IVHpsQ1drRRAB
ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok.author: Ray Tan
ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok.text: My fav duck noodles stall in District 5. I like the herbal duck leg noodles with mushrooms (Vnd147k). The duck leg is nicely braised. Flavorful and meat is almost fall off the bone. The broth is herbalicious while not too overpowering and you can taste hints of the mushrooms. I like the broth so much i almost drank all of it. The egg noodles which i heard is handmade is relatively chewy as well. The only drawback here is the price. For Vnd147k it’s almost a luxury to the locals. I wished it could be more affordable.

ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok.name: places/ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25wTldrWkJSbkpxVGtaWWJ6aGpha1pRVTFNNFdXYxAB
ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok.author: Kwan
ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok.text:
Excellent noodles done to perfection, the flavor on the duck leg goes well and through but some parts can be alittle tough. Its a big leg.
The soup is intense but its a flavor profile I'm personally not used to for a broth.

Need to try their dry noodles and fried duck next time

ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok.name: places/ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUN5dWJIWHNBRRAB
ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok.author: Nam Luu
ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok.text:
If you just want legit egg noodles, Hai Ky makes their own fresh in-house. When I say, "house" I mean it.

We've been coming here for years and nothing changes. There's always an older person perusing the Chinese newspapers. The food is always delicious, the xi quach has tons of tendon and meat falling off the bone... The broth is rich with just enough fat to please. The garlic oil and tiny succulent cubes of fried pork fat add even more richness to every bite.

Start with a plate of fried wontons... then your choice of noodle soup (char siu, roast chicken, duck, wonton and more!) and chase it all with gobs of tendon and tender pork.

This is my choice for egg noodle soup or dry egg noodles. It is hands down a Ho Chi Minh staple. If you do not visit, you're missing the yummiest bowl of Chinese style egg noodles in town.

ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok.name: places/ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNkaTRUckNREAE

ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok.text: Open from 11am until night. Price is pretty higher as well as the quality of foods. Fast service with welcoming staffs. Must try when in District 5.

ChIJPxE1Df0udTERxe0Ah8Fdzok.text:
True stewed duck with herb serve with egg noodles soup.
Best in town, for a price thou.
The pickle papaya is perfect compliment for the soup.
The soup itself is mildly sweet with the taste of Chinese herbs and good balance...
I recommend this noodles shop... $$$

ChIJ_7wAIzwvdTERlt_MdVf7a8M.text:

Surprisingly, the quality of Banh Mi of this stall is so nice and the price is almost half. Just 40k. The famous stall selling 73k...

The location of this stall is just located beside the roundaabout and its just a small stall.
Definitely worth a try if you looking for banh mi midnight.
Good job, boss.

ChIJc_0a0gwvdTERYbC11XMP5Vo.text:
Hey shop, it's only 300m from my company but the food is quite good. I ordered rice paper dipping, rolling and mixing. I think rolling is the best, delicious and easy to eat. The taste is also okay, the eggs are fresh and not stale. 
Mixed rice paper has the same taste, simple toppings like dried chicken, dried beef, eggs with peanuts, Vietnamese coriander, with mango is even better. 
The dipping sauce of the rice paper is a bit sweet, the rice paper is not salty. Suggest the restaurant should give a cup so that if you don't finish it, it's easier to take it home than to eat it.

ChIJc_0a0gwvdTERYbC11XMP5Vo.text: When I went to buy it, I was very careful to ask for the dipping sauce to be non-spicy! When I received the product, I took it out to check and asked again if it was non-spicy and had no chili! But the chili sauce bag was bright red! It didn't have that before! Now I'm lazy and just mix one type and sell it to deceive customers! The shop has been around for probably 7-8 years, but now business is so bad! I'll never come back!

ChIJQed6WLgvdTERUrESgbM1mFo.text: Must have eaten here far too many times because it is one of the best and most convenient ramen spot. It is at the edge of J town, friendly crew manning the shop, noodles are cooked upon ordering. Beer is always cold, there seems like always something interesting going on outside the window if you enjoy people watching.

ChIJQed6WLgvdTERUrESgbM1mFo.name: places/ChIJQed6WLgvdTERUrESgbM1mFo/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2w5SlpUZHJOMlo2WkVVd2RtRnFOblZpYVVWR2RVRRAB
ChIJQed6WLgvdTERUrESgbM1mFo.author: Ming Shen Tham
ChIJQed6WLgvdTERUrESgbM1mFo.text:
Tried the shrimp cappuccino ramen here and it turned out to be a pretty enjoyable bowl. The broth was flavourful, though I personally would’ve liked the shrimp taste to be a bit stronger to really stand out.
The grilled prawn that came with the ramen was delicious — nicely charred and full of flavour. Surprisingly, the alfalfa sprouts worked really well in the dish, adding a refreshing crunch that balanced out the richness of the broth.
The char siew was another highlight, with that charred, smoky edge that gave it depth and made it very satisfying.
Overall, a solid bowl of ramen with some interesting touches — worth a try if you’re looking for something a little different from the usual.

ChIJQed6WLgvdTERUrESgbM1mFo.name: places/ChIJQed6WLgvdTERUrESgbM1mFo/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2kxelgyWmZWMVEwTFdWWWFqaExMV1p2VDJSMFNWRRAB
ChIJQed6WLgvdTERUrESgbM1mFo.author: Bích Ngọc Nguyễn Thị
ChIJQed6WLgvdTERUrESgbM1mFo.text:
I had a dinner here once, the cappucino ramen had a very simple taste, just like water with salt and some fat. I don't see the special in it. The ingredients didn’t well put together, I’ve had more complex tasting ramen so many times before so this is a big NO for me. My friend’s dish is also sadly fatty spicy and boring, even though it’s pricey.
The fried chicken is another sad story, it’s sweet outside (which is not my personal preferences), it was over-heated so it dried and hard a bit, and the sauce is not how it should taste, I’ve eaten this and made it on my own so I know exactly how It should be, it lacked the sour and salt as well. I don't really understand why this place has so many guests! The atmosphere is stuffy and hot.
Other than that, the waiters are really kind. They helped me walk my motorbike when I got in, but not when I left 💁 Maybe not kind enough I guess?!
Eventually, both me and my friend had a diarrhoea after, but maybe that’s just us.
Highly rcm for someone wants to explore new places.

ChIJ11KUPvctdTERNgrIET2KCX0.text:
The food is delicious. But:

I think you guys will lose a lot of customers because of the free iced tea in the corner.

This morning, K and his wife went with their little baby, the beef pan was hot so they couldn't go get it, they asked the uniformed staff to get the iced tea for them, and I also asked them to get it for me. They followed the "rules" 1,2, the rule here is that if you want it, you have to come get it yourself because the iced tea is free.

For a restaurant, I think we shouldn't be too rigid in some cases. Maybe the staff didn't handle it well or weren't trained. I'm giving constructive feedback. I hope the restaurant will make timely adjustments in the future.

ChIJH1WlOAAvdTERX-BB91TLlxY.author: Hà Trang Minh (Bryan Trang)
ChIJH1WlOAAvdTERX-BB91TLlxY.text:
Nestled on Bùi Thị Xuân Street in District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, the Mì Tàu Xì restaurant is a culinary landmark celebrated for its iconic mì tàu xì khô (dry Chinese-style noodles), a true specialty that defines Saigon’s street food culture. This cozy, no-frills eatery draws crowds with its signature dish: golden, chewy noodles tossed in a rich, savory blend of fermented black bean sauce (tàu xì), topped with tender char siu pork, crisp vegetables, and crunchy fried shallots. The dish’s bold, umami-packed flavor and perfect texture make it a must-try for noodle lovers.
The restaurant’s open-air setup buzzes with the energy of sizzling woks and fragrant aromas, offering an authentic taste of Vietnam’s Chinese-influenced cuisine. Each plate is crafted with fresh, high-quality ingredients, ensuring every bite is a delight. Beyond the famed mì tàu xì khô, the menu includes variations with beef, chicken, or seafood, but the dry noodles steal the show. Affordable prices, quick service, and a welcoming vibe make it a favorite for locals and visitors. For a quintessential Saigon food experience, this Bùi Thị Xuân gem is unbeatable.

ChIJBcYmsj8vdTERdorXln76jI4.text:
This was my first meat during my recent trip to Vietnam via landing in HCMC. Good decision as this really made me full!

I ordered the vegan premium banh mi and also the black sugar bubble nut milk tea.

The banh mi was the thickest, most filling and largest one I had throughout my entire trip! Had vegan meat, tofu, lettuce, basil, tomatoes. Really good banh mi, and definitely one of the best places to get vegan banh mi in the city! Although it is a bit more ‘pricier’ than other vegan banh mi in the city/the standard price in general. But still worth it.

The bubble tea I had was ok, but as dairy-free option isn’t widely available for bubble tea (I think), it’s great to find a vegan option here. I found the tapioca pearls to be a bit medium hard than chewy and soft.

Seating was mostly indoors. Suitable for 1-3 people in a group.

ChIJTS87G28pdTERdyKrALVtLnI.name: places/ChIJTS87G28pdTERdyKrALVtLnI/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNqM3NtVlB3EAE
ChIJTS87G28pdTERdyKrALVtLnI.author: Thanh Hảo Lê
ChIJTS87G28pdTERdyKrALVtLnI.text:
Nestled in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City, Bánh mì pate ngon - Hoàng Oanh Cây Nhãn is a haven for banh mi enthusiasts. With its humble storefront and unassuming décor, this hidden gem has been serving up mouthwatering banh mi for over 40 years.

A Symphony of Flavors

The star of the show at Bánh mì pate ngon is undoubtedly the banh mi pate. The pate, made with a secret family recipe, is rich, creamy, and bursting with flavor. It's perfectly complemented by the crispy baguette, fresh vegetables, and a tangy cilantro sauce. Each bite is an explosion of textures and tastes that will leave you wanting more.

Beyond the Pate

While the banh mi pate is the undisputed champion, Bánh mì pate ngon also offers a variety of other delectable banh mi options. The banh mi thit nuong (grilled pork banh mi) is a crowd favorite, with its tender, flavorful pork and a slightly sweet marinade. For those seeking a vegetarian option, the banh mi chay (vegetarian banh mi) is a delightful surprise, packed with fresh veggies and a savory tofu filling.

A Local Gem

Bánh mì pate ngon is more than just a restaurant; it's a beloved local institution. The friendly staff and welcoming atmosphere make you feel right at home, and the prices are incredibly affordable. It's no wonder that Bánh mì pate ngon has been a neighborhood staple for decades.

A Must-Visit for Banh Mi Lovers

If you're a banh mi aficionado, Bánh mì pate ngon is an absolute must-visit. With its exceptional banh mi, charming ambiance, and affordable prices, it's a true gem of Ho Chi Minh City's culinary scene. So, grab your friends or family and head over to Bánh mì pate ngon for a taste of authentic Vietnamese banh mi that will tantalize your taste buds and leave you with lasting memories.

Additional Tips:

Be prepared for a bit of a wait, especially during peak hours. The banh mi is made fresh to order, and it's worth the wait.
If you're feeling adventurous, try the banh mi dac biet (special banh mi). It's a loaded creation with a variety of meats, veggies, and sauces.
Don't forget to try the homemade chili sauce. It's the perfect condiment to add a bit of spice to your banh mi.
I hope this review has given you a taste of what makes Bánh mì pate ngon - Hoàng Oanh Cây Nhãn so special. Whether you're a local or just visiting Ho Chi Minh City, I highly recommend checking it out. You won't be disappointed!

ChIJvRSrfHIpdTERJY7NSaP8OWE.author: Julia Kooper
ChIJvRSrfHIpdTERJY7NSaP8OWE.text:
A Disappointing Mi Quang Experience

I’ve tried Mi Quang in several places around Vietnam and usually enjoy this iconic dish, but unfortunately, this was the worst experience I’ve had. The broth lacked flavor, the noodles were overcooked and mushy, and the chicken was tough, dry, and clearly inedible. To make things worse, the dish was served with old chicken skin that had an unpleasant smell and texture.

On top of the poor food quality, the service was equally disappointing. They asked me to pay before I had even requested the bill, which felt very unprofessional and uncomfortable. Additionally, they didn’t serve the free iced tea that’s typically expected in many restaurants here—I only got it after specifically asking for it.

Overall, this place failed to deliver both in taste and service. I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone looking for an authentic and enjoyable Mi Quang experience.

ChIJZV4BB3ApdTER8uut1Mv_9VM.text:
Donno about other reviews but food is indeed authentic. Prepare to have your taste buds and satisfaction fulfilled as you are blown away by how appetising the servings are.

The owner was wonderfully bright and so too were the staff as friendly.

Would say this place is only my list of "highly recommends", dare I say even on my "must-go's", for anyone coming to visit Vietnam whether for a short trip or even as a local/native to the area. You just can't go wrong here.

Tips of the natives: for any of the "my quang" noodles (and yes I just said Quang province noodles noodles), they are best served with a plentiful serving of vegetables and a few pieces crackers crunched up into thumbed sized pieces. A rule of thumb (badumtss) is to have a small plate of vegetables with one bowl of noodles.

ChIJ05ZiIgApdTERyzTmSbQepZg.author: Minh Nguyễn Anh
ChIJ05ZiIgApdTERyzTmSbQepZg.text:
The name of the restaurant is “harsh” but the food is “extremely delicious”! 
The first time I heard the name “Revenge Noodles” I was curious, when I tried it I was “shocked” because it was so delicious! The mixed noodles are super flavorful, the noodles are chewy and delicious, not mushy or dry. The sauce is both salty and spicy, stimulating the taste buds. Especially, there are a lot of toppings – char siu, soft-boiled eggs, wontons, minced meat, sausage, crispy fried pork skin… you can’t finish eating them all! 

The restaurant space is small but clean, with its own style, very youthful and liberal. The staff is cute, serves quickly and very attentively. The menu is also diverse, in addition to mixed noodles, there are also noodle soup, fried buns, wontons, lemongrass and lime chicken feet which are also extremely delicious. 

The price is very reasonable for the quality – one bowl is enough to fill you up for the whole day. It is the type of restaurant that “gives energy” to tired days. 

Strongly recommended for those who love mixed noodles and like to try quality – unique – strange places to eat!

ChIJ05ZiIgApdTERyzTmSbQepZg.name: places/ChIJ05ZiIgApdTERyzTmSbQepZg/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VKV25tdFRMbGZ1SVJ3EAE
ChIJ05ZiIgApdTERyzTmSbQepZg.author: Duck Fatty (Review)
ChIJ05ZiIgApdTERyzTmSbQepZg.text:
📷 About transportation: the restaurant is quite easy to find, highly recognizable, right in front, convenient to visit.
📷 About space:
Open space, in front of a house.
The distance between tables is a bit small because the yard is not wide.
1 table vs 1 tray, 2 soup chairs.
📷 About service:
There are 2 pieces of paper to choose the request for noodles, the back is a fun dice game, also a membership registration (as in the photo I took).
The noodle counter is quite creative, choose what you eat and drink.
📷 About drinks: I ordered iced tea, it took a while to come out, the taste is quite good.
📷 About food:
Delicious noodles, egg topping is a bit runny, minced meat is quite salty.
The soup is delicious, choose sweet and it is really sweet.
📷 About price:
Depending on the noodles you choose, the price will change, if you want to save money, choose Hao Hao, Indomie; or if you want to eat more, choose Korean noodles.
⚖️ Overall rating:
In general, the restaurant is okay, not too excellent, I was impressed by the name of the restaurant so I stopped by to try it.
Still enough to make me want to come back next time.
SUGGESTION: THERE ARE A LOT OF MOSQUITOES, OWNER, PLEASE GIVE ME A PIECE OF MOSQUITO INCENSE!!!
⭐️ Rating: 7.5/10 points.

Location: the restaurant is located near the 208 Ng Gia Tri apartment building, past the intersection of Ng Gia Tri and Ung Van Khiem, quite easy to find because the restaurant has a prominent red cart and the words "Revenge of Life" are quite large 😄
The restaurant follows the youth trend in choosing noodles and toppings (eggs, sausages, beef, etc.)
The noodles are also quite diverse such as Hao Hao, Korean spicy noodles, Indomie noodles... priced from 10-35k/package
When you arrive at the restaurant, they will give you a piece of paper to choose general information such as spicy/sauce/green onions... then go to the cart to choose noodles and toppings.
The experience is quite good, suitable for young students.
However, I find the general price a bit higher.
You can come to experience and try it, it's quite good, when you crave mixed noodles, this is also a reasonable place.

The food is rich, but I heard the table next to me said it was a bit salty so you can consider it according to your taste.

The menu is diverse: from noodles, salads, rolls to hot pots, all are available. The price is super reasonable, I ordered 3 dishes as shown in the picture (mixed jackfruit, banh loc, mixed Quang noodles) and it only cost about 155k.

Personal feelings:
- Mixed jackfruit: delicious, harmonious flavor, especially not too much onion like many other restaurants in the Central region.
- Banh loc: okay to eat, just a little bit mushy in the dough.
- Mixed Quang noodles: seems to be the signature dish here, worth trying

The staff is nice, polite and enthusiastic. The restaurant is clean, airy, feels comfortable, and the dishes are served quite quickly

Will come back again!

ChIJj-mrna0pdTERRM7ABrIWXJw.text:
This noodle, pasta, and rice noodle shop is an ideal destination for those looking for a delicious, cheap, and quality late-night meal. With an extremely reasonable price of only 25,000 - 30,000 VND, the shop is not only attractive because of the price but also because of the diversity in the menu. Here, you can enjoy all the toppings such as soft stewed bones, chewy ham, fatty intestines, crispy pork skin, fragrant quail eggs, flavorful lean meat, delicious beef balls, and smooth blood. 

The noodles or noodles at the shop are always cooked just right, keeping the toughness and smoothness. In particular, the broth is clear and sweet, combined with the rich flavor of fried onions and fresh vegetables. Each dish is presented very neatly and hygienically, creating a feeling of satisfaction from the first look. 

The shop opens in the evening, very suitable for those who are busy during the day. The space of the restaurant is simple with plastic tables and chairs but clean, creating a comfortable feeling. ChIJj-mrna0pdTERRM7ABrIWXJw.text:
The restaurant is located in an alley, from Binh Trieu bridge in the direction of Binh Thanh to Thu Duc, there will be a noodle sign 50m into it. 

The restaurant sells cheap noodle soup, the price is about the same as other noodle soup carts, but the quality feels much better. The broth is sweet and clear, not too MSG-intoxicated, the beef balls are also normal, not outstanding, but in return, the meat and vegetables are plentiful enough to fill you up. 

If you consider the cheap noodle soup shops on the sidewalk that can be delicious around the Binh Loi bridge roundabout, then in addition to the restaurant near Hiep Binh Chanh ward police station, you can consider this place to eat. 

The price I ordered for the full portion with ham was 35k, free self-service iced tea.

ChIJcZcdkzUvdTERXsiSawzxONc.author: Phuong Joey Nguyen
ChIJcZcdkzUvdTERXsiSawzxONc.text:
Stepping into Cơm Xưa felt like a warm embrace from home. The aroma alone, a delicate dance of simmering broth, fragrant herbs, and that unmistakable hint of fish sauce, instantly planted me right back in the heart of Hanoi. There's a certain warmth and unpretentious deliciousness that defines Northern Vietnamese home cooking, and my recent experience with this restaurant perfectly embodied that. It wasn't about fancy presentation or elaborate techniques; it was about honest flavors, fresh ingredients, and the kind of food that feels like a hug from the inside out.

Accompanying their signature slow braised fish (cá kho) was a simple yet delightful stir-fried morning glory with garlic (rau muống xào tỏi). The vibrant green stalks were crisp-tender, their mild sweetness perfectly complemented by the pungent aroma and flavor of fresh garlic. It was a reminder that even the simplest vegetables can be transformed into something truly satisfying.

A bowl of canh chua (sour soup), likely with fish or shrimp, offered a refreshing counterpoint. The tangy broth, balanced with a hint of sweetness and the fresh flavors of herbs and vegetables, cleansed the palate and added a bright note to the meal. It was the kind of soup that felt both nourishing and invigorating.

But my journey didn't end there. Their "bún chả" was another standout. The grilled pork patties, with their slightly charred edges and sweet-savory marinade, were divine. Dipping them into the sauce, perfectly balanced with its sweet, sour, salty, and spicy notes, alongside a generous portion of fresh vermicelli noodles and crisp greens, was pure Hanoian bliss. It evoked memories of lively street-side eateries, the sizzle of the grill, and the happy chatter of locals.

Even the smaller details resonated. The slightly chipped ceramic bowls, the clinking of glasses filled with "trà đá", and the friendly, unhurried service all contributed to an atmosphere that felt authentically Hanoian, not just a mere imitation.

What truly stood out was the feeling of being welcomed into someone's home, even if it wasn't literally the case. There was an authenticity in the flavors, a sense that these were recipes passed down through generations, cooked with love and without pretense. The focus was on the quality of the ingredients and the harmony of tastes, rather than elaborate garnishes or trendy presentations.

This experience wasn't just about eating; it was about connecting with a culinary tradition that values simplicity, freshness, and the joy of sharing a meal. If you have the opportunity to savor Northern Vietnamese home-cooked food, embrace it. It's a taste of genuine warmth and a true reflection of the region's culinary heart. It’s the kind of food that nourishes not just the body, but also the soul.

ChIJQ8w0jrQodTERWKKe4Kp8SOc.text: Another great restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City. It was a little bit difficult to find the place, but once we did we were very happy. The place is an old converted house that is absolutely beautiful. The service is top notch and they make themselves very accessible without hovering and polite at all times. All of the food on the menu looked great, but we opted for the set lunch menu at 150K VND, with 3 courses. We added a fresh spring roll on top of this as an appetizer since we love the fresh spring rolls in Vietnam. Nothing disappointed and there was more than enough food. The two three course lunches along with the fresh spring rolls, 2 tiger beers, and a ice tea came to 555K Dong. I would highly recommend this place and will certainly come back if I get a chance.

ChIJE45lDqMpdTERxgAGjIArBOU.text:
I just had lunch at the restaurant and was really satisfied with the space and the quality of the food.
🏠 About the space:
The restaurant is airy, clean, the seats are neat, the tables and chairs are cleaned carefully. There are fans and tissues. Not too crowded, so the feeling of eating on the spot is comfortable, not constrained.
🍚 About the food:
I ordered [for example: grilled ribs rice + sour soup] - the rice was served hot, the grilled meat was fragrant, soft, well-marinated, not dry. The sour soup was cooked lightly, with lots of vegetables, not too sour - very suitable for the taste. In addition, there are also stir-fried vegetables, pickles to eat with rice, very delicious.
It feels like eating at home but more neat and convenient.
💁‍♀️ Service:
The owner (or staff) is enthusiastic, cute, serves dishes quickly, does not keep customers waiting long. If you need to change the side dish, you can ask for support right away.
💸 Price: From 35k–45k/portion, full, worth the money, with free iced tea (if available), very suitable for office workers.

ChIJKwuYRgApdTERgOPw9hd9e4I.text:
My younger brother and I went to eat at the restaurant at 9am. There was no one there, just the two of us, and we ordered two bowls of chicken vermicelli, because today there were no meatballs.
The restaurant used instant vermicelli to cook and serve customers. The chicken in the bowl was not known to be frozen shredded chicken or chicken floss; the meat was very loose and not fresh at all. The round balls in the picture were frozen shrimp and crab balls; the taste was worse than frozen crab sticks or shrimp balls bought at the supermarket.
In short, these were the two worst bowls of chicken vermicelli I have ever eaten. The price was 30k/bowl, not cheap at all compared to the general level, let alone compared to the ingredients. I respectfully request the restaurant owner to review the way they cook and serve customers, otherwise sooner or later the restaurant will have to close. No one wants to eat at a restaurant that cooks poorly, uses cheap ingredients, and looks down on customers like that.

ChIJTTM953vXdDERvfsNU0VFJ9I.text:
The restaurant looks quite nice from the outside, but the service should be reviewed. 
The other day my group went to eat at this restaurant and one of our group members ate a piece of personal tape in a plate of stir-fried chicken gizzards with squash (there was proper evidence) and I called the manager out to talk to him, but he refused to come out and of course, there was no solution nor an apology to my customers. I don't know if it's because of poor management or because the restaurant's culture of treating customers like that is so familiar or what, but seeing the manager's face is really boring. 
Because no one in my group has the habit of posting on Facebook and doesn't want to make a big deal out of it, we just paid and left, otherwise if we met other people, they might yell at us. 
If I could, I wouldn't give any stars. The restaurant is rude.

ChIJL_kCXgDZdDER6aBEeeQl5T8.text: This restaurant is close to home. The prices are very reasonable, the owner is very dedicated to the restaurant. At first, I didn't pay much attention when I passed by, but because I saw a lot of people coming, I decided to try it out, and it became my regular restaurant. Regarding the food, it's probably due to the demand of the drivers and workers nearby, so the dishes are quite varied, with slight changes every day. I wish the restaurant could change the menu more often. However, the dishes are new, hot, and delicious every day. When eaten with raw vegetables, the rice is very delicious because it's clean. The price is surprisingly good. The owner and the shop assistants are quite cute. I will come back often. The food is diverse and always changes every day, the price is reasonable.

ChIJL_kCXgDZdDER6aBEeeQl5T8.name: places/ChIJL_kCXgDZdDER6aBEeeQl5T8/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTUN3XzY2OXZ3RRAB

Then the owner came out with a broom and swept in front of me, saying how could I eat so dirty? This was the first time someone said that to my face. I ate and thought it was ok so I turned around and drove 2km. But when I heard that, I broke up with them. I also work in the service industry but I've never commented on anyone like that before. This time I'm so frustrated that I'm here to say it.

ChIJvRwWWI8pdTERQdiiXVQIlIE.author: ekkun
ChIJvRwWWI8pdTERQdiiXVQIlIE.text: Apparently, this round banh mi has been famous in Go Vap for quite some time for its rich fillings. The round baguette has a crunchy texture with a buttery aroma, and the sweetness of the flour spreads the more you chew it. The filling is a classic style of pate, meat, crisp vegetables, and the tartness of raw vinegar. Lately, the more Jiro-style banh mi has become popular, but this simplicity is particularly appealing. And since this shop seems to specialize in chicken, I bought some Ko Ga Kai La Train (chicken jerky with lemongrass) as a souvenir, which was also a great choice! I was so hooked that it seemed like they even calculated how it would pair with beer.

ChIJ0fjpWwEpdTERDls1sIJSsCI.text: The roasted pork sandwiches here were pretty good. The pork skin was crispy and the meat was not too fatty. Once the sandwich was stuffed with everything, they placed it in a little grilled (like panini) to make the bread hot and crispy outside. Since they made their own breads there, you always have new and fresh breads. Price is very cheap $28,000vnd for a sandwich.  I have not tried the pork and steam rice noodle yet. I recommend this place.

ChIJ7SUnJAAzdTERYgMLKhVHfvk.text:
A familiar restaurant for inter-provincial buses – Delicious, fast, convenient!
The restaurant is a familiar stop for many buses going to provinces about 150 km from Ho Chi Minh City, such as Vinh Long, Tien Giang, Ben Tre, Dong Thap. The reason is simple: after eating here, you can go straight home without stopping again!
The highlight is grilled pork rice vermicelli – crispy, fragrant roasted pork skin, served with hot grilled pork rice vermicelli, very delicious. In addition, there are grilled pork pieces, roasted duck, and especially grilled pork bread for only 25,000 VND – quick, filling, ideal for those who need to fill their stomachs before going home to eat their mother's cooking.
Fast service, clean space, suitable for both drivers and passengers to take a short rest before continuing the journey.

ChIJ1fADL3AvdTERFEgOgUc0oA0.author: Tuan Nguyen
ChIJ1fADL3AvdTERFEgOgUc0oA0.text:
The sandwich cart has been in operation for decades, is very popular and famous at Xom Chieu night market. It is most famous for its Pha Lau sandwich, and also sells delicious vegetarian sandwiches and meat sandwiches. 

The exact address is also attached to the name on the signboard, Banh Mi 181 Xom Chieu. 

The shop only sells from noon to late at night, sometimes after 11pm the sandwich cart is still bustling with customers. 

Although crowded, the sandwiches are made very quickly so customers don't have to wait long. The owner and staff are probably all the same person. Everyone is very friendly and hospitable. 

I bought all 3 types of sandwiches sold here. According to the picture I took, the smallest one (wrapped in colored paper) is vegetarian sandwich for 18k, the loaf wrapped in white paper is meat sandwich for 22k and finally the largest loaf wrapped in nylon is Pha Lau sandwich for 25k. 

I bought it home and found it unusually heavy, so I happily weighed it, but I didn't mean anything by it. The vegetarian sandwich weighed 177g. I was quite surprised by the weight of the two larger sandwiches, the meat sandwich was 282g and the stewed offal was 332g. 

- The meat sandwich had a rather fatty butter taste, the other ingredients were thinly sliced ​​and quite a lot compared to the price of 22k, the taste was quite normal because I knew it wasn't the strong point of this sandwich shop. But it tasted okay, and the price was cheap too. 

- I found the vegetarian sandwich to be very delicious, with vegetarian ingredients that looked like real meat, including vegetarian pate, vegetarian butter, vegetarian sausage, vegetarian shredded pork made from mushroom stems and crispy fried vegetarian anchovies. The sandwich was made by a vegetarian woman in the family, so everyone could rest assured that no meat was mixed in. 

- The stewed offal signature sandwich of the 181 Xom Chieu sandwich cart. The first time I ate it, it was delicious and impressive, but today when I bought it, the filling of my sandwich was uneven, only pig ears and duck eggs. The flavor was still delicious, still had the divine stew sauce, but the ingredients were weird, it should have had liver, stomach, and tongue added evenly for the sandwich to be more delicious.

ChIJQzKlyWsvdTERlubridzXQhs.author: Thanh Hảo Lê
ChIJQzKlyWsvdTERlubridzXQhs.text:
District 4 in Ho Chi Minh City is a whirlwind! Scooters zip past you on narrow streets, shop signs fight for attention with a dizzying array of colors, and the air thrums with a constant hum. It's exhilarating and a little overwhelming.

Seeking refuge from the sensory overload, I stumbled upon Bánh Mì Lúa, a tiny stall tucked away on a side street.  The woman running it greeted me with a warm smile that instantly calmed the chaos around me.  Though my Vietnamese is limited, we managed to communicate through a mix of hand gestures and laughter.

I opted for the classic Bánh Mì, and let me tell you, it was phenomenal! The bread was crusty on the outside and soft on the inside, the perfect vessel for the explosion of flavors within.  Tender slices of pate mingled with pickled vegetables, fresh herbs, and a touch of chili sauce. Each bite was a party in my mouth!

Bánh Mì Lúa might be a small stall, but it's a giant when it comes to flavor and hospitality. It was the perfect antidote to the bustling streets of District 4, and a delicious reminder of the warmth you can find in the most unexpected places.

ChIJx-kHUkkpdTERKmt5JVPTcuQ.text: This bánh xèo is truly a local gem! I recommend going at night if you don’t want to get overwhelmed by the heat. The bánh xèo and herbs are fresh and delicious, and cooked to order, so you do have to wait, but they’re extremely quick. Since this is a spot that caters to locals, the menu is completely in Vietnamese. Prepare accordingly! Otherwise they are very friendly and accommodating. The bánh xèo tasted like it was made with a lot of love. ❤️
