ChIJY9fLj0UpdTERQVDi6vq8a0g.author: Leonard Lim
ChIJY9fLj0UpdTERQVDi6vq8a0g.text: Cuu Van Long at Landmark 81 presents an excellent-value seafood buffet with an extensive selection that includes seafood, dim sum, sushi, meats, local specialties, and desserts. The standout feature is the wide range of fresh seafood, replenished daily and prepared through various methods such as steaming, grilling, and stir-frying. The dessert offerings are abundant and well-executed, complementing the overall dining experience. In summary, Cuu Van Long provides impressive variety and quality at a commendable price point, making it a strong choice for buffet dining in Ho Chi Minh City.

In this buffet nothing to complain…. Large assortment of sea products and very well cooked.
Western is a bit limited but we are in Vietnam. Congratulations for this Brunch!! I will come back

ChIJY9fLj0UpdTERQVDi6vq8a0g.text:
We swore we’d never eat at a buffet again; we’re too old to be stuffing ourselves with subpar food. And we kept that promise for over ten years, ever since I turned 50. Yet here we are, on our third buffet in a month.

My husband and I agree: Cửu Vân Long has truly earned its five stars from these old folks. The seafood is fresh, and although the selection stays the same each day, it gives the comforting impression that they’re consistent, not just cooking with whatever’s cheapest ingredients on sale at the market.

What impressed me most was the extremely enthusiastic and attentive staff. From the time of ordering to serving, they were always smiling, friendly, asking about customers and ready to support when needed. It was this friendliness that made me feel comfortable and want to come back many times. 
In short, this is a dining place worth experiencing, both delicious and with dedicated service. I will definitely recommend it to friends and come back in the near future!

ChIJ9eAtbSwrdTERyTJu6D2N-BM.text:
I have eaten Teo a lot since 2024 and just came back in November 2025 and noticed that the quality of the restaurant's food has gotten a lot WORSE
First: when you catch live shrimp in the pond and bring it to the processing counter, the staff will tell you to release it back into the pond, there are already pre-processed shrimp -> the shrimp when brought out are extremely soft and have died for a long time, not live shrimp, you can tell right away when you eat it, I don't understand why they are doing this trick now??
Second, the drinking glasses are extremely dirty and feel cold, scratched, dirty ....
Third, the chef has also been changed, no longer making delicious food like before.
Fourth, the amount of frozen food that has not yet thawed is much larger
As for the service attitude of the staff, it does not affect me at all. The quantity of dishes is still guaranteed, but as said, the freshness is really no longer.
For a customer who lives far away like me, but believes in Teo, I came and received a not so happy experience.

Wish the shop success and improvement.

If the shop rep curses me, you will understand how the quality has changed.

ChIJi5KSBjQvdTERGv8CCcXN6mE.name: places/ChIJi5KSBjQvdTERGv8CCcXN6mE/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURQNjREeWxBRRAB
ChIJi5KSBjQvdTERGv8CCcXN6mE.author: M
ChIJi5KSBjQvdTERGv8CCcXN6mE.text:
As a non-vegetarian that just eats it occasionally (now weekly), I basically just require good tofu at a vegetarian buffet. They didn't have any. Maybe the deep-fried stuff was it(?), but it didn't look great.

I came for a late lunch, close to 2 pm, but I expected a few more options. I would recommend looking at the food first, then paying - I paid first. The selection is pretty small, but they do have 3 big vats of soup/curry - those are their main items. Unless I missed the other items, because of time, or perhaps they rotate items daily...

I will say, of what I had, everything tasted good. The curry was standard V-style coconut curry. It was good, but I just didn't feel like having a lot of it. The vegetable soup was also good, but I was already checked out in my mind.

You're supposed to take your shoes off before you enter. There's a few small floor seating tables and a few tables with chairs.

50K/$1.95 is too much for what I had and compared to other vegetarian buffets; however, most of the tables were full, and people seemed to like it. I had to go to a cơm tấm place right after because I needed more food - although that was not a great experience either (nothing to do with this place, though).

With 10K/$0.40 for parking, 60K to eat here minimum if you come by motorbike.

ChIJi5KSBjQvdTERGv8CCcXN6mE.text: Peaceful and relaxed vibe, this little hidden nook is unassuming from the outside, not even a sign so you could almost say its a speak easy for vegans. You cant miss it though with the shaded entry and many shoes out front - dont forget to take yours off before you enter. Delicious healthy food, buffet style and you take your own dishes to the wash bucket when you're done (don't worry, you don't need to wash them). Great value and a kind and warm English speaking owner named Suong.

ChIJi5KSBjQvdTERGv8CCcXN6mE.name: places/ChIJi5KSBjQvdTERGv8CCcXN6mE/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURuZ3NlTkZ3EAE
ChIJi5KSBjQvdTERGv8CCcXN6mE.author: Thanh Hảo Lê
ChIJi5KSBjQvdTERGv8CCcXN6mE.text:
Quán Chay Nhà, tucked away in a quiet corner of Ho Chi Minh City, offers a unique and flavorful vegetarian dining experience. The restaurant boasts a charming, rustic ambiance with its simple wooden decor and warm lighting. The menu is extensive, featuring a diverse range of dishes from familiar Vietnamese classics like pho and spring rolls to more creative options like lemongrass tofu and coconut curry.

While the food is undoubtedly the star of the show, I found the service to be a bit inconsistent. Sometimes, the staff were incredibly attentive and friendly, eager to assist with menu recommendations and ensuring a pleasant dining experience. Other times, the service felt a bit slow and inattentive.

The quality of the food, however, largely made up for any service shortcomings. The dishes I tried were all beautifully presented and bursting with flavor. The vegetable pho was particularly memorable, with a rich and flavorful broth and a generous portion of fresh vegetables. The spring rolls were crispy and light, and the dipping sauce was a perfect accompaniment.

Overall, Quán Chay Nhà is a worthwhile dining experience for vegetarians and non-vegetarians alike. The delicious food and charming atmosphere make it a standout option in the city's vibrant culinary scene. While the service can be inconsistent, the overall experience is still highly enjoyable. I would definitely recommend making a reservation, especially during peak hours, as the restaurant can get quite busy.

Disclaimer: This review reflects my personal experience and opinions. Your experience may differ.

ChIJYYSPjP8vdTERMv9Ug1QLIn4.text: This is the best vegetarian restaurant in Ho Chi Minh, where you can escape the hustle and bustle of the city and enjoy amazing, delicious food. Chay Garden is a peaceful respite from busy Saigon streets. The atmosphere is soothing (think spa like environment), the staff are welcoming yet  respectful and non invasive.

Your Michelin star is well deserved and should be sustained.
Thank you for this memorable experience.

Find your inner Zen while sitting back, relaxing, and eating healthy vegetarian food. While the outer patio is decorated with pleasant foliage and a flowing lake, you'd find the most comfort in their air conditioned interior. After careful deliberation on what to eat to save room for my second lunch after this, the Fried Tofu made its impression, delicately battered and fried to a golden crisp, while maintaining a silky smooth bite that practically melts on your tongue. Each bite is packed with flavour, as it's tossed together with a Hong Kong-style salt, combining aromatics like garlic, onion and pepper into a salivating bite. Their in-house mixed salad was also a textural marvel of colourful julienned vegetables, bulked with fried oyster mushrooms and fried taro for a satisfying crunch. Dressed table-side by yours truly, the sweet and tangy sesame dressing had a pleasant nuttiness. Presented as a generous platter of Vietnamese herbs, including some rarer varieties - like tangy mango leaves - alongside unripe banana slices, starfruit, rice paper, and vermicelli. The extra-firm tofu, wrapped in toasted nori brought a gentle umami, reinforced by a tangy sriracha and fermented beancurd dip.

ChIJaXN_88YvdTERZBy-6Yk79PM.author: Bredgy L.
ChIJaXN_88YvdTERZBy-6Yk79PM.text:
Food @bredgyeats for more follow posts!

Eating a vegetarian diet is healthy. Disagree, at least when you eat 4000 calories animal-free every day, a trivial feat when you’re travelling in Vietnam. The crispy abalone mushrooms, perfumed with a fruity plum drizzle, bring contrasting textures with its bouncy stem and shatteringly crisp cap with fried garlic and cilantro on top. Following closely out of the fryer, the egg tofu is encased in a fine breadcrumb coating that's crisp yet delicate, begging you to bite through it. Lightly dusted with aromatic spices and salt, and topped with seaweed shrimps that add a gentle umami accent. Smashing through the equatorial rain, reveals the rainbow salad, offering a mix of textures, dressed in a mild but balanced fish sauce. Crisp cucumber, carrots, and fried shallots mingle with thai basil, sesame seeds, and crunchy coconut core. A boost of elegance and crisp is created through the crispy rice puffs - the most delicious utensil ever. The pot of gold at the end of the rainbow, was deep-fried mushroom stems that bring a unique, firm, chewy texture that's distinct from any meat. The doughy batter eagerly absorbs the sweet and sour sauce, which brings excitement that can only be expressed in capital letters. Finally, this dish weaves complexity with uniqueness, a savory sauce with a mild fermented fish (vegetarian, somehow?) aroma coats a filling of bouncy seitan. The gluten is wrapped in an umami-rich sheet of nori and fried tofu skin, creating another contrast of textures that keep each bite interesting.

ChIJaXN_88YvdTERZBy-6Yk79PM.name: places/ChIJaXN_88YvdTERZBy-6Yk79PM/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNyX0plazFnRRAB

ChIJaXN_88YvdTERZBy-6Yk79PM.text: This vegetarian restaurant offers an innovative and delightful dining experience. Each plate is thoughtfully crafted, balancing nutrition with taste in an impressive display of culinary artistry. The ambiance is warm and inviting, with modern decor and a relaxed atmosphere. ChIJu_LpjhUvdTER-6zPXn7ldPs.name: places/ChIJu_LpjhUvdTER-6zPXn7ldPs/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURub3EzbmNREAE
ChIJu_LpjhUvdTER-6zPXn7ldPs.author: Thanh Hảo Lê
ChIJu_LpjhUvdTER-6zPXn7ldPs.text:
Nhà hàng buffet chay Mãn Tự was a unique and memorable dining experience. The concept of "pay what you feel" was incredibly refreshing and truly aligned with the restaurant's Buddhist philosophy. It encourages diners to contribute based on their own means and appreciation for the meal.

The food itself was surprisingly diverse and flavorful. While vegetarian, the dishes were far from bland. There were a variety of options, from familiar Vietnamese staples like spring rolls and pho to more creative dishes like mock meats and colorful stir-fries. Everything was fresh and well-prepared.

The ambiance was peaceful and serene, reflecting the restaurant's spiritual focus. The decor was simple yet elegant, and the soft music created a calming atmosphere. The service was attentive and friendly, with the staff always ready to assist with any questions or requests.

However, there were a few minor drawbacks. The selection, while diverse, could sometimes feel a bit repetitive. Also, the restaurant can get quite busy, especially during peak hours, which may result in longer wait times for food replenishment.

Overall, I highly recommend Nhà hàng buffet chay Mãn Tự to anyone seeking a unique and meaningful dining experience in Ho Chi Minh City. It's a place where you can enjoy delicious vegetarian food while supporting a worthy cause.

ChIJu_LpjhUvdTER-6zPXn7ldPs.name: places/ChIJu_LpjhUvdTER-6zPXn7ldPs/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNacG9yWFVBEAE

The best part is you can pay any price at your disposal. When I ate today, I saw this place served good meals for the seniors, children shop sellers, deliveryman, workers to the unemployed. It is so great that despite financial hardship, this place still exists to serve people.

ChIJt4Yu77ondTERsbqNbqk7TQc.text:
Coming to Chay Garden Thảo Điền, I felt a warm welcome right from the gate. Though a bit hidden — sharing the entrance with a Thai restaurant from the same group — once inside, the calm and cozy space with a hint of Thai vibe feels relaxing and pleasant. The friendly staff make the place even more inviting.

The food is truly impressive — every small dish is full of balanced flavors, well-portioned, and beautifully presented. You should definitely try the hot pot — hearty, flavorful, and perfect for sharing. And don’t miss the banana cake for dessert — it’s really good!

A lovely spot for a casual meal, a small family gathering, or for anyone exploring vegan food. For long-time vegans, it’s also a refreshing place to discover something new and inspiring.

ChIJMbrGDR8ndTERC-7faCPDLQQ.name: places/ChIJMbrGDR8ndTERC-7faCPDLQQ/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xvM2FuRkhSVXN4UW5KRU1GWmFaVUZ4VTB4clRrRRAB
ChIJMbrGDR8ndTERC-7faCPDLQQ.author: Young Mi
ChIJMbrGDR8ndTERC-7faCPDLQQ.text:
From the moment I walked into this vegetarian haven, I was enveloped in a calm, Zen-like atmosphere that immediately set the tone for a truly memorable dining experience. The minimalist decor, soft lighting, and soothing music created a peaceful escape from the outside world.
The service was absolutely impeccable—attentive, warm, and genuinely welcoming without being intrusive. Every staff member seemed deeply connected to the philosophy of the place, and it showed in how thoughtfully they approached everything from the menu explanation to the timing of each course.
Now, let’s talk about the food—wow. Each dish was a work of art, showcasing the natural beauty and flavor of fruits and vegetables in creative, inspired ways. From the vibrant starters to the hearty mains and delicate desserts, every bite was bursting with freshness and intention. The flavors were clean yet complex, proving that you don’t need meat to create deeply satisfying, nourishing meals.
I left feeling full, balanced, and grateful for such a mindful and delicious experience. Whether you're a dedicated vegetarian or simply someone who appreciates quality, soul-nourishing food, this restaurant is an absolute must-visit.

ChIJMbrGDR8ndTERC-7faCPDLQQ.name: places/ChIJMbrGDR8ndTERC-7faCPDLQQ/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTUNBNE9QdkJnEAE
ChIJMbrGDR8ndTERC-7faCPDLQQ.author: clink k
ChIJMbrGDR8ndTERC-7faCPDLQQ.text:
I visited Bongensai, a Japanese vegetarian restaurant,in late December 2024 and had a pleasant experience. The menu is extensive, offering a wide variety of delicious vegetarian dishes that are both palatable and presentable. The zen setting of the restaurant is peaceful and beautifully designed, with several Buddha statues adding to the serene atmosphere.

The prices are very reasonable, which makes it even more enjoyable. There's also a charming little shop on-site that sells traditional clothing, which is a nice touch if you're interested in souvenirs or something unique.

The food was good, though I do feel that the dessert could use a little improvement. Still, overall, I left quite happy with my visit and will be returning if i am in HCM. If you are looking for a zen and flavorful dining experience Bongensai is worth a try.

ChIJMbrGDR8ndTERC-7faCPDLQQ.name: places/ChIJMbrGDR8ndTERC-7faCPDLQQ/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VPdndsT3VGMU16M2hBRRAB

ChIJMbrGDR8ndTERC-7faCPDLQQ.text: wonderful vegetarian. ambience, convivial company,and great food. We were served by Loi - such a lovely person.... her quiet and graceful presence was perfect for the setting

ChIJMbrGDR8ndTERC-7faCPDLQQ.text: A zen place follows Japan style and foods. First entry is impressed by peace and warm atmosphere. We choose buffet cost 350k vnd instead of a-la-carte orders. ChIJMbrGDR8ndTERC-7faCPDLQQ.text:
Food was excellent. Atmosphere was excellent.

Service was quite poor. The servers seem overly focused in conversations with one another. When I tried to get their attention, one of the waiters noticed but completely turned his back to me and continued to talk with the others.

Only one of the waiters was friendly, the others seem annoyed. I asked for water, they said to order from the drink menu. They charged me 3,000 for the wet wipe on the table (which I don't know if they do for everyone, but after the poor service, felt like a "don't come back" kind of message)

ChIJdbx2tt4udTERHrtnMCKRqK8.name: places/ChIJdbx2tt4udTERHrtnMCKRqK8/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xVd1RXRjJaMjQxYmt4M2QxTkhOV1ZPYWkxeE0yYxAB
ChIJdbx2tt4udTERHrtnMCKRqK8.author: Bredgy L.
ChIJdbx2tt4udTERHrtnMCKRqK8.text:
Food @bredgyeats for more follow posts!

Five Color Salad – An addicting and refreshing fish sauce dressing that leans on the sweeter side, with a great contrast of textures of the salad that are served with the still warm, freshly fried crawn cracker puffs. Included inside are carrots, thai basil, beech mushrooms, cucumbers, cabbage, mango, fried beech mushrooms, fried tofu skin.

Stir Fried Mixed Mushrooms – Stir fried with a slightly piquant and aromatic satay sauce, the mushrooms are crisp and bouncy and fully coated with flavour. It’s served on top of raw shredded cabbage, adding a crunchy contrast in textures. I found each bite to be quite greasy though.

Viet Chay Salted Tofu in Clay Pot – Soft tofu is cooked with a salty and savory slurry with tiny bits of gluten and fermented soybeans, that also add some contrast in texture. It can get quite salty when eaten with the sauce, goes well with rice.

ChIJdbx2tt4udTERHrtnMCKRqK8.name: places/ChIJdbx2tt4udTERHrtnMCKRqK8/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNQa2ZHRnN3RRAB
ChIJdbx2tt4udTERHrtnMCKRqK8.author: Anh Ngô
ChIJdbx2tt4udTERHrtnMCKRqK8.text:
Had a warmy dinner at a hidden vegan restaurant located inside a souvenir shop.

My friend told me about this place as this is her favorite spot for vegetarian options, otherwise I wouldn't recognize this gem when crossing it on the street because it is hidden inside.

We ordered quite a lot to try different options, and all of them were so good. I think the salad and the steamed (purple) rice were the spotlight because I was impressed. They also gave us a free hot milk tea before meal and I love it.

Staff was very attentive and fast, so we had a satisfying experience with their service. However, what I don't like is that the space is a bit cramped, and it gets quite hot at peak hour when there are lots of people.

Overall, this place is a must-try for vegetarian/ vegan meals. They have parking lots for motorbikes but not sure about car parking. You should call them to ask in advance and maybe book a table as well because I heard that this place is usually packed.

ChIJdbx2tt4udTERHrtnMCKRqK8.name: places/ChIJdbx2tt4udTERHrtnMCKRqK8/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURpc2JTVEZREAE

ChIJdbx2tt4udTERHrtnMCKRqK8.text:

The portion for noodles is quite big, it took me half an hour to finish. The taste was complex, mild and feel like they use a lot instant spices for the broth, couldn’t feel the naturally clear and sweet taste of veggies broth, many “fake meats” in the bowl with some mushrooms, broccoli.
Dessert was okay.
The reviews on Google mention that they offer free milk tea that’s good but I didn’t see any. Serving time is slow. Some staffs are really nice and busy, the others are too lazy, inattentive and having such inappropriate manners for a vegan restaurant.

Cozy ambience along with polite staff made this place more amazing.
Mango sticky rice and tofu dishes is a must try here.

ChIJ4XRHgM0odTERr703Zn4VVWU.text:
The food is phenomenal. I ordered a soup and the curry - both incredibly tasty, rich and arriving in big portions, as well as reasonably priced.

I was skeptical when walking in as I arrived near closing time. A few members of the staff almost rushed me in, which got me a bit annoyed. They didn’t allow me to sit upstairs and started cleaning around me while I was sitting down, even though the restaurant was still open.The staff was nice, but doesn’t speak a word of English, which isn’t a problem, but makes communication a bit tricky. I ordered the rice, but got served with noodles.

The ambiance is a bit strange with constant music and weird videos of a lady in a buddhist temple playing on the TV in front of you. The food makes up for all these little things and I definitely recommend this place and intend to come back.

ChIJLQO1TLAvdTERLFXRWilNCXI.text: A bit crowded but the place was clean and tidy. The food was delicious, staffs were friendly. A good place to consider if you are craving vegetarian food.

ChIJf3tI1-kodTERhDKXKiBzev4.text: Ok vegan /vegetarian Vietnamese food. It’s looks like just a takeaway shop in front but there’s actually a huge number of tables and restaurant space in the back. I got the mixed random rice and it was just ok - I didn’t like the tofu seasonings and there weren’t many veggies added. Service was super pleasant and the price was very cheap.

ChIJf3tI1-kodTERhDKXKiBzev4.text:
Amazing place with cheap vegan food! You can check the size of banh xeo 🤣🤣😍 and menu, they don't have English menu, but you can scan the photo of menu through google translate

They also have wi-fi, service is quick. But nobody there speak English.

ChIJf3tI1-kodTERhDKXKiBzev4.text: Definitely my favorite Vegan place in HCM! Food  is flavorful...Too bad, due to cỏvid, thí place is now, carry out only! So, take home ...it is

ChIJf3tI1-kodTERhDKXKiBzev4.text: So even though they don't really speak much English here, this is a well established vegan eatery. With an amazing selection of foods freshly prepared. With good service and very affordable prices. You can also buy some tasty vegan treats at the mini shop inside the eatery for take away. Highly recommended! Love this place.

ChIJf3tI1-kodTERhDKXKiBzev4.name: places/ChIJf3tI1-kodTERhDKXKiBzev4/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURjelAtTktnEAE
ChIJf3tI1-kodTERhDKXKiBzev4.author: Saigon Go
ChIJf3tI1-kodTERhDKXKiBzev4.text: The best one for vegetarian, service is ok

ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.author: Filthy Vegan
ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.text: Love the food from Ba Xa. Been coming to their vegan restaurants scattered all over Saigon. Great food at affordable prices. Clean and quiet inside with air conditioning.

ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.name: places/ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT21STlJXcHJVVGg2UVc4NFRURktkR1EzVVZoTmJVRRAB
ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.author: Johnny Nguyen
ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.text:
Came here based on the review. In conclusion, nothing that great. We have been eating at many vegetarian places around Saigon and this was not it.

Price was on the higher end. Portion size was decent. Tea on the other hand is 6.5k! I’m not saying we can’t afford it but for tea, it should be at least 2k same as all the other restaurants.

Would I come back? Probably not. It was worth a try.

ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.name: places/ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURQMHRXYzFRRRAB
ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.author: Sofia Sebastian
ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.text: We ordered the braised dishes. Unfortunately, they seemed to be the wrong choices as they weren't palatable at all. They were filled with seasonings so we couldn't savor the natural taste of the mushrooms. The service was rather slow despite friendly and accommodating staff. But I was impressed by how they made that dish we ordered to look like real pork although it was weird to be in a vegan restaurant with food designed and made to appear as the ones you actually try to avoid.

ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.name: places/ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUQ3MUpfMjdBRRAB
ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.author: Barbara Bt
ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.text: The meal was quite enjoyable, but the fried tofu didn't quite live up to my expectations. The staff member who spoke English was still learning, but he put in a lot of effort, and he even promptly corrected a mistake with my order. The takeout fish was exceptional, and I'm definitely looking forward to going back for more delicious Vietnamese vegan food. The restaurant was conveniently located and easy to find with the help of Google Maps, and the prices were very reasonable.

ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.name: places/ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUQzamRPVmJnEAE
ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.author: Eric Nguyen
ChIJXSxfUXspdTER1T8xvDsqGVE.text: I'm so stuffed right now, but in the best way possible 😋. Everything was seriously next-level delicious! 💯  I could eat that meal again and again.  No regrets, just pure foodie happiness 😄. Anyone else have a dish they could eat on repeat forever?  Tell me in the comments! 👇  #foodie  #foodcoma #worthit  #sodelicious

ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.name: places/ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2poc1VXUTJabGg0VUZOelowSkhlRnBoY1dKTWNtYxAB
ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.author: Introverted traveller
ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.text:
Happened across this place while exploring on google maps.
Greeted by staff, enjoyed mi Quang and gọi cuốn appetizer. Food is good.
Visited ahead of the lunch crowd, so my experience of this space was calm and quiet.

Very positive experience and will return soon

ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.name: places/ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUREX052MHhRRRAB
ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.author: Sofia Sebastian
ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.text: The food was okay. Not outstanding, but they are neat in their service. The waitress was commendable as she was friendly and smily. The drinks were nice cos they were not so sweet. It was just a pity that they didn't have the brown rice tea when we were there. The fruit spring roll reminded us of home. It was with banana and jackfruit inside. The stir fried noodle with turmeric was delicious but the serving was rather small.

ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.name: places/ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VKYk5yYTd1ck1LZC1RRRAB
ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.author: Becci Lisa
ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.text:
All perfect. We loved the food so we ordered take away food too - to eat at the next day.
Try the sweet and sour soup 🍜

ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.name: places/ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTUNnbW9TcmhRRRAB
ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.author: Tatjana Mijailovic
ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.text: Best vegetarian hủ tiếu i’ve had so far! Also tried their vegan mi quang and gio cuon and they were both so good! The staff doesn’t speak any english but they have english menu so ordering was easy. Highly recommend!

ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.name: places/ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNZdVp2cVFBEAE
ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.author: Steven Huynh
ChIJjzD0B1kpdTERAvzErEYU_9s.text: Ordered Pho and brown rice juice, the vegies and tofu are very fresh. The broth is nice too.

ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.name: places/ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2tSUE5XVnlkVnB6YVdGdlUxTmZibGc0TlVkeFNtYxAB
ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.author: Bellie B
ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.text:
Lovely local restaurant. They only serve a few dishes in the morning (not the whole menu) but I came for pho so I didn't mind! Super friendly staff who spoke English.

Not just a restaurant problem but a Vietnam problem - there were loads of old Vietnamese men smoking in the outdoor area, so you're kinda forced indoors if you care about health which I'd say a fair few vege folk are 🥦

ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.name: places/ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xWUU1VbFpTbXd4Tm5OUVdsRk5UbGRTUW10M1JYYxAB
ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.author: Federico Ruzich
ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.text: The food was surprisingly good, tasty, flavourful. Staff is friendly and service quick. Huge vegetarian menu to choose with different options. Very deceiving pictures on Google Maps, the place looks different. 2 items on the menu were not available so we had to please ourselves with something else but the food was tasty and portions were ok

ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.name: places/ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNIbk1pcWx3RRAB
ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.author: Filthy Vegan
ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.text: Huge interior. Huge menu. Quick service. Most importantly though is the food. Absolutely delicious vegan food. I first came to this restaurant about 20 years ago backpacking. I forgot all about it. Came today and the food is just as brilliant as it was all those years ago

ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.name: places/ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xwUFZHWXlZM2g0YUZwcGEwMVdhVzlTYzNCdlNFRRAB
ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.author: Erin Biskup
ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.text:
Huge bowl of Thai Style Vermicelli for breakfast! It was delicious but on the verge of being too spicy for me…my husband loved it!
Menu is very limited for breakfast. We will probably return for lunch or dinner to try other things.

ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.name: places/ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNYbDltTmNBEAE
ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.author: thtn78
ChIJw-UnRRcvdTERhlf0LoYfyeU.text: Breakfast options for that day was Banh Canh (round thick rice noodles) and Hu Tieu (flat thin rice noodles). Service was fast and soups were delicious.

ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.name: places/ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25kYWFtWkRYelZ6VG1kaFJVWlZka1JHTUdoSVFuYxAB
ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.author: Naomi Aust
ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.text: I really appreciate that this place is entirely plant-based, but the flavours didn’t quite hit the mark for us. We went twice and both times felt a bit underwhelmed. The pad Thai was decent and the stir-fried garlic chives were actually very nice, but the other dishes we tried were fairly average. It might be worth a try, but I don’t think we’ll be returning.

ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.name: places/ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT21OMVdUZFdWV1U1ZEZwR1prcHdjamxaVW5BNGFYYxAB
ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.author: Guy Braverman
ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.text: Pretty little restaurant run by a group of young women. It was very nice sitting in a quiet air conditioned restaurant and enjoying delicious Vietnamese lunch. I loved everything about it, the decor, the ambiance the soft music playing in the background and most of all the tasty food. I had a spicy noodle soup and garlic fried breaded tofu, both were wonderful. Portion sizes are very generous and prices are reasonable. Highly recommend.

ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.name: places/ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xaSVVrcG5ia1ZWYjBwNFJGUm9WRTUzYm1WMWRtYxAB
ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.author: Emma Prüßner
ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.text: Amazing vegan Vietnamese cuisine! 💚 Very fresh and tasty. The vegan fish and beef were incredible too.

ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.name: places/ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VNajdqSzJjX05hU3ZBRRAB
ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.author: Phú Ngô
ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.text: The restaurant has the variety to choose from. The food are delicious, huge and reasonally priced. And the space is cozy, the tables are evenly spaced and give us privacy. Definitely one of the best vegan restaurant in town.

ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.name: places/ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUMzNzU2UVRBEAE
ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.author: Tee Wang
ChIJHyAHTiQvdTERWXoOWvE7VlM.text: Tiny little place that could sit roughly about 30 people. Food is delicious if you’re tired of eating all the meats and wanted to have vegetarian food. Every single dish was delicious. Friendly staff. Fast service. Would definitely recommend this place to anyone who loves vegetarian food. Affordable prices. I’ve been to some vegetarian restaurants with prices that are a bit outrageous.

ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.name: places/ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT201MVpYQkJWSGxsYzBFNWRETTViVE5TZWw4M1YyYxAB
ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.author: Megha Nayar
ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.text:
Edit: The restaurant reached out to me and offered to re-send or refund my order. I chose to have the soup again, which they promptly sent across. Very responsive service, and the quality of the soup was good too.

They charge 105k VND for their Almond Pumpkin soup, but the quantity is shockingly little. The photo I’ve posted here was taken before I started eating - it was about 100 ml of soup. The container is the size of a small coffee cup. And it was half-empty. The average soup bowl in restaurants around Saigon is double this quantity.

I had to order another lunch from elsewhere after this joke of a meal.

I’ve noticed this trend - restaurants think it’s a good idea to cheat customers ordering online, because we’re not physically present to argue with them. Yes, you duped me once, but I will neither visit nor order again.

Order date: 14/11/25, around 12 pm via Grab.

ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.name: places/ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2paRVRIRjNPSE5aYjJKcWVESk1abGREZDJwU1dHYxAB
ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.author: Sean Dubra
ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.text:
The wife and I met a friend here for lunch and it did not disappoint.

We don’t typically eat lunch so we went a little light. I had soup along with edamame and she had a salad. The three of us shared fresh rolls. Everything was excellent and we both highly recommend this place.

Service was great and portions were adequate. Check it out if this is the type of food you eat. You will not regret it,

ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.name: places/ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VLaTRzOURVZ2FINGFREAE
ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.author: Amy Nguyen
ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.text: This place is a great spot to enjoy vegan food, even if you’re not a vegetarian. The menu is super diverse, so it’s hard to decide what to order. I recommend going with a group so you can try a variety of dishes. Each floor has a unique decoration theme, which is really cool. But I found it a bit strange when they placed a Buddha statue on the third floor then still have upper floors with people walking and seating above Buddha…well I just felt weird though. The food and drinks were enjoyable and worth trying. However, the service was quite expensive due to the added service tax and tax percentage. The staff was friendly and provided prompt service.

ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.name: places/ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTURBcG9hT193RRAB
ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.author: Hoàng Quỳnh
ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.text:
I stumbled upon this restaurant by chance while taking a walk near my place, looking for a quick dinner spot. At first, I didn’t realize it was a “chay Tuệ” (a type of vegetarian cuisine). Even after checking the menu, I still didn’t notice.

Since I was dining alone, I decided to try the Thai mixed rice. It was flavorful and well-prepared. I also ordered an iced tea. The food was good, but the pricing is more on the fine-dining side—quite expensive, especially with the added taxes and service fees. The most affordable dish was already over 100K, and that’s before tax.

If you come here with a group, expect to spend around 400K-500K per person to enjoy a variety of dishes. If dining alone, you’ll likely only be able to try one dish since the portions are quite generous.

The restaurant itself has a beautiful interior, the staff are professional, and service is quick.

Overall, I’d rate it around 8-9/10. I’d love to come back and try more dishes next time.

ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.name: places/ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2s4M2VWbHRNRFYyV1RCQmRsRldaM1ZsYlZWS1RsRRAB
ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.author: Chloe Nguyen
ChIJvbWW9GQpdTERGiJKRTbsJw4.text: The vegan dishes here are quite unique — I really love the presentation. The staff are welcoming and very helpful.

ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.name: places/ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VNbWkzSnpTN1pHRi13RRAB
ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.author: Ben Herman
ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.text: An absolute must-visit all-you-can-eat vegetarian buffet, although it can be very busy. The dishes are fantastic and it’s self serve. At 50k, it’s more than worth it. Theres just a ton of great food and I’ll certainly be back. Service was fine and Theres motorbike parking in the alley but it can be packed.

ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.name: places/ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURfajdtNEJ3EAE
ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.author: M
ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.text:
[Update Apr 9, 2025] Tried this for the second time. I tried to go a week prior, but it was full. The food was as good as the previous time. The selection was a little different. The beans and tofu were warm. Everything tasted fresh, and they replenished the items. The soups were hot. Both soups I had were good - one was a little sweeter than the other.

---

I was confused after seeing this on Maps because I knew I had tried a vegetarian buffet right here, but didn't see my review for it... This is a different vegetarian buffet almost next door (maybe it is?) to Như Y Veg Buffet.

Again, speaking as a non-vegetarian, this food was very good. I thought the other place was ok. This place is worth coming back to (for me).

The now defunct Nhien's Plant Base was the best Vegan/Vegetarian buffet I've been to in Vietnam (it was cheaper at 40K and had a larger selection with better tasting items than other buffets), I think the taste here is comparable. The price is still very good here (50K/$2). I will try the replacement of Nhien's at some point (I tried a couple days ago, but it was already closed for Tết).

I normally try veg buffets for lunch, not dinner, but I did try dinner here (if that makes a difference). Similar size seating to Như Y, but a lot different selection of food.

Everything was fresh. Less emphasis on making your own salad than some places. The tofu was really good. The (what looks like 잡채/stir-fried cellophane noodles) noodles were probably the weak point, but I still had a lot of it.

The deep-fried tofu (I think that's what it was) was really good. Of the 2 soups & curry, the one on the right tasted good. The one on the left was very good. The curry was good, too.

ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.name: places/ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURfLU1QdGZREAE
ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.author: Kaitlin Smith
ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.text:
loved it loved it loved it.
as veggie options go this is amazing. they have a good spread of food as a buffet which you can pick and choose from.
we came here two days in a row and some things slightly changed too so was exciting to try new things both times.

ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.name: places/ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VMM2s4YUtzcU1TWVl3EAE
ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.author: Robert Kurowski
ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.text: 50,000 for all you can eat vegetarian food everything was really delicious and fresh. It’s a small little alley but you must go here. We got here right when it opened and it already started getting crowded. Very very popular place and location.

ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.name: places/ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8/reviews/ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTUNJNnVyRVlBEAE
ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.author: A E
ChIJxfYHTU4vdTERxkjMoXWGSf8.text: AMAZING !! We discovered this place on a whim, and despite not everyone we went with being vegetarian, no one had a bad word to say. The value for money is insane - 50,000VND for unlimited food !! And the food itself is such high quality, authentic fresh and exciting. We had to come back again and it was just as good !! Come here if you’re vegetarian or not because it’s worth every penny (Dong 🤪🤪)

ChIJJ_nWVQQvdTERDONFCVvDsK0.name: places/ChIJJ_nWVQQvdTERDONFCVvDsK0/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25CbVZ5MTJiaTFhTm1GSGRHUkxaazFLUjBKb01rRRAB
ChIJJ_nWVQQvdTERDONFCVvDsK0.author: Frank Kays
ChIJJ_nWVQQvdTERDONFCVvDsK0.text:
Every visit to Shamballa has been excellent. The food is full of flavor, and it is worth trying whether you are vegetarian or not. I am not vegetarian, but I avoid meat during Lent. I first visited Shamballa during Lent in 2025 and have returned because the food is that good.

My favorite dishes so far are the Shamballa Crispy Mushrooms, Grilled Eggplant, Shamballa Rolls, and the Cassava Salad (not pictured). I have honestly enjoyed every dish I have tried.

The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, and the staff are friendly and attentive. They take the time to point out ingredients you might not expect in certain dishes. Today our server was Diep Diep, and she was excellent. She was cheerful, attentive, and very helpful. #EatLikeFrank

ChIJJ_nWVQQvdTERDONFCVvDsK0.name: places/ChIJJ_nWVQQvdTERDONFCVvDsK0/reviews/Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25NeGRWVnpMWGRIWTNST1ZrbFJMWGt5YVRscVNVRRAB

ChIJefooOfkudTER5LO21o7W4mg.text:
Food @bredgyeats for more follow posts!

Fried Egg Tofu (8.7/10)- No meat, no problems! This fried egg tofu stuffed is my new vegetarian addiction. The outer skin is delicately crisp and is contrasted with a jiggly and fragrant eggy inside, and rounded out with the slight sweetness of the pork floss, an unequivocally addicting bite.

Miso Glazed King Oyster (8.25/10) - How can king oyster mushrooms taste bad when coated with a sweet and umami miso glaze? They don't, and that sauce is so precious that the shredded cabbage is a blessing to soak it all up.

Banh Xeo (7/10) - The following banh xeo and braised mushrooms were both well made, sporting a crispy texture and a delicious amount of umami. The batter was rich from the coconut milk and doesn't feel overly thick, letting the finely chopped fillings to shine a bit more.

Braised Mushrooms (7.25/10) - Mushrooms were cooked nicely and nestled inside an aluminum bowl to trap the heat inside, containing the rich mushroom sauce that's piping hot and full of earthy umami notes. Additionally that are some veggies to provide a nice textural contrast.

Lotus Seed Rice (6.5/10) - Wrapped inside lotus leaves is a surprisingly light tasting rice that won't weight you down. The lotus seeds are the main star of the show, providing a subtle but pleasant sweet flavour with a creamy texture. The rice was soft and had carrots and mushrooms in it for a slight depth of flavour.

If I were living in Vietnam, I would absolutely have no problem eating salad every day, seeing the endless combinations these creative chefs come up with. The innovation doesn’t stop short of just salads, though, as this imitation of braised pork belly features mushroom patties with a meaty, wheat gluten-like texture, resting underneath a fatty layer of coconut milk and tapioca flour. The beautifully golden brown exterior is full of aromatic, nutty flavours, and when mixed with the sweet and sour sauce with lychees and longan, it’s hard to not acknowledge the skills of the chef. It’d be your lucky day if you order the Lucky Salad and were a fan of taro, which is occasionally interrupted with lotus root, sprouts, cucumber, carrot, fried onions, mushrooms, water chestnuts, and a yogurt tangerine dressing.

I keep my expectations low for buffet spot, and this place nicely delivered. Their salad seasonings and dressing are addicting, their soup is quite unique and customizable as they have a spice bar next to it. Their stews are questionable as the vegan beef stew is too sweet for my taste. Hotpot too is sweet and seems like the seasonings were la lazy at our table's hot pot. I would expect something lighter and less intense than ours. Love that they change dishes almost constantly, refill/replace dishes back and forth, with dedicated logistics. However some staffs were not too attentive to our table, as we are a corner table but overall this is a decent place deserves everyone's attention.

The place can get jam packed depending on when you arrive, make sure to go early or book a table in advance.

ChIJK9Fc8_8mdTER3Q9JYs7GGsg.name: places/ChIJK9Fc8_8mdTER3Q9JYs7GGsg/reviews/ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURuMElULXl3RRAB

ChIJK9Fc8_8mdTER3Q9JYs7GGsg.text:
It's a high-end vegetarian buffet, but you are going to pay for it; 220K/$8.90 for an adult.

Although the food is diverse, out of stuff I actually enjoyed, it's a lot less than the food at Buffet Chay Thong Dong in Vinhomes Grand Park, and this one is 100K more. I could have eaten 11 meals for the same price at the cheap local buffet I've been to a few times (Quán chay Hoàng Đạt) - quite frankly, I think I'd prefer the cheap one.

This has a fancy salad bar layout. There's a yogurt area, beverage area, desert (mostly flan and yogurt, some fruit - there is an ice cream machine, I think), soup area, and the main course area. The food is high quality, but I personally don't feel I will go back for 220K.

ChIJY7TTN_4vdTERQfjKEK6xuTE.author: Scott Nguyen
ChIJY7TTN_4vdTERQfjKEK6xuTE.text:
Nấm - Vegetarian Bistro is a delightful dining spot for those seeking a healthy, plant-based meal in Ho Chi Minh City. Known for its innovative take on vegetarian cuisine, the bistro combines fresh ingredients with a creative approach, offering a diverse menu that satisfies both vegetarians and non-vegetarians alike. The ambiance is relaxed and cozy, making it a great place for a casual meal with friends or family.

The menu features a variety of flavorful dishes, from Vietnamese-inspired vegetarian options to international fusion plates. Each dish is thoughtfully prepared, emphasizing fresh vegetables, herbs, and plant-based proteins. The presentation is visually appealing, and the portion sizes are generous, providing a wholesome and satisfying meal.

In addition to the food, Nấm also offers a selection of refreshing drinks, including fruit juices, smoothies, and herbal teas, complementing the light and healthy dining experience. The staff are friendly and attentive, contributing to the bistro’s welcoming atmosphere.

Whether you're a dedicated vegetarian or simply looking to try something new, Nấm - Vegetarian Bistro delivers a flavorful and nourishing experience in a charming setting.

ChIJNabgFi0sdTERteVpACwe41Y.text:
I was shown to a table and given a menu, which I began to study. As soon as I lowered my head and looked at the table, I saw a pile of lottery tickets between my head and the menu. Having looked up, I saw a woman trying to sell them. I immediately showed her the way to the exit, indicating that she had nothing to do here and must leave. She stood still and didn't obey. I then stood up and showed her the way to the exit more explictly. She still didn't obey. I then pushed her out of the restaurant, as the staff stood silent, watching. Me, I'm a customer, it is not my job to maintain discipline in your restaurant and escort troublemakers out. You should not have allowed this woman to enter. And, as soon as you notice a troublemaker, you should escort them out. You may not let them pester customers.

I then returned to my seat and waited for someone to come take my order. I waited, waited... but no-one came. I decided to leave and go eat somewhere else.

Food @bredgyeats for more follow posts!

Vegetarian meal #126420 in Vietnam, paired with a thorough shower on the wheel that I didn’t ask for. Reminds me how delightful it is to have four seasons in a year, and this colourful salad reinforces that thought. It brings a refreshing contrast of textures – think crunchy root vegetables, springy fried mushrooms, and peanuts, with a savory fish sauce to complete the flavour. On the other hand, the garlic salt coating the crispy discs of egg tofu is an easy crowd pleaser, echoing my thoughts of the vegetarian duck, plus a side of pineapple fried rice to stuff our palates.

They also have eco-friendly straws, pottery for bows, dishes, and spoons if I recall correctly.

The place's atmosphere is quite nice and peaceful, Buddha's tune is played gently in the background. Your inner voice settle down a bit just by sitting there ;)
You should see the toilet upstair, it has nice view indeed, nice decor and airflow.

Price is reasonable, your stomach will be satisfied :)

ChIJhb4SewApdTERHMzLvzmxats.text:
I have been to this restaurant quite a few times before and when I crave vegan food, the food/dishes here have been delicious. It’s been a bit of time since I’ve been here and decided to go back as I had that craving. I was extremely disappointed.  Apparently with a new chef comes a very very very limited menu. The sad part is that they removed all of the delicious dishes they used to have. The food looked great in presentation, but it really lacked in flavor. One of the dishes, while happy it wasn’t over seasoned, was completely under-seasoned and a bit bland. With this new chef and new menu, I will absolutely not be returning to this restaurant. If they bring back the quality and taste that came with the older menu, I would return but because they removed all the dishes that were great tasting and that I came for, it’s completely off my list and I wouldn’t recommend it, not even close to the standard it used to be.
The atmosphere is still nice…but the restaurant, on a Saturday night, had only one staff member.

ChIJhb4SewApdTERHMzLvzmxats.text:
This vegan restaurant is located in a charming and picturesque street in Ho Chi Minh. The service is impeccable, and the Japanese-style decor creates a comfortable and welcoming atmosphere. The ambiance is calm and relaxing, perfect for a quiet dinner.

The menu is rich and varied, with generous portions and delicious dishes. The presentation is meticulously curated, and the freshness of the ingredients is truly outstanding. The quality-price ratio is excellent.

We discovered this place by pure chance, as it was right below our hotel. Being vegetarians, it quickly became our go-to spot for many evenings. Highly recommended, especially for those looking for something unique and well-prepared!

ChIJfY-L5rUvdTERlJcJ8JQmZ-M.author: Rose Nguyen
ChIJfY-L5rUvdTERlJcJ8JQmZ-M.text:
Tue Marina truly surprised me — in the best way. It’s one of those vegetarian restaurants where you don’t feel like you’re “missing” anything at all. Every dish is crafted with so much care, balance, and creativity that even non-vegetarian diners would fall in love.

The atmosphere is calm and elegant, with a soothing, nature-inspired vibe that instantly makes you feel grounded. The staff are kind, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about the ingredients and the philosophy behind the food.

The dishes were the highlight: fresh, flavorful, beautifully plated, and thoughtfully seasoned. You can really taste the quality of the produce and the intention behind every combination. Nothing felt heavy — just clean, delicious, nourishing food.

If you’re looking for a vegetarian restaurant that goes beyond the basics and delivers a refined, mindful dining experience, Tue Marina is absolutely worth a visit. I would happily come back again.

ChIJd1eA-_0ldTERqt41YRbgK-U.author: James Quang Nguyen
ChIJd1eA-_0ldTERqt41YRbgK-U.text:
I’ve visited this restaurant three times. During my first two visits with friends, I noticed some unpolished details but overlooked them to avoid seeming upset in their company.

This review is based on my third visit, which I made alone, giving the restaurant another chance.

The food was neither as flavorful nor as valuable as the menu prices suggested, and the service was genuinely disappointing.

The waitress who greeted me was pleasant enough and recommended the restaurant’s bestsellers after placing the menu on the wrong side of the table.
Since I prefer spicy flavors, so I requested sliced chilies, but the ones served were dry and old, as shown in the attached photo.

After finishing my meal, I asked for the bill. The waitress called over a cashier, who approached me shuffling in slippers and handed me the bill without a word. I paid, and she returned with my change in the same manner—still silent, without a “thank you” or even basic courtesy.

She made no eye contact, offered no smile, and left an awkward silence accompanied only by the sound of her shuffling slippers.

Price is considered cheap for the area, between 60k to 70kg in average per meal, however the drinks are a bit expensive. Overall, i enjoyed it and wish have more drink options.

Ordered the fried rice and garlic tofu. Asked for a pure vegan version, the rice came without any sauce mixed in, did the chef run out of soy sauce? Very lacking of any flavour. The garlic tofu tasted buttery, although I specifically mentioned no dairy. For the price, the food was very underwhelming, I didn't even eat half of it. The entire menu seems to have relatively high prices, especially the drinks. Maybe this is why the restaurant is empty..
Nice cooled AC room, friendly and helpful waitresses, nice design, perhaps some of the other dishes are nicer but I'm not willing to come back again.

Edited 19/7
For giving a generic response to me and other reviews that have made comments of the same nature regarding the taste, quality of ingredients and the menu being overpriced..  if you want to answer the review questions, just do it genuinely. Obviously this place doesn't care about their customers or their reputation

ChIJ0Q0f-sQodTERQ7zWB5egHzs.text:
⭐ 5/5 – Outstanding Vegetarian Dining Experience!
I had an amazing experience at KIM SA Vegetarian Restaurant on Phan Đăng Lưu. From the moment I arrived, I was impressed by the warm and inviting atmosphere. The restaurant is beautifully decorated with soft lighting, plants, and a cozy, relaxing vibe that makes you feel welcomed right away.
The staff were extremely friendly, attentive, and always ready to help with recommendations. Even though the place was busy, service was quick and everything arrived fresh and beautifully presented.
The food itself was absolutely delicious. Every dish was full of flavor, well-seasoned, and thoughtfully prepared. I especially loved how they used a variety of mushrooms and vegetables to create rich, satisfying textures without relying on mock meats. The portions were generous, and the balance of flavors felt both comforting and exciting.
One thing I really appreciated is how clean and organized everything was, from the dining area to the overall service flow. The prices are also very reasonable for the quality you get.
Overall, KIM SA is definitely one of the best vegetarian restaurants in the area. I highly recommend it to anyone—vegetarian or not—looking for a tasty, fulfilling meal.

ChIJ0Q0f-sQodTERQ7zWB5egHzs.text:
We came here for lunch and was seated immediately, though our seat on the ground floor could have used a bit more space (not sure if they have an upstair seating area).

The highlights from what we ordered were the Rolls of the Middle, Mangolia salad, Veggie braised mushrooms with pepper, and the veggie roast pork with tamarind sauce (the later two go great with rice).

We also got a veggie Indian curry, but it was quite underwhelming. It tasted similar to those prepackaged curry powder at the supermarket (but more diluted), and there was no kick to it in terms of spiciness, which is what I usually look for when eating curries.

Nevertheless, the other dishes (which tasted great) and the affordable price made up for it (around 200k per person).

I recommend you come here if you're fancying for a quick, tasty, and reasonably-priced vegetarian meal.

ChIJbaeNZCspdTEREadFbltGF9s.text:
In the words of the famous Galileo Galilei, “one does not eat well in Italy, one eats well in Vietnam”

My visit to the Koi Café was nothing short of wonderful, and it truly felt like stepping into a magical little world tucked away from the busyness of everyday life. From the moment you arrive, the atmosphere captures your attention—the décor is beautifully thought out, blending natural elements with cozy, artistic touches that make the entire space feel warm, welcoming, and genuinely special. It’s the kind of place where you can immediately relax, take a deep breath, and just enjoy being present.

One of the most enchanting features of the café is the opportunity to feed the koi fish. Watching them swim gracefully and playfully as they gather around is both calming and surprisingly joyful. It adds an interactive element that makes the experience memorable and sets this café apart from others.

The menu is another highlight. The food offers a delightful mix of Vietnamese and Thai flavors, bringing together the best of both cuisines in dishes that are rich, fresh, and full of vibrant ingredients. Their selection of fresh juices and smoothies is impressive as well—refreshing, flavorful, and perfect for pairing with any meal or simply enjoying on their own.

Overall, the Koi Café is a place where great food, peaceful surroundings, and a touch of magic come together perfectly. I truly enjoyed every moment of my visit, and I’m already looking forward to coming back again.

Let me start off by saying this place is so unique and visually stunning. That being said, the food isn't great and the service was terrible. We arrived and chose to wait for a water table. We were escorted to a table to wait at. A server came up to take our order. I told him we were just waiting for a table. He left a pad at the table and told us to write down what we wanted on the pad. ??? Then another guy approached us. Again we stated we were waiting for a water table. He took the pad and asked us what we wanted. He said our food would be delivered to our table once we were actually seated. Then they started bringing us our food in the waiting area. I had to find the original guy who sat us in the waiting area and he apologized, then got us the worst water table in the place but...whatever, we were just happy to finally be seated.
Our food came with no utensils. We had to ask for napkins 3 times...which we never got. The crispy corn was completely flavorless and our fish and chips entree was so-so at best. Drinks were just so so too. The only reason I give them 3 stars was simply because the place is mind blowing.
It's an interesting place to experience and gets some great pics. But don't be expecting good food and service. This was just our experience.
But definitely worth a visit...Just to have a look and grab a drink if nothing else.

ChIJW8bVvUwvdTERMK3h6j6UBuk.text:
Beanthere Coffee on Hồ Hảo Hớn is one of those places that makes you slow down in the middle of Saigon’s restless rhythm. It’s not just about coffee—it’s about how space, light, and detail come together to create a gentle pause.

Highlights:
•	Calm yet central location
Tucked away in District 1, the café manages to feel both convenient and hidden. It’s close to the city buzz, yet inside, you find a surprising sense of quiet.
•	Minimalist, warm design
The interior is clean and modern with wood accents, plants, and natural light. Tables are arranged thoughtfully for both individuals looking to work and groups catching up.
•	Great coffee quality
True to its name, Beanthere takes beans seriously. From robust espresso to slow-drip brews, the flavors are balanced, rich, and well-prepared. Non-coffee options like matcha and fruit teas are also solid choices.
•	Work and study friendly
Strong Wi-Fi, plenty of charging spots, and a calm atmosphere make it a go-to for students, freelancers, or anyone needing focus time.
•	Staff and service
The baristas are attentive and approachable, happy to recommend beans or brews based on your taste.

Conclusion:
Beanthere Hồ Hảo Hớn is a refined spot for coffee lovers and remote workers alike—a little sanctuary in the heart of District 1.
